   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.util.ArrayList;
   4import java.util.List;
   5import java.util.Map;
   6import java.util.Set;
   7import java.util.TreeSet;
   8import java.util.regex.Pattern;
   9
  10import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
  11
  12/**
  13 * The conformance gate. Every rule has an identifier, every finding names one, and the build fails
  14 * on any {@link Finding.Severity#ERROR}.
  15 *
  16 * <p>The linter is the reason this book's catalog is worth copying. A specification that lives only
  17 * in prose decays into a style guide: the first ten tools follow it, the next forty follow whoever
  18 * reviewed them, and by the time anyone notices, the model is being shown four different ways to
  19 * name an account. What a reviewer should be arguing about is whether the description tells the
  20 * truth and whether the risk tier is honest. Everything mechanical belongs here.
  21 *
  22 * <p>Rules come in seven families. NAM and DSC govern the two fields the model's choice turns on.
  23 * INP and OUT govern the schemas. ANN governs the hints the runtime trusts. GOV governs the
  24 * metadata the firm needs. ONT checks the descriptor against the domain ontology, which is where
  25 * drift between a catalog and its own design shows up first.
  26 */
  27public final class ConformanceLinter {
  28
  29    private static final Pattern NAME = Pattern.compile("^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,63}$");
  30    private static final int DESCRIPTION_MIN = 120;
  31    private static final int DESCRIPTION_MAX = 2000;
  32    private static final int PARAMETER_LIMIT = 12;
  33
  34    /** Phrases a seven-part description is expected to contain, each with the rule that wants it. */
  35    private static final List<Expectation> DESCRIPTION_PARTS = List.of(
  36            new Expectation("TS-DSC-03", List.of("use when", "use this when", "call this when",
  37                    "use it when", "use whenever", "use before", "use only after", "use after"),
  38                    "when to use the tool"),
  39            new Expectation("TS-DSC-04", List.of("do not use", "does not ", "not for ", "never use"),
  40                    "when not to use the tool, and what to use instead"),
  41            new Expectation("TS-DSC-07", List.of("read ", "returns", "shows", "says"),
  42                    "how to read the result"));
  43
  44    private record Expectation(String rule, List<String> anyOf, String what) {
  45    }
  46
  47    private final Ontology ontology;
  48
  49    public ConformanceLinter(Ontology ontology) {
  50        this.ontology = ontology;
  51    }
  52
  53    /** Lint one catalog as a whole: per-descriptor rules, then the rules about the set. */
  54    public List<Finding> lint(List<ToolDescriptor> catalog) {
  55        List<Finding> findings = new ArrayList<>();
  56        Set<String> names = new TreeSet<>(catalog.stream().map(ToolDescriptor::name).toList());
  57        for (ToolDescriptor descriptor : catalog) {
  58            findings.addAll(lintOne(descriptor, names));
  59        }
  60        findings.addAll(lintSet(catalog));
  61        return findings;
  62    }
  63
  64    public List<Finding> lintOne(ToolDescriptor descriptor, Set<String> catalogNames) {
  65        List<Finding> findings = new ArrayList<>();
  66        naming(descriptor, findings);
  67        description(descriptor, catalogNames, findings);
  68        schema(descriptor, "inputSchema", descriptor.inputSchema(), findings);
  69        schema(descriptor, "outputSchema", descriptor.outputSchema(), findings);
  70        inputs(descriptor, findings);
  71        annotations(descriptor, findings);
  72        governance(descriptor, findings);
  73        if (ontology != null) {
  74            ontology(descriptor, findings);
  75        }
  76        return findings;
  77    }
  78
  79    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ NAM
  80
  81    private void naming(ToolDescriptor d, List<Finding> out) {
  82        if (d.name() == null || !NAME.matcher(d.name()).matches()) {
  83            out.add(Finding.error("TS-NAM-01", String.valueOf(d.name()),
  84                    "name must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,63}$ — the intersection of what every "
  85                            + "runtime accepts; camelCase, dots and hyphens are not portable"));
  86            return;
  87        }
  88        if (d.name().split("_").length < 3) {
  89            out.add(Finding.error("TS-NAM-02", d.name(),
  90                    "name must be <domain>_<entity>_<operation>; two segments leave the model "
  91                            + "guessing which catalog a tool belongs to"));
  92        }
  93        if (d.title() == null || d.title().length() < 3 || d.title().length() > 60) {
  94            out.add(Finding.error("TS-NAM-07", d.name(),
  95                    "title must be 3 to 60 characters: it is what a human sees in an approval "
  96                            + "dialog, not a second description"));
  97        }
  98        if (d.title() != null && d.title().endsWith(".")) {
  99            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-NAM-08", d.name(), "title should not end in a period"));
 100        }
 101    }
 102
 103    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ DSC
 104
 105    private void description(ToolDescriptor d, Set<String> catalogNames, List<Finding> out) {
 106        String text = d.description();
 107        if (text == null || text.length() < DESCRIPTION_MIN) {
 108            out.add(Finding.error("TS-DSC-01", d.name(),
 109                    "description must be at least %d characters; a one-line description is the "
 110                            + "single most common cause of the wrong tool being chosen"
 111                            .formatted(DESCRIPTION_MIN)));
 112            return;
 113        }
 114        if (text.length() > DESCRIPTION_MAX) {
 115            out.add(Finding.error("TS-DSC-02", d.name(),
 116                    "description must be at most %d characters; past that it crowds out the "
 117                            + "conversation and the model skims it".formatted(DESCRIPTION_MAX)));
 118        }
 119        String lower = text.toLowerCase();
 120        for (Expectation part : DESCRIPTION_PARTS) {
 121            if (part.anyOf().stream().noneMatch(lower::contains)) {
 122                out.add(Finding.warning(part.rule(), d.name(),
 123                        "description does not appear to say " + part.what()));
 124            }
 125        }
 126        if (text.contains("`") || text.contains("**") || text.contains("\n- ")) {
 127            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-DSC-08", d.name(),
 128                    "description should be plain prose; markdown is rendered inconsistently and "
 129                            + "costs tokens that buy nothing"));
 130        }
 131        if (lower.contains(" i ") || lower.startsWith("i ") || lower.contains("we ")) {
 132            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-DSC-09", d.name(),
 133                    "description should be written about the tool, not in the first person"));
 134        }
 135        for (String referenced : referencedTools(text)) {
 136            if (!referenced.equals(d.name()) && !catalogNames.contains(referenced)) {
 137                out.add(Finding.error("TS-DSC-10", d.name(),
 138                        "description points the model at " + referenced
 139                                + ", which is not in this catalog — a dangling redirection is "
 140                                + "worse than none, because the model will try it"));
 141            }
 142        }
 143        if (d.annotations() != null && !d.annotations().readOnlyHint()
 144                && !lower.contains("confirm") && !lower.contains("approve")
 145                && !lower.contains("nothing is") && !lower.contains("irreversible")
 146                && !lower.contains("cannot be undone")) {
 147            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-DSC-06", d.name(),
 148                    "a tool that changes state should say in its description what the change is "
 149                            + "and whether it can be undone"));
 150        }
 151    }
 152
 153    /** Tool names mentioned in prose, so that cross-references can be checked mechanically. */
 154    public static Set<String> referencedTools(String text) {
 155        Set<String> found = new TreeSet<>();
 156        var matcher = Pattern.compile("\\b([a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+){2,})\\b").matcher(text);
 157        while (matcher.find()) {
 158            found.add(matcher.group(1));
 159        }
 160        return found;
 161    }
 162
 163    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ INP / OUT
 164
 165    private void schema(ToolDescriptor d, String where, JsonNode root, List<Finding> out) {
 166        if (root == null || !root.isObject()) {
 167            out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-01", d.name(), where, "must be a JSON Schema object"));
 168            return;
 169        }
 170        if (!"object".equals(root.path("type").asString(""))) {
 171            out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-02", d.name(), where,
 172                    "top level must be type: object — a bare array or scalar leaves the model no "
 173                            + "field names to reason about"));
 174        }
 175        walk(d, where, root, out);
 176    }
 177
 178    private void walk(ToolDescriptor d, String at, JsonNode node, List<Finding> out) {
 179        if (node == null || !node.isObject()) {
 180            return;
 181        }
 182        node.propertyNames().forEach(key -> {
 183            SchemaProfile.Prohibition prohibited = SchemaProfile.prohibitionFor(key);
 184            if (prohibited != null) {
 185                out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-03", d.name(), at + "/" + key, prohibited.why()));
 186            } else if (!SchemaProfile.PERMITTED.contains(key)) {
 187                out.add(Finding.warning("TS-INP-04", d.name(), at + "/" + key,
 188                        "keyword is outside the profile; confirm every runtime forwards it before "
 189                                + "relying on it"));
 190            }
 191        });
 192        if ("object".equals(node.path("type").asString(""))
 193                && !node.path("additionalProperties").isBoolean()) {
 194            out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-05", d.name(), at,
 195                    "every object must set additionalProperties: false, or the model's invented "
 196                            + "extra field is silently accepted and silently ignored"));
 197        }
 198        if (node.path("additionalProperties").isBoolean()
 199                && node.path("additionalProperties").asBoolean()) {
 200            out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-06", d.name(), at, "additionalProperties must be false"));
 201        }
 202        JsonNode properties = node.path("properties");
 203        if (properties.isObject()) {
 204            properties.propertyNames().forEach(name -> {
 205                JsonNode child = properties.get(name);
 206                if (!child.has("description") && !child.has("$ref")) {
 207                    out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-07", d.name(), at + "/properties/" + name,
 208                            "every property needs a description; the field name is not the "
 209                                    + "contract and the model will infer the wrong units"));
 210                }
 211                if (child.has("type") && "number".equals(child.path("type").asString(""))
 212                        && at.startsWith("input")) {
 213                    out.add(Finding.warning("TS-INP-12", d.name(), at + "/properties/" + name,
 214                            "money and prices must be decimal strings, not JSON numbers; "
 215                                    + "0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3 and an order ticket cannot absorb that"));
 216                }
 217                walk(d, at + "/properties/" + name, child, out);
 218            });
 219        }
 220        JsonNode defs = node.path("$defs");
 221        if (defs.isObject()) {
 222            defs.propertyNames().forEach(name -> walk(d, at + "/$defs/" + name, defs.get(name), out));
 223        }
 224        if (node.has("items")) {
 225            walk(d, at + "/items", node.get("items"), out);
 226            if (!node.has("maxItems") && at.startsWith("output")) {
 227                out.add(Finding.warning("TS-OUT-05", d.name(), at,
 228                        "an unbounded array in a result is an unbounded token bill; set maxItems "
 229                                + "and page the rest"));
 230            }
 231        }
 232    }
 233
 234    private void inputs(ToolDescriptor d, List<Finding> out) {
 235        JsonNode properties = d.inputSchema() == null
 236                ? null : d.inputSchema().path("properties");
 237        if (properties == null || !properties.isObject()) {
 238            return;
 239        }
 240        int count = properties.size();
 241        if (count > PARAMETER_LIMIT) {
 242            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-INP-08", d.name(),
 243                    "%d parameters; past %d the model starts omitting the ones it is least sure "
 244                            + "about. Consider two tools".formatted(count, PARAMETER_LIMIT)));
 245        }
 246        properties.propertyNames().forEach(name -> {
 247            if (SchemaProfile.RESERVED_PARAMETERS.contains(name)) {
 248                out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-09", d.name(), "inputSchema/properties/" + name,
 249                        "reserved parameter name: identity, entitlement and override flags are "
 250                                + "established by the runtime and must never be arguments the "
 251                                + "model can set"));
 252            }
 253            JsonNode property = properties.get(name);
 254            if (property.path("description").asString("").isBlank()) {
 255                return;
 256            }
 257            if ("string".equals(property.path("type").asString(""))
 258                    && !property.has("enum") && !property.has("pattern")
 259                    && !property.has("format") && !property.has("maxLength")) {
 260                out.add(Finding.warning("TS-INP-10", d.name(), "inputSchema/properties/" + name,
 261                        "an unconstrained string accepts anything the model invents; add an enum, "
 262                                + "a pattern, a format or at least a maxLength"));
 263            }
 264        });
 265        JsonNode required = d.inputSchema().path("required");
 266        if (required.isArray()) {
 267            for (JsonNode name : required.values()) {
 268                if (!properties.has(name.asString(""))) {
 269                    out.add(Finding.error("TS-INP-11", d.name(),
 270                            "required names " + name.asString("") + ", which is not a property"));
 271                }
 272            }
 273        }
 274    }
 275
 276    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ ANN
 277
 278    private void annotations(ToolDescriptor d, List<Finding> out) {
 279        ToolDescriptor.Annotations a = d.annotations();
 280        if (a == null) {
 281            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ANN-01", d.name(),
 282                    "all four annotations must be stated explicitly, even at their defaults"));
 283            return;
 284        }
 285        if (a.readOnlyHint() && a.destructiveHint()) {
 286            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ANN-02", d.name(),
 287                    "readOnlyHint and destructiveHint cannot both be true"));
 288        }
 289        if (a.readOnlyHint() && !a.idempotentHint()) {
 290            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ANN-03", d.name(),
 291                    "a read-only tool is idempotent by construction; idempotentHint must be true"));
 292        }
 293        Governance g = d.governance();
 294        if (g == null) {
 295            return;
 296        }
 297        if (!a.readOnlyHint() && !g.requiresApproval() && g.riskTier() >= 2) {
 298            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ANN-04", d.name(),
 299                    "a tier " + g.riskTier() + " tool that changes state must require approval"));
 300        }
 301        if (g.requiresApproval() && (g.approval().confirmationTemplate() == null
 302                || g.approval().confirmationTemplate().isBlank())) {
 303            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ANN-05", d.name(),
 304                    "approval mode " + g.approval().mode() + " needs a confirmationTemplate; "
 305                            + "a dialog that says \"allow this tool?\" is not informed consent"));
 306        }
 307        if (g.requiresApproval() && g.approval().expiresInSeconds() == null) {
 308            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-ANN-06", d.name(),
 309                    "approval should expire; an approval with no window is a standing instruction"));
 310        }
 311        if (a.readOnlyHint() && g.riskTier() > 1) {
 312            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-ANN-07", d.name(),
 313                    "a read-only tool at tier " + g.riskTier() + " is unusual; if it is that "
 314                            + "sensitive, say why in the capability note"));
 315        }
 316    }
 317
 318    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ GOV
 319
 320    private void governance(ToolDescriptor d, List<Finding> out) {
 321        if (!d._meta().containsKey(ToolDescriptor.GOVERNANCE_KEY)) {
 322            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-01", d.name(),
 323                    "_meta must carry a governance block under " + ToolDescriptor.GOVERNANCE_KEY));
 324            return;
 325        }
 326        Governance g = d.governance();
 327        if (g.version() == null || !g.version().matches("^\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+$")) {
 328            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-02", d.name(), "version must be semantic (major.minor.patch)"));
 329        }
 330        if (g.owner() == null || g.owner().team() == null || g.owner().escalation() == null) {
 331            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-03", d.name(),
 332                    "owner must name a team, a contact and a paging escalation; an unowned tool "
 333                            + "in production is an incident waiting for a volunteer"));
 334        }
 335        if (g.entitlements() == null || g.entitlements().isEmpty()) {
 336            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-04", d.name(),
 337                    "at least one entitlement; a tool anyone may call is a tool nobody checked"));
 338        }
 339        if (g.recordKeeping() == null || g.recordKeeping().auditEvent() == null
 340                || g.recordKeeping().retention() == null) {
 341            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-05", d.name(),
 342                    "recordKeeping must name an audit event and a retention period"));
 343        } else if (!g.recordKeeping().retention().startsWith("P")) {
 344            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-06", d.name(),
 345                    "retention must be an ISO 8601 duration such as P6Y"));
 346        }
 347        if (g.containsPii() && (g.piiFields() == null || g.piiFields().isEmpty())) {
 348            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-07", d.name(),
 349                    "containsPii is true but piiFields is empty; masking and retention are "
 350                            + "mechanical and need the pointers"));
 351        }
 352        if (g.lifecycle() == Governance.Lifecycle.ACTIVE
 353                && g.conformanceLevel() == Governance.ConformanceLevel.L0) {
 354            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-08", d.name(),
 355                    "an active tool must be at least L1"));
 356        }
 357        if (g.rateLimit() == null || g.rateLimit().perPrincipalPerMinute() == null) {
 358            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-GOV-09", d.name(),
 359                    "no per-principal rate limit; an agent in a retry loop will find out why "
 360                            + "that matters"));
 361        }
 362        if (g.evaluation() == null && g.riskTier() >= 2) {
 363            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-10", d.name(),
 364                    "a tier " + g.riskTier() + " tool must cite the evaluation suite that "
 365                            + "measures whether the model picks it correctly"));
 366        }
 367        if (g.riskTier() >= 2 && (g.availability() == null || g.availability().killSwitch() == null)) {
 368            out.add(Finding.error("TS-GOV-11", d.name(),
 369                    "a tier " + g.riskTier() + " tool must name a kill switch; somebody will "
 370                            + "need to turn it off at two in the morning"));
 371        }
 372        if (g.lifecycle() == Governance.Lifecycle.DEPRECATED
 373                && !d.description().toLowerCase().contains("deprecat")) {
 374            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-GOV-12", d.name(),
 375                    "a deprecated tool should say so in its description and name its replacement"));
 376        }
 377    }
 378
 379    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ ONT
 380
 381    private void ontology(ToolDescriptor d, List<Finding> out) {
 382        Ontology.Capability capability = ontology.capabilityOf(d.name());
 383        if (capability == null) {
 384            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-01", d.name(),
 385                    "no capability in the ontology; either the ontology is missing a row or the "
 386                            + "tool is doing something the domain was never designed to do"));
 387            return;
 388        }
 389        String expected = ontology.nameFor(capability);
 390        if (!expected.equals(d.name())) {
 391            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-02", d.name(),
 392                    "the ontology derives the name " + expected + " for this capability"));
 393        }
 394        Ontology.Entity entity = ontology.entities().get(capability.entity());
 395        Ontology.Operation operation = ontology.operations().get(capability.operation());
 396        if (entity == null || operation == null) {
 397            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-03", d.name(),
 398                    "capability names an entity or operation the ontology does not declare"));
 399            return;
 400        }
 401        if (d.annotations() != null && d.annotations().readOnlyHint() != operation.readOnly()) {
 402            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-04", d.name(),
 403                    "operation " + capability.operation() + " is "
 404                            + (operation.readOnly() ? "read-only" : "state-changing")
 405                            + " in the ontology; readOnlyHint disagrees"));
 406        }
 407        Governance g = d.governance();
 408        if (g == null) {
 409            return;
 410        }
 411        int tier = ontology.riskTierFor(capability);
 412        if (g.riskTier() != tier) {
 413            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-05", d.name(),
 414                    "the ontology sets tier " + tier + " for this capability; the descriptor says "
 415                            + g.riskTier() + ". Change the override in the ontology, with a note, "
 416                            + "or change the descriptor"));
 417        }
 418        if (g.approval() != null && g.approval().mode() != ontology.approvalFor(capability)) {
 419            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-06", d.name(),
 420                    "tier " + tier + " requires approval mode " + ontology.approvalFor(capability)));
 421        }
 422        if (entity.entitlement() != null && !g.entitlements().contains(entity.entitlement())
 423                && operation.readOnly()) {
 424            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-07", d.name(),
 425                    "entity " + capability.entity() + " requires the entitlement "
 426                            + entity.entitlement()));
 427        }
 428        if (g.dataClassification() != null && entity.classification() != null
 429                && g.dataClassification().ordinal() < entity.classification().ordinal()) {
 430            out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-08", d.name(),
 431                    "entity " + capability.entity() + " is classified "
 432                            + entity.classification() + "; a tool returning it cannot be "
 433                            + g.dataClassification()));
 434        }
 435        patterns(d, capability, out);
 436    }
 437
 438    /** Every identifier-typed parameter must carry the ontology's pattern, character for character. */
 439    private void patterns(ToolDescriptor d, Ontology.Capability capability, List<Finding> out) {
 440        JsonNode properties = d.inputSchema().path("properties");
 441        for (String type : capability.consumes()) {
 442            Ontology.IdentifierType identifier = ontology.identifierTypes().get(type);
 443            if (identifier == null || identifier.pattern() == null) {
 444                continue;
 445            }
 446            boolean carried = properties.values().stream().anyMatch(property ->
 447                    identifier.pattern().equals(property.path("pattern").asString(""))
 448                            || identifier.pattern()
 449                                    .equals(property.path("items").path("pattern").asString("")));
 450            if (!carried) {
 451                out.add(Finding.error("TS-ONT-09", d.name(),
 452                        "consumes " + type + " but no parameter carries its pattern "
 453                                + identifier.pattern() + "; a looser pattern here is how a "
 454                                + "malformed identifier reaches the handler"));
 455            }
 456        }
 457    }
 458
 459    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ the set
 460
 461    /** Rules about the catalog rather than about any one descriptor. */
 462    public List<Finding> lintSet(List<ToolDescriptor> catalog) {
 463        List<Finding> out = new ArrayList<>();
 464        Map<String, Long> byTitle = new java.util.HashMap<>();
 465        for (ToolDescriptor d : catalog) {
 466            byTitle.merge(d.title() == null ? "" : d.title().toLowerCase(), 1L, Long::sum);
 467        }
 468        byTitle.forEach((title, count) -> {
 469            if (count > 1) {
 470                out.add(Finding.error("TS-SET-01", "(catalog)",
 471                        count + " tools share the title \"" + title + "\"; a human approving one "
 472                                + "of them cannot tell which"));
 473            }
 474        });
 475        if (ontology != null) {
 476            Set<String> present = new TreeSet<>(catalog.stream().map(ToolDescriptor::name).toList());
 477            for (Ontology.Capability capability : ontology.capabilities()) {
 478                if (!present.contains(capability.tool())) {
 479                    out.add(Finding.error("TS-SET-02", capability.tool(),
 480                            "the ontology declares this capability but no descriptor implements it"));
 481                }
 482            }
 483            for (String dead : ontology.unreachableIdentifiers()) {
 484                out.add(Finding.error("TS-SET-03", "(catalog)",
 485                        dead + " is consumed by a tool but produced by none; the agent has no "
 486                                + "way to obtain it except from the customer typing it exactly"));
 487            }
 488        }
 489        long writers = catalog.stream()
 490                .filter(d -> d.annotations() != null && !d.annotations().readOnlyHint()).count();
 491        if (writers > 0 && catalog.size() / writers < 2) {
 492            out.add(Finding.warning("TS-SET-04", "(catalog)",
 493                    "most of this catalog changes state; a model needs reads to orient itself "
 494                            + "before it is safe to let it write"));
 495        }
 496        return out;
 497    }
 498
 499    public static boolean failed(List<Finding> findings) {
 500        return findings.stream().anyMatch(f -> f.severity() == Finding.Severity.ERROR);
 501    }
 502}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.io.IOException;
   4import java.io.InputStream;
   5import java.nio.file.Files;
   6import java.nio.file.Path;
   7import java.util.ArrayList;
   8import java.util.Comparator;
   9import java.util.List;
  10
  11import tools.jackson.databind.DeserializationFeature;
  12import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
  13import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;
  14
  15/**
  16 * Reads descriptors from JSON and writes them back. One mapper, configured once, shared by the
  17 * linter, the registry, the handlers and the tests, so that a descriptor cannot pass the linter
  18 * under one set of Jackson settings and fail in production under another.
  19 *
  20 * <p>Two settings matter, and one default is worth naming. Unknown properties fail, because a
  21 * misspelled governance key is a review finding rather than something to shrug off at load time.
  22 * Null fields are left out, so the descriptor a reviewer reads is the descriptor its author wrote.
  23 * And Jackson 3 writes {@code java.time} values as ISO-8601 strings without being asked, which is
  24 * what the model needs: it reads {@code 2026-10-01T14:30:00Z} as a time and reads
  25 * {@code 1790865000} as a quantity.
  26 */
  27public final class DescriptorCodec {
  28
  29    private static final JsonMapper MAPPER = JsonMapper.builder()
  30            .enable(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES)
  31            .build();
  32
  33    private DescriptorCodec() {
  34    }
  35
  36    public static JsonMapper mapper() {
  37        return MAPPER;
  38    }
  39
  40    public static ToolDescriptor read(String json) {
  41        return MAPPER.readValue(json, ToolDescriptor.class);
  42    }
  43
  44    public static ToolDescriptor read(Path file) throws IOException {
  45        return read(Files.readString(file));
  46    }
  47
  48    public static ToolDescriptor read(InputStream in) throws IOException {
  49        try (in) {
  50            return read(new String(in.readAllBytes()));
  51        }
  52    }
  53
  54    /** Pretty JSON, two-space indent, trailing newline: the form the catalog is committed in. */
  55    public static String write(ToolDescriptor descriptor) {
  56        return MAPPER.writerWithDefaultPrettyPrinter().writeValueAsString(descriptor) + "\n";
  57    }
  58
  59    public static <T> T convert(JsonNode node, Class<T> type) {
  60        return MAPPER.treeToValue(node, type);
  61    }
  62
  63    public static JsonNode tree(String json) {
  64        return MAPPER.readTree(json);
  65    }
  66
  67    public static JsonNode tree(Object value) {
  68        return MAPPER.valueToTree(value);
  69    }
  70
  71    public static String json(Object value) {
  72        return MAPPER.writeValueAsString(value);
  73    }
  74
  75    /**
  76     * Every {@code *.json} file in a directory, read in name order so that a catalog listing is
  77     * stable across machines and the book's figures do not reshuffle between builds.
  78     */
  79    public static List<ToolDescriptor> readDirectory(Path directory) throws IOException {
  80        List<ToolDescriptor> descriptors = new ArrayList<>();
  81        try (var files = Files.list(directory)) {
  82            for (Path file : files.filter(f -> f.toString().endsWith(".json"))
  83                    .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Path::getFileName)).toList()) {
  84                descriptors.add(read(file));
  85            }
  86        }
  87        return descriptors;
  88    }
  89}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3/**
   4 * The closed error taxonomy: fifteen codes, and a tool may return no others.
   5 *
   6 * <p>A closed taxonomy exists so that the agent can be taught once what to do about each code
   7 * instead of guessing from prose. Two properties are attached to every code because they are the
   8 * only two questions the model actually needs answered: may I try this again, and is the fix
   9 * mine to make?
  10 *
  11 * <p>{@link #retryable} says whether an identical retry could plausibly succeed. {@link #callerCanFix}
  12 * says whether the caller has anything to change — a bad argument it can correct, a token it can
  13 * refresh — as opposed to a condition it can only report. When both are false the agent's only
  14 * correct move is to tell the customer and stop; an agent that loops on {@code NOT_ENTITLED} is a
  15 * defect in the toolset, not in the model.
  16 *
  17 * <p>Each code also carries the sentence the generated briefing shows the model. Keeping that
  18 * sentence here, next to the flags it has to agree with, is the difference between a prompt that
  19 * matches the taxonomy and a prompt that used to.
  20 */
  21public enum ErrorCode {
  22
  23    /** Arguments failed the input schema, or failed a rule the schema cannot express. */
  24    INVALID_ARGUMENT(false, true,
  25            "Your arguments were wrong. The message names the field. Fix it and call the same tool "
  26                    + "again — a different tool will have the same problem."),
  27
  28    /** The name is not in this principal's catalog. Never a hint to try a near miss. */
  29    UNKNOWN_TOOL(false, true,
  30            "That tool does not exist in this session. Use one of the tools you were given, "
  31                    + "spelled exactly as given. Do not guess at a similar name."),
  32
  33    /** The named entity does not exist, or exists outside what this principal may see. */
  34    NOT_FOUND(false, true,
  35            "The thing you named is not there. Do not try variations of the identifier. Use the "
  36                    + "list tool the remediation points at, and tell the customer if it is "
  37                    + "genuinely absent."),
  38
  39    /** The request is well formed but the principal lacks the entitlement. Do not retry. */
  40    NOT_ENTITLED(false, false,
  41            "This session is not permitted to do that. Say so plainly and stop. Do not look for "
  42                    + "another tool that might not check."),
  43
  44    /** A human has to agree first. The accompanying approval reference says who and how. */
  45    APPROVAL_REQUIRED(false, true,
  46            "A human has to agree first. Show the customer what the message quotes, wait for a "
  47                    + "clear yes, then call the same tool again with identical arguments. If they "
  48                    + "say no, stop."),
  49
  50    /** The confirmation token has expired or was already spent. Preview again. */
  51    CONFIRMATION_EXPIRED(false, true,
  52            "The confirmation is no longer good. Preview again, read the customer the fresh "
  53                    + "figures, and proceed only if they agree again."),
  54
  55    /** The world is not in the state the call needs — market closed, position already flat. */
  56    PRECONDITION_FAILED(false, false,
  57            "The world is not in a state where this can happen. Tell the customer the reason in "
  58                    + "the message. Nothing you call will change it."),
  59
  60    /** Someone else changed the entity first. Re-read it before deciding again. */
  61    CONFLICT(false, true,
  62            "Something changed underneath you. Read the entity again, tell the customer what it "
  63                    + "says now, and ask before acting on the new state."),
  64
  65    /** Too many calls from this principal. The retryAfterSeconds field says how long to wait. */
  66    RATE_LIMITED(true, false,
  67            "You have called this too often. Wait the number of seconds in retryAfterSeconds, "
  68                    + "tell the customer there is a short delay, and do not call anything else in "
  69                    + "the meantime."),
  70
  71    /** A budget is exhausted for the period. Waiting will not help inside this session. */
  72    QUOTA_EXCEEDED(false, false,
  73            "A budget is used up for today. Waiting will not help in this conversation. Tell the "
  74                    + "customer and offer what you can still see."),
  75
  76    /** A system the tool depends on is down. Retrying later may work; retrying now will not. */
  77    UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE(true, false,
  78            "A system behind this tool is down. Tell the customer the feature is unavailable right "
  79                    + "now. Do not retry in this conversation."),
  80
  81    /** A dependency did not answer in time. The call may or may not have taken effect. */
  82    UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT(true, false,
  83            "It is not known whether that took effect. Never say it did or did not. Read the "
  84                    + "entity back with the matching get tool and report what you find."),
  85
  86    /** The request matches more than one entity. The candidates field lists them; ask. */
  87    AMBIGUOUS_REQUEST(false, true,
  88            "More than one thing matches. Read the candidates to the customer and ask which they "
  89                    + "mean. Do not pick for them."),
  90
  91    /** A legitimate request this tool does not implement. Another tool may; the catalog says. */
  92    UNSUPPORTED(false, false,
  93            "This tool does not do that. If the message names another tool, use it. Otherwise tell "
  94                    + "the customer it is not something you can do."),
  95
  96    /** Something broke that the caller cannot act on. Report the requestId and stop. */
  97    INTERNAL_ERROR(true, false,
  98            "Something broke. Tell the customer the request failed, give them the requestId from "
  99                    + "the envelope, and stop.");
 100
 101    private final boolean retryable;
 102    private final boolean callerCanFix;
 103    private final String guidance;
 104
 105    ErrorCode(boolean retryable, boolean callerCanFix, String guidance) {
 106        this.retryable = retryable;
 107        this.callerCanFix = callerCanFix;
 108        this.guidance = guidance;
 109    }
 110
 111    /** The sentence the generated toolset briefing shows the model for this code. */
 112    public String guidance() {
 113        return guidance;
 114    }
 115
 116    /** Whether an identical retry could plausibly succeed. */
 117    public boolean retryable() {
 118        return retryable;
 119    }
 120
 121    /** Whether the caller has something to change before trying again. */
 122    public boolean callerCanFix() {
 123        return callerCanFix;
 124    }
 125
 126    /** True when the agent's only correct move is to report the condition and stop. */
 127    public boolean terminal() {
 128        return !retryable && !callerCanFix;
 129    }
 130}

tool-contract/src/main/java/com/example/brokerage/tooling/contract/Finding.java40 lines

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3/**
   4 * One conformance finding. The rule identifier is the point: a review comment that says "this
   5 * description is a bit thin" starts an argument, and one that says "TS-DSC-04: the description
   6 * never says when not to use the tool" starts a fix.
   7 */
   8public record Finding(String rule, Severity severity, String tool, String where, String message) {
   9
  10    public enum Severity {
  11        /** A MUST in the specification. The build fails. */
  12        ERROR,
  13        /** A SHOULD. The build passes and the review asks about it. */
  14        WARNING,
  15        /** Worth knowing when reading a catalog, never a gate. */
  16        INFO
  17    }
  18
  19    public static Finding error(String rule, String tool, String message) {
  20        return new Finding(rule, Severity.ERROR, tool, null, message);
  21    }
  22
  23    public static Finding error(String rule, String tool, String where, String message) {
  24        return new Finding(rule, Severity.ERROR, tool, where, message);
  25    }
  26
  27    public static Finding warning(String rule, String tool, String message) {
  28        return new Finding(rule, Severity.WARNING, tool, null, message);
  29    }
  30
  31    public static Finding warning(String rule, String tool, String where, String message) {
  32        return new Finding(rule, Severity.WARNING, tool, where, message);
  33    }
  34
  35    @Override
  36    public String toString() {
  37        String place = where == null || where.isEmpty() ? "" : " at " + where;
  38        return "%-6s %-10s %s%s: %s".formatted(severity, rule, tool, place, message);
  39    }
  40}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.util.List;
   4
   5import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnoreProperties;
   6import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonInclude;
   7import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonProperty;
   8
   9/**
  10 * The governance block, carried in {@code _meta} under a reverse-DNS key so that it travels with
  11 * the descriptor and is never rendered into the model's context.
  12 *
  13 * <p>Every field here answers a question somebody will eventually ask in an incident review: who
  14 * owns this, what can it see, who may call it, who has to agree before it runs, how long do we
  15 * keep the record, and what breaks when it is turned off.
  16 */
  17@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  18@JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = false)
  19public record Governance(
  20        String version,
  21        Lifecycle lifecycle,
  22        ConformanceLevel conformanceLevel,
  23        int riskTier,
  24        Owner owner,
  25        DataClassification dataClassification,
  26        boolean containsPii,
  27        List<String> piiFields,
  28        List<String> entitlements,
  29        Approval approval,
  30        RecordKeeping recordKeeping,
  31        Cost cost,
  32        RateLimit rateLimit,
  33        List<String> dependencies,
  34        Availability availability,
  35        Evaluation evaluation) {
  36
  37    /**
  38     * The JSON spellings are pinned with {@link JsonProperty} rather than derived from the Java
  39     * names, because these strings appear in published descriptors and in audit records: renaming
  40     * a Java constant must never silently change a wire value.
  41     */
  42    public enum Lifecycle {
  43        @JsonProperty("draft") DRAFT,
  44        @JsonProperty("active") ACTIVE,
  45        @JsonProperty("deprecated") DEPRECATED,
  46        @JsonProperty("retired") RETIRED
  47    }
  48
  49    public enum ConformanceLevel { L0, L1, L2, L3 }
  50
  51    public enum DataClassification {
  52        @JsonProperty("public") PUBLIC,
  53        @JsonProperty("internal") INTERNAL,
  54        @JsonProperty("customer-confidential") CUSTOMER_CONFIDENTIAL,
  55        @JsonProperty("restricted") RESTRICTED
  56    }
  57
  58    /**
  59     * How much human agreement an invocation needs. The mode is a property of the tool, not of
  60     * the conversation: an agent cannot talk its way into a lower mode.
  61     */
  62    public enum ApprovalMode {
  63        @JsonProperty("none") NONE,
  64        @JsonProperty("notify") NOTIFY,
  65        @JsonProperty("confirm") CONFIRM,
  66        @JsonProperty("dualControl") DUAL_CONTROL,
  67        @JsonProperty("humanExecution") HUMAN_EXECUTION
  68    }
  69
  70    public record Owner(String team, String contact, String escalation) {
  71    }
  72
  73    public record Approval(ApprovalMode mode, String confirmationTemplate, Integer expiresInSeconds) {
  74    }
  75
  76    public record RecordKeeping(String auditEvent, String retention, List<String> regulatoryBasis) {
  77    }
  78
  79    public record Cost(@JsonProperty("class") String costClass, Integer p95LatencyMs) {
  80    }
  81
  82    public record RateLimit(Integer perPrincipalPerMinute, Integer perPrincipalPerDay) {
  83    }
  84
  85    public record Availability(String slo, String killSwitch) {
  86    }
  87
  88    /** What the agent evaluation suite last measured. Stale numbers are a review finding. */
  89    public record Evaluation(String suite, String lastRunAt, Double selectionAccuracy,
  90                             Double refusalAccuracy, Double argumentAccuracy) {
  91    }
  92
  93    public boolean requiresApproval() {
  94        return approval != null && approval.mode() != ApprovalMode.NONE
  95                && approval.mode() != ApprovalMode.NOTIFY;
  96    }
  97}

   7/**
   8 * One attempt to call one tool. Everything a handler is allowed to know.
   9 *
  10 * <p>Note what is <em>not</em> here: the conversation. A handler cannot read the chat history,
  11 * cannot see the system prompt, and cannot be talked into anything, because it is never shown the
  12 * talking. All it has is a descriptor, a set of arguments that have already been validated against
  13 * that descriptor's schema, and a principal the runtime established. That is the whole reason a
  14 * tool is a safer surface than a prompt.
  15 *
  16 * @param descriptor the contract this call is being held to
  17 * @param arguments  the model's arguments, already validated; a handler never re-checks the schema
  18 * @param principal  who the call is for
  19 * @param requestId  the correlation identifier, echoed in the envelope and in the audit record
  20 * @param startedAt  when the runtime accepted the call, for the latency the envelope reports
  21 */
  22public record Invocation(ToolDescriptor descriptor, JsonNode arguments, Principal principal,
  23                         String requestId, Instant startedAt) {
  24
  25    public String string(String name) {
  26        JsonNode node = arguments.path(name);
  27        return node.isMissingNode() || node.isNull() ? null : node.asString();
  28    }
  29
  30    public String string(String name, String fallback) {
  31        String value = string(name);
  32        return value == null ? fallback : value;
  33    }
  34
  35    public Integer integer(String name) {
  36        JsonNode node = arguments.path(name);
  37        return node.isMissingNode() || node.isNull() ? null : node.asInt();
  38    }
  39
  40    public int integer(String name, int fallback) {
  41        Integer value = integer(name);
  42        return value == null ? fallback : value;
  43    }
  44
  45    public boolean flag(String name, boolean fallback) {
  46        JsonNode node = arguments.path(name);
  47        return node.isMissingNode() || node.isNull() ? fallback : node.asBoolean();
  48    }
  49
  50    public JsonNode node(String name) {
  51        return arguments.path(name);
  52    }
  53
  54    public boolean has(String name) {
  55        JsonNode node = arguments.path(name);
  56        return !node.isMissingNode() && !node.isNull();
  57    }
  58}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.io.IOException;
   4import java.io.InputStream;
   5import java.nio.file.Files;
   6import java.nio.file.Path;
   7import java.util.ArrayList;
   8import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
   9import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
  10import java.util.List;
  11import java.util.Map;
  12import java.util.Set;
  13
  14import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonInclude;
  15
  16/**
  17 * The domain ontology: the things a brokerage tool can operate on, the operations it can perform,
  18 * the identifiers that join one call to the next, and the policy that follows from both.
  19 *
  20 * <p>An ontology sounds like an academic luxury until the catalog passes about a dozen tools. Then
  21 * three problems arrive together. Names stop agreeing with each other, so the model cannot
  22 * generalize from one tool to the next. Nobody can say whether the catalog is complete, because
  23 * there is no statement of what it ought to cover. And the risk tier on each descriptor becomes a
  24 * matter of whoever wrote it, which is exactly the kind of judgment an auditor will ask you to
  25 * justify two years later.
  26 *
  27 * <p>This ontology fixes all three mechanically. The tool name is <em>derived</em> from the entity
  28 * and the operation rather than chosen, so {@code brokerage_order_cancel} could not have been
  29 * called {@code cancelOrder} or {@code brokerage_cancel_order}. Completeness is a question about
  30 * the capability table rather than about anyone's memory. And the risk tier comes from the
  31 * operation, with every exception recorded as an override that a reviewer can see.
  32 *
  33 * <p>It also produces the one thing an agent needs that no single descriptor can give it: the
  34 * <em>producer graph</em>. {@code brokerage_order_place} requires a {@code ConfirmationToken},
  35 * and exactly one capability in the catalog produces one. That is why preview-before-place is
  36 * structural here rather than advisory — not because the description asks nicely, but because
  37 * there is no other way for the agent to obtain the argument.
  38 */
  39@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  40public record Ontology(
  41        String id,
  42        String version,
  43        String domain,
  44        String description,
  45        Map<String, IdentifierType> identifierTypes,
  46        Map<String, Entity> entities,
  47        Map<String, Operation> operations,
  48        List<Capability> capabilities,
  49        Policies policies) {
  50
  51    /**
  52     * A value that joins one call to the next. Identifier types are declared once here and
  53     * referenced by the schemas, which is what stops one descriptor accepting
  54     * {@code ^acct_[A-Z0-9]+$} while its neighbour accepts {@code ^ACC-\d{4}$}.
  55     */
  56    public record IdentifierType(String description, String pattern, String example,
  57                                 boolean opaque) {
  58    }
  59
  60    /**
  61     * A thing the domain is about. {@code term} and {@code collectionTerm} are the slugs that
  62     * appear in tool names; {@code classification} and {@code entitlement} are the floor that
  63     * every descriptor touching this entity must meet or exceed.
  64     */
  65    public record Entity(String label, String term, String collectionTerm, String identifier,
  66                         String description,
  67                         Governance.DataClassification classification,
  68                         String entitlement, boolean mutable, List<Relation> relations) {
  69
  70        public Entity {
  71            relations = relations == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(relations);
  72        }
  73    }
  74
  75    /** How one entity reaches another. The agent reads these as paths, not as decoration. */
  76    public record Relation(String name, String target, String cardinality, String description) {
  77    }
  78
  79    /**
  80     * A verb from the closed vocabulary. The vocabulary is closed so that {@code readOnly},
  81     * {@code idempotent} and the base risk tier can be checked against the name instead of
  82     * trusted from the descriptor, which is the one place a tool author's optimism is most
  83     * expensive.
  84     */
  85    public record Operation(String gloss, boolean readOnly, boolean idempotent, int baseRiskTier,
  86                            String semantics) {
  87    }
  88
  89    /**
  90     * One tool, stated as (operation, entity) with the identifiers it needs and the identifiers it
  91     * hands back. This table <em>is</em> the catalog's specification: the descriptors implement it.
  92     *
  93     * @param cardinality {@code one} or {@code many}; decides the singular or plural term in the name
  94     * @param consumes    identifier types that must be in hand before this tool can be called
  95     * @param produces    identifier types this tool returns, making further calls possible
  96     * @param riskTier    null to take the operation's base tier; a number to override it
  97     * @param note        why an override exists, or what the capability is for; printed by reviews
  98     */
  99    @JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
 100    public record Capability(String tool, String operation, String entity, String cardinality,
 101                             List<String> consumes, List<String> produces, Integer riskTier,
 102                             String note) {
 103
 104        public Capability {
 105            consumes = consumes == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(consumes);
 106            produces = produces == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(produces);
 107        }
 108
 109        public boolean many() {
 110            return "many".equals(cardinality);
 111        }
 112    }
 113
 114    /**
 115     * The rules that turn a risk tier into an approval mode, and the ceiling on what a single
 116     * agent turn may do without a human. These live in the ontology rather than in each
 117     * descriptor so that raising the bar is one edit, reviewable in one diff.
 118     */
 119    public record Policies(Map<Integer, Governance.ApprovalMode> approvalByRiskTier,
 120                           Map<Integer, String> evidenceByRiskTier,
 121                           int maxTierWithoutApproval,
 122                           List<String> dualControlAbove) {
 123    }
 124
 125    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ derived views
 126
 127    /** The name this capability must carry: {@code <domain>_<term>_<operation>}. */
 128    public String nameFor(Capability capability) {
 129        Entity entity = entities.get(capability.entity());
 130        String term = capability.many() ? entity.collectionTerm() : entity.term();
 131        return domain + "_" + term + "_" + capability.operation();
 132    }
 133
 134    /** The tier this capability must carry: the operation's base tier unless overridden. */
 135    public int riskTierFor(Capability capability) {
 136        return capability.riskTier() != null
 137                ? capability.riskTier()
 138                : operations.get(capability.operation()).baseRiskTier();
 139    }
 140
 141    public Governance.ApprovalMode approvalFor(Capability capability) {
 142        return policies.approvalByRiskTier().getOrDefault(riskTierFor(capability),
 143                Governance.ApprovalMode.CONFIRM);
 144    }
 145
 146    public Capability capabilityOf(String toolName) {
 147        return capabilities.stream().filter(c -> c.tool().equals(toolName)).findFirst().orElse(null);
 148    }
 149
 150    /**
 151     * Identifier type to the tools that hand one out. This is the index behind every "from
 152     * {@code brokerage_accounts_list}" in a description, and the linter checks the prose against
 153     * it so the two cannot drift.
 154     */
 155    public Map<String, List<String>> producers() {
 156        Map<String, List<String>> index = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 157        for (String type : identifierTypes.keySet()) {
 158            index.put(type, capabilities.stream().filter(c -> c.produces().contains(type))
 159                    .map(Capability::tool).toList());
 160        }
 161        return index;
 162    }
 163
 164    /**
 165     * The tools that must run before this one, because they are the only source of something it
 166     * consumes. An agent that is told this once stops guessing identifiers.
 167     */
 168    public Set<String> prerequisitesOf(String toolName) {
 169        Capability capability = capabilityOf(toolName);
 170        if (capability == null) {
 171            return Set.of();
 172        }
 173        Map<String, List<String>> producers = producers();
 174        Set<String> needed = new LinkedHashSet<>();
 175        for (String type : capability.consumes()) {
 176            producers.getOrDefault(type, List.of()).stream()
 177                    .filter(tool -> !tool.equals(toolName))
 178                    .forEach(needed::add);
 179        }
 180        return needed;
 181    }
 182
 183    /**
 184     * Identifier types nothing in the catalog produces. Every one is a dead end: a tool the agent
 185     * can read about but can never correctly call, because the argument has to come from the
 186     * customer typing it exactly right.
 187     */
 188    public List<String> unreachableIdentifiers() {
 189        Map<String, List<String>> producers = producers();
 190        List<String> dead = new ArrayList<>();
 191        for (Capability capability : capabilities) {
 192            for (String type : capability.consumes()) {
 193                if (producers.getOrDefault(type, List.of()).isEmpty() && !dead.contains(type)) {
 194                    dead.add(type);
 195                }
 196            }
 197        }
 198        return dead;
 199    }
 200
 201    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ loading
 202
 203    public static Ontology read(String json) {
 204        return DescriptorCodec.mapper().readValue(json, Ontology.class);
 205    }
 206
 207    public static Ontology read(Path file) throws IOException {
 208        return read(Files.readString(file));
 209    }
 210
 211    public static Ontology read(InputStream in) throws IOException {
 212        try (in) {
 213            return read(new String(in.readAllBytes()));
 214        }
 215    }
 216}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.util.Set;
   4
   5/**
   6 * Who the call is for. Established by the runtime from the session, and never, under any
   7 * circumstances, from an argument the model supplied.
   8 *
   9 * <p>This is the single most important boundary in a tool system, and it is easy to cross by
  10 * accident. The temptation is obvious: an {@code accountId} parameter is already in the schema, so
  11 * why not a {@code customerId} parameter too, and then one agent can serve a whole book of
  12 * business. The answer is that the model's arguments are derived from the conversation, the
  13 * conversation contains whatever the customer typed, and a customer who types another person's
  14 * identifier has just read their account. Identity is not negotiable by the party being
  15 * identified.
  16 *
  17 * <p>So {@code accountId} is a legitimate parameter — the model chooses between accounts the
  18 * customer holds — while {@code customerId} is not, and the linter rejects it by name.
  19 *
  20 * @param subject     the authenticated subject, as the audit record will show it
  21 * @param customerId  the customer whose data this session may see, resolved from the subject
  22 * @param entitlements scopes the subject holds, checked against each descriptor before execution
  23 * @param sessionId   the conversation, for binding confirmation tokens and for correlating audit
  24 */
  25public record Principal(String subject, String customerId, Set<String> entitlements,
  26                        String sessionId) {
  27
  28    public Principal {
  29        entitlements = Set.copyOf(entitlements);
  30    }
  31
  32    public boolean holds(String entitlement) {
  33        return entitlements.contains(entitlement);
  34    }
  35
  36    public boolean holdsAll(Iterable<String> required) {
  37        for (String entitlement : required) {
  38            if (!holds(entitlement)) {
  39                return false;
  40            }
  41        }
  42        return true;
  43    }
  44}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.util.List;
   4import java.util.Set;
   5
   6import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
   7
   8/**
   9 * The JSON Schema profile a descriptor's schemas must stay inside.
  10 *
  11 * <p>JSON Schema is far larger than any tool-calling runtime supports, and the parts that are
  12 * supported unevenly are exactly the parts that fail silently: a model shown
  13 * {@code oneOf} will cheerfully produce an object matching none of the branches, and the runtime
  14 * that dropped the keyword on the way to the model has no way to say so. So the profile is a
  15 * whitelist, not a blacklist, and the linter enforces it.
  16 *
  17 * <p>The rule behind the whitelist: a keyword is permitted when it either constrains a scalar in a
  18 * way every runtime forwards, or describes structure. Keywords that express alternation,
  19 * negation or conditionals are not permitted — model them as an enum and separate fields, or as
  20 * two tools.
  21 */
  22public final class SchemaProfile {
  23
  24    /** Keywords any schema in a descriptor may use. */
  25    public static final Set<String> PERMITTED = Set.of(
  26            "type", "properties", "required", "additionalProperties", "items", "description",
  27            "enum", "const", "default", "format", "pattern", "minimum", "maximum",
  28            "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum", "minLength", "maxLength", "minItems",
  29            "maxItems", "uniqueItems", "$defs", "$ref", "title", "examples");
  30
  31    /**
  32     * Keywords that are rejected rather than ignored, each for a reason the author needs to hear.
  33     * The message is the one the linter prints, so it says what to do instead.
  34     */
  35    public static final List<Prohibition> PROHIBITED = List.of(
  36            new Prohibition("oneOf", "Alternation is forwarded inconsistently and the model cannot "
  37                    + "see which branch it failed. Use an enum discriminator, or split the tool."),
  38            new Prohibition("anyOf", "Same as oneOf, with the added problem that a partially valid "
  39                    + "object passes. Name the variants explicitly."),
  40            new Prohibition("allOf", "Composition the model cannot see through. Inline the fields."),
  41            new Prohibition("not", "Negative constraints give the model nothing to aim at. State "
  42                    + "the permitted values."),
  43            new Prohibition("if", "Conditional schemas are dropped by most runtimes, so the model "
  44                    + "never learns the condition. Split into two tools or validate in the handler."),
  45            new Prohibition("then", "The branch of a conditional the model never sees. Split the "
  46                    + "tool, or enforce the rule in the handler and state it in the description."),
  47            new Prohibition("else", "The other branch of a conditional the model never sees. Split "
  48                    + "the tool, or enforce the rule in the handler and state it in the "
  49                    + "description."),
  50            new Prohibition("dependentRequired", "Cross-field requirements belong in the description "
  51                    + "and in the handler, where a violation can be explained."),
  52            new Prohibition("dependentSchemas", "See dependentRequired."),
  53            new Prohibition("patternProperties", "An object whose keys carry meaning is a list of "
  54                    + "records. Model it as an array."),
  55            new Prohibition("additionalItems", "Tuple typing is not forwarded. Use a fixed object."),
  56            new Prohibition("unevaluatedProperties", "Depends on annotation collection the runtime "
  57                    + "does not perform. Close the object with additionalProperties: false."),
  58            new Prohibition("$dynamicRef", "Resolution varies by implementation."),
  59            new Prohibition("$recursiveRef", "Withdrawn from the specification."),
  60            new Prohibition("contentEncoding", "Binary in an argument is a design mistake. Pass a "
  61                    + "reference the tool can resolve."),
  62            new Prohibition("contentMediaType", "See contentEncoding."));
  63
  64    /** Parameter names a descriptor may not use, because a runtime or the firm has claimed them. */
  65    public static final Set<String> RESERVED_PARAMETERS = Set.of(
  66            // Identity. Established by the runtime from the session, never by the model.
  67            "principal", "principalId", "customerId", "customerNumber", "userId", "user",
  68            "subject", "onBehalfOf", "impersonate",
  69            // Authorization. A scope the caller can name is not a scope.
  70            "role", "roles", "scope", "scopes", "entitlement", "entitlements",
  71            // Credentials. If a tool needs one, the runtime holds it.
  72            "token", "accessToken", "apiKey", "secret", "password",
  73            // Overrides. Every one of these is a way around a check somebody wrote on purpose.
  74            "dryRun", "force", "skipValidation", "skipChecks", "override", "sudo", "admin",
  75            // Runtime bookkeeping. Supplied by the pipeline, echoed in the envelope.
  76            "requestId", "traceId", "idempotencyKey", "toolName", "_meta");
  77
  78    public record Prohibition(String keyword, String why) {
  79    }
  80
  81    private SchemaProfile() {
  82    }
  83
  84    public static Prohibition prohibitionFor(String keyword) {
  85        return PROHIBITED.stream().filter(p -> p.keyword().equals(keyword)).findFirst().orElse(null);
  86    }
  87
  88    /**
  89     * True when this node is a schema object rather than a map of schemas. {@code properties} and
  90     * {@code $defs} hold schemas under arbitrary names, so their children are schemas and they
  91     * themselves are not; everything else that has a {@code type} or a {@code $ref} is.
  92     */
  93    public static boolean isSchemaObject(JsonNode node) {
  94        return node != null && node.isObject()
  95                && (node.has("type") || node.has("$ref") || node.has("enum") || node.has("const"));
  96    }
  97}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.util.List;
   4import java.util.Map;
   5
   6import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnore;
   7import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonInclude;
   8import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
   9
  10/**
  11 * A tool descriptor: everything a runtime needs to publish one tool to a model, and everything
  12 * the firm needs to govern it. Eight fields, and only eight, because the descriptor is the
  13 * contract and anything else is an implementation detail of whoever is serving it.
  14 *
  15 * <p>Four of the fields are rendered into the model's context and the model's decisions turn on
  16 * them: {@code name}, {@code title}, {@code description} and {@code inputSchema}. One field,
  17 * {@code outputSchema}, is a promise to the caller rather than a prompt to the model. The rest
  18 * never reach the model at all: {@code annotations} tell the runtime how much to trust the call,
  19 * {@code icons} decorate a user interface, and {@code _meta} carries governance.
  20 *
  21 * <p>The descriptor is transport-neutral on purpose. It names no protocol and no framework, which
  22 * is what lets one catalog serve a Spring AI agent, a desktop client and a batch job without any
  23 * of them renaming a thing.
  24 */
  25@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  26public record ToolDescriptor(
  27        String name,
  28        String title,
  29        String description,
  30        JsonNode inputSchema,
  31        JsonNode outputSchema,
  32        Annotations annotations,
  33        List<Icon> icons,
  34        Map<String, JsonNode> _meta) {
  35
  36    /** The reverse-DNS namespace this book's governance block is published under. */
  37    public static final String GOVERNANCE_KEY = "com.example.tooling/governance";
  38
  39    public ToolDescriptor {
  40        icons = icons == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(icons);
  41        _meta = _meta == null ? Map.of() : Map.copyOf(_meta);
  42    }
  43
  44    /**
  45     * Behavioral hints. All four are stated explicitly on every descriptor, even where the value
  46     * is the specification's default, because "absent" and "false" are read differently by
  47     * different runtimes and a trading tool cannot afford that ambiguity.
  48     */
  49    public record Annotations(boolean readOnlyHint, boolean destructiveHint,
  50                              boolean idempotentHint, boolean openWorldHint) {
  51
  52        public static Annotations readOnly() {
  53            return new Annotations(true, false, true, true);
  54        }
  55    }
  56
  57    /** Decorative only. No control anywhere may depend on an icon being present or absent. */
  58    @JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  59    public record Icon(String src, String mimeType, String theme, List<String> sizes) {
  60    }
  61
  62    /** The governance block, parsed. Absent only on a descriptor that has not been reviewed yet. */
  63    @JsonIgnore
  64    public Governance governance() {
  65        JsonNode node = _meta.get(GOVERNANCE_KEY);
  66        return node == null ? null : DescriptorCodec.convert(node, Governance.class);
  67    }
  68
  69    /** The catalog identifier: dotted, hierarchical, and never sent over the wire. */
  70    @JsonIgnore
  71    public String catalogId() {
  72        return name.replace('_', '.');
  73    }
  74}

tool-contract/src/main/java/com/example/brokerage/tooling/contract/ToolFailure.java52 lines

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import java.util.List;
   4import java.util.Map;
   5
   6/**
   7 * How a handler says no.
   8 *
   9 * <p>It is an exception for the handler's convenience — a guard clause reads better than threading
  10 * a result type through five method calls — and the runtime converts it straight into an
  11 * {@code ok: false} envelope. The model never sees an exception, a class name or a stack trace.
  12 *
  13 * <p>Nothing else may escape a handler. An unexpected exception is caught by the pipeline, logged
  14 * with the request identifier, and returned as {@link ErrorCode#INTERNAL_ERROR} with no detail,
  15 * because the alternative is leaking a database constraint name into a customer conversation.
  16 */
  17public class ToolFailure extends RuntimeException {
  18
  19    private final transient ToolResult.Failure failure;
  20
  21    public ToolFailure(ToolResult.Failure failure) {
  22        super(failure.code() + ": " + failure.message());
  23        this.failure = failure;
  24    }
  25
  26    public ToolResult.Failure failure() {
  27        return failure;
  28    }
  29
  30    public static ToolFailure of(ErrorCode code, String message, String remediation) {
  31        return new ToolFailure(ToolResult.Failure.of(code, message, remediation));
  32    }
  33
  34    public static ToolFailure notFound(String what, String remediation) {
  35        return of(ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND, what + " was not found.", remediation);
  36    }
  37
  38    public static ToolFailure invalidArgument(String message, String remediation) {
  39        return of(ErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT, message, remediation);
  40    }
  41
  42    public static ToolFailure precondition(String message, String remediation) {
  43        return of(ErrorCode.PRECONDITION_FAILED, message, remediation);
  44    }
  45
  46    /** For {@link ErrorCode#AMBIGUOUS_REQUEST}: the choices the caller has to pick between. */
  47    public static ToolFailure ambiguous(String message, String remediation,
  48                                       List<Map<String, Object>> candidates) {
  49        return new ToolFailure(ToolResult.Failure.of(ErrorCode.AMBIGUOUS_REQUEST, message,
  50                remediation).withCandidates(candidates));
  51    }
  52}

tool-contract/src/main/java/com/example/brokerage/tooling/contract/ToolHandler.java26 lines

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3/**
   4 * The code behind one tool.
   5 *
   6 * <p>A handler is startlingly small in a well-built catalog, and that is the measure of whether
   7 * the descriptor is doing its job. Everything generic — schema validation, entitlements, approval,
   8 * rate limiting, the envelope, redaction, audit — happens in the pipeline around it. What is left
   9 * is the domain call and the few rules a JSON Schema cannot express.
  10 *
  11 * <p>If a handler is long, it is usually because the tool is doing two things, and the fix is two
  12 * tools. The second most common reason is that it is re-validating arguments the pipeline already
  13 * validated, which means somebody did not trust the schema — and an untrusted schema is a schema
  14 * the model is also being misled by.
  15 */
  16public interface ToolHandler {
  17
  18    /** The descriptor name this handler implements. Matched at startup, not at call time. */
  19    String name();
  20
  21    /**
  22     * Do the work and return the payload, which must conform to the descriptor's
  23     * {@code outputSchema}. Throw {@link ToolFailure} to return a taxonomy error instead.
  24     */
  25    Object handle(Invocation invocation);
  26}

   2
   3import java.time.Instant;
   4import java.util.List;
   5import java.util.Map;
   6
   7import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonInclude;
   8
   9/**
  10 * The result envelope. Every tool in the catalog returns this shape, successful or not, which is
  11 * why the envelope is specified once here rather than repeated in fourteen output schemas.
  12 *
  13 * <p>Two decisions in this record do most of the work.
  14 *
  15 * <p>The first is that failures arrive as data, not as exceptions. A tool that throws gives the
  16 * runtime a stack trace and gives the model a wall of text it was never taught to read. A tool
  17 * that returns {@code ok: false} with a code from the closed taxonomy gives the model something it
  18 * can branch on, and gives the agent's author something to assert in a test.
  19 *
  20 * <p>The second is that {@code meta} is never optional. {@code asOf} tells the model how old the
  21 * answer is, which matters the moment a quote is involved; {@code complete} tells it whether it is
  22 * looking at everything or at a page; {@code requestId} is the only thing a customer can quote back
  23 * to support. Leaving any of the three to the handler's discretion means some handler will omit it.
  24 *
  25 * @param <T> the payload type, which must conform to the descriptor's {@code outputSchema}
  26 */
  27@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  28public record ToolResult<T>(boolean ok, T data, Failure error, Meta meta) {
  29
  30    /**
  31     * A failure the model is expected to read and act on. {@code message} is written for the model
  32     * and is safe to paraphrase to a customer; {@code remediation} is written in the imperative
  33     * because that is the form an agent follows most reliably.
  34     */
  35    @JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  36    public record Failure(ErrorCode code, String message, String remediation, boolean retryable,
  37                          Integer retryAfterSeconds, List<Map<String, Object>> candidates,
  38                          String approvalReference) {
  39
  40        public static Failure of(ErrorCode code, String message, String remediation) {
  41            return new Failure(code, message, remediation, code.retryable(), null, null, null);
  42        }
  43
  44        public Failure retryAfter(int seconds) {
  45            return new Failure(code, message, remediation, true, seconds, candidates, approvalReference);
  46        }
  47
  48        /** Attach the choices the caller must pick between, for {@link ErrorCode#AMBIGUOUS_REQUEST}. */
  49        public Failure withCandidates(List<Map<String, Object>> options) {
  50            return new Failure(code, message, remediation, retryable, retryAfterSeconds, options,
  51                    approvalReference);
  52        }
  53
  54        public Failure withApprovalReference(String reference) {
  55            return new Failure(code, message, remediation, retryable, retryAfterSeconds, candidates,
  56                    reference);
  57        }
  58    }
  59
  60    /**
  61     * Provenance for the payload. Present on success and on failure, because "when did you ask"
  62     * is as interesting after a timeout as after a fill.
  63     *
  64     * @param asOf      the instant the data describes, not the instant the envelope was written
  65     * @param complete  false when the payload was paged or truncated
  66     * @param nextCursor an opaque forward cursor, or null when complete
  67     * @param truncated what was dropped to fit the budget, in words the model can relay
  68     */
  69    @JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  70    public record Meta(Instant asOf, String toolVersion, String requestId, boolean complete,
  71                       String nextCursor, String truncated, Long latencyMs) {
  72    }
  73
  74    public static <T> ToolResult<T> success(T data, Meta meta) {
  75        return new ToolResult<>(true, data, null, meta);
  76    }
  77
  78    public static <T> ToolResult<T> failure(Failure error, Meta meta) {
  79        return new ToolResult<>(false, null, error, meta);
  80    }
  81
  82    public static <T> ToolResult<T> failure(ErrorCode code, String message, String remediation,
  83                                            Meta meta) {
  84        return failure(Failure.of(code, message, remediation), meta);
  85    }
  86}

   1{   2  "name": "brokerage_instruments_search",   3  "title": "Find a tradeable instrument by name or ticker",   4  "description": "Resolves what a customer said into candidate instruments, with the ticker, full legal name, exchange, type and sector of each. Use whenever the customer names a company rather than a ticker, when a ticker they gave does not look valid, or before any order where you are not certain which listing they mean. Do not use to get a price — that is brokerage_quotes_get — and do not use to find what the customer already owns, which is brokerage_positions_list and does not need a search at all. Read the candidates as a list to choose between, not an answer: when more than one is returned, or when exactMatch is false, name the alternatives and ask the customer which they mean. Several real cases need this. Apple is both AAPL and APLE, a hospitality trust. Alphabet trades as GOOGL and GOOG with different voting rights. Share classes carry a dot, as in BRK.B. Picking the first candidate silently is how the wrong company gets bought, and that error is not reversible once it fills.
