   1{   2  "name": "brokerage_quotes_get",   3  "title": "Get current quotes for up to ten symbols",   4  "description": "Returns the current two-sided market for each symbol given: last price, bid, ask, size, change on the day, volume, the spread in basis points, and the session the venue is in. Use when the customer asks what something is trading at, asks to compare instruments, or before explaining what an order would cost. Pass every symbol in one call rather than calling once per symbol. Do not use to look up a company by name — that is brokerage_instruments_search — and do not use it for past prices, which is brokerage_price_history_get. Read asOf before quoting a number to the customer: a quote is perishable and one taken minutes ago is not the market now. Read session too, and say so when it is not regular — in pre-market and after-hours the spread widens and the last price may be hours old. Read spreadBasisPoints before recommending a market order; above about 25 basis points the fill can be well away from the last price and a limit order is the better advice. This changes nothing and may be called freely.",   5  "inputSchema": {   6    "type": "object",   7    "properties": {   8      "symbols": {   9        "type": "array",  10        "minItems": 1,  11        "maxItems": 10,  12        "uniqueItems": true,  13        "description": "The tickers to quote, uppercase, exactly as returned by brokerage_instruments_search or brokerage_positions_list.",  14        "items": {  15          "type": "string",  16          "pattern": "^[A-Z]{1,5}(\\.[A-Z])?$",  17          "description": "One ticker."  18        }  19      }  20    },  21    "required": ["symbols"],  22    "additionalProperties": false  23  },  24  "outputSchema": {  25    "$defs": {  26      "decimal": {  27        "type": "string",  28        "pattern": "^-?[0-9]{1,15}(\\.[0-9]{1,6})?$",  29        "description": "A decimal number as a string, so that no amount is rounded by binary floating point on the way here."  30      }  31    },  32    "type": "object",  33    "properties": {  34      "session": {  35        "type": "string",  36        "enum": ["CLOSED", "PRE_MARKET", "REGULAR", "AFTER_HOURS"],  37        "description": "Which session the venue is in right now. Ask for the shortest window that answers the question. A year of daily bars is 250 rows and the model will read the first thirty; the summary already carries the range and the return.    1{   2  "name": "brokerage_balances_get",   3  "title": "Get the money in one account",   4  "description": "Returns the money view of one account: ledger cash, settled cash, cash reserved for working orders, buying power, market value of holdings, total equity, any margin loan, and the maintenance requirement and excess. Use when the customer asks what they have, what they can spend, whether they can afford something, or how much the account is worth. Do not use to decide whether a specific order would be accepted — brokerage_order_preview applies every rule to the actual ticket and is the only correct answer to that question. Read the right field for the question asked, because four of them are different numbers and the customer means a different one each time. buyingPower is what can be spent on a new purchase now. settledCash is what can be spent without risking a good-faith violation in a cash account. totalEquity is what the statement shows. cash is the ledger figure and is the one least likely to be what they meant. In a cash account, buyingPower never exceeds settledCash. Say which number you are quoting. This changes nothing and may be called freely.",   5  "inputSchema": {   6    "type": "object",   7    "properties": {   8      "accountId": {   9        "type": "string",  10        "pattern": "^acct_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{16}$",  11        "description": "The account to report on, from brokerage_accounts_list."  12      }  13    },  14    "required": ["accountId"],  15    "additionalProperties": false  16  },  17  "outputSchema": {  18    "$defs": {  19      "decimal": {  20        "type": "string",  21        "pattern": "^-?[0-9]{1,15}(\\.[0-9]{1,6})?$",  22        "description": "An amount as a decimal string, never a JSON number, so that no cent is lost to binary floating point."  23      }  24    },  25    "type": "object",  26    "properties": {  27      "accountId": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^acct_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{16}$", "description": "The account these figures are for." },  28      "currency": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[A-Z]{3}$", "description": "ISO 4217 currency for every amount here." },  29      "cash": { "$ref": "#/$defs/decimal", "description": "Ledger cash.    1{   2  "name": "brokerage_order_preview",   3  "title": "Price an order without placing it",   4  "description": "Computes exactly what would happen if an order were placed — estimated cost, commission, resulting buying power, every reason it would be refused and every condition the customer should know about — and places nothing. Use when the customer is considering an order, asks what something would cost, asks whether they can afford it, or has asked to trade and must see the terms before approving them. Every call to brokerage_order_place and brokerage_order_replace must be preceded by this tool, because it issues the confirmationToken those tools require and nothing else does. Do not use to report an existing order; that is brokerage_orders_list. Read canPlace first: false means the order would be refused, blockers says why, and the correct response is to tell the customer rather than to try again. Read maxPermissibleQuantity on a blocker when there is one, because it turns a dead end into a smaller order the customer can accept. Read warnings and say them out loud; they are conditions the customer may not want even though the order would go through. The confirmationToken is valid for 120 seconds and for this exact order only, so if anything changes, preview again. For a market order estimatedCost is an estimate from the current quote and the fill may differ, materially so when the spread is wide. Every argument here must match the preview character for character; the confirmationToken is bound to those terms and the order will be refused if anything differs, including the quantity, the price or the time in force. Do not use this to change an existing order, which is brokerage_order_replace, and do not use it to find out whether an order is possible, which is brokerage_order_preview. The effect is immediate and cannot be undone: a filled order can only be reversed by trading in the opposite direction, at whatever the market then is, and the customer bears that difference. Read status on the result: FILLED means it is done at averageFillPrice, WORKING means it is live and waiting, and REJECTED means nothing happened and rejectReason says why. brokerage-catalog/src/main/resources/prompts/conduct.md23 lines

   1You are a brokerage assistant for a retail customer of Example Securities. You have tools that   2read their accounts and, in some sessions, tools that can trade.   3   4How to behave:   5   6- Be exact about money. Quote the figure a tool returned, say which figure it is, and say when it   7  was taken. Never round a price or work out a total yourself.   8- Never act on an assumption about which account or which instrument the customer means. If more   9  than one fits, ask, naming the alternatives.  10- Before anything that trades, show the customer what it would cost and what it would leave them  11  with, and get a clear yes. "Go ahead" to a specific order is a yes; earlier enthusiasm is not.  12- Report what happened, not what you attempted. If a tool says an order is working rather than  13  filled, say working. If a cancellation did not take effect because the order filled first, say  14  that plainly, immediately, and before anything else.  15- You do not give investment advice, make recommendations, or offer opinions on whether something  16  is a good buy, a good price, or a good idea. You can explain what a figure means and what an  17  order would do. If asked whether to buy something, say that is not something you can advise on,  18  and offer the facts instead.  19- You do not give tax advice. You can read the customer their lots and holding periods and state  20  the general rule, and then say their own position is for them and their accountant.  21- You do not predict prices, and you do not characterize the market as likely to do anything.  22- If a tool refuses, read the refusal and tell the customer what it says. Do not look for another  23  tool that might not refuse.

F.4 The domain

brokerage-domain: a self-contained brokerage with deterministic market data, a risk engine, an order book and single-use confirmation tokens.

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;

   3import java.math.BigDecimal;

  14/**
  15 * Accounts and what is in them.
  16 *
  17 * <p>The demonstration book of business is deliberately awkward. One customer has four accounts,
  18 * two of which are retirement accounts where a short sale is impossible and a wash sale is
  19 * irrelevant; one is a cash account, where "buying power" means something different from the
  20 * margin account next to it; and one is restricted. An agent that was only ever shown a single
  21 * margin account will confidently do the wrong thing on three of the four, and the only way to
  22 * find that out before a customer does is to make the test data look like the real thing.
  23 */
  24@Component
  25public class Accounts {
  26
  27    /** What the account may do, which decides more rules than the balance does. */
  28    public enum AccountType {
  29        CASH("Cash", false, false),
  30        MARGIN("Margin", true, true),
  31        IRA_TRADITIONAL("Traditional IRA", false, false),
  32        ROTH_IRA("Roth IRA", false, false);
  33
  34        private final String label;
  35        private final boolean marginAllowed;
  36        private final boolean shortingAllowed;
  37
  38        AccountType(String label, boolean marginAllowed, boolean shortingAllowed) {
  39            this.label = label;
  40            this.marginAllowed = marginAllowed;
  41            this.shortingAllowed = shortingAllowed;
  42        }
  43
  44        public String label() {
  45            return label;
  46        }
  47
  48        public boolean marginAllowed() {
  49            return marginAllowed;
  50        }
  51
  52        public boolean shortingAllowed() {
  53            return shortingAllowed;
  54        }
  55
  56        public boolean retirement() {
  57            return this == IRA_TRADITIONAL || this == ROTH_IRA;
  58        }
  59    }
  60
  61    /** Why an account cannot trade, when it cannot. Null for a healthy account. */
  62    public enum Restriction {
  63        /** Awaiting a deposit to settle. Buys allowed up to settled cash only. */
  64        UNSETTLED_FUNDS,
  65        /** Flagged as a pattern day trader below the equity minimum. Closing orders only. */
  66        DAY_TRADE_RESTRICTED,
  67        /** Under review. Nothing may be placed. */
  68        FROZEN
  69    }
  70
  71    public record Account(String accountId, String nickname, AccountType type, String currency,
  72                          String customerId, LocalDate openedOn, Restriction restriction,
  73                          BigDecimal cash, BigDecimal settledCash, BigDecimal marginLoan,
  74                          int dayTradesUsed) {
  75
  76        public boolean tradeable() {
  77            return restriction != Restriction.FROZEN;
  78        }
  79    }
  80
  81    /**
  82     * The money view. Four numbers, and the reason there are four rather than one is that a
  83     * customer asking "how much do I have" means a different one each time: {@code cash} is what
  84     * the ledger says, {@code settledCash} is what may be spent today without a good-faith
  85     * violation, {@code buyingPower} is what may be spent on this instrument in this account, and
  86     * {@code totalEquity} is what the statement will show.
  87     */
  88    public record Balances(String accountId, String currency, BigDecimal cash,
  89                           BigDecimal settledCash, BigDecimal cashReservedForOrders,
  90                           BigDecimal buyingPower, BigDecimal marketValue, BigDecimal totalEquity,
  91                           BigDecimal marginLoan, BigDecimal maintenanceRequirement,
  92                           BigDecimal maintenanceExcess, int dayTradesUsed) {
  93    }
  94
  95    /** One holding, aggregated over its lots. */
  96    public record Position(String accountId, String symbol, String name, String sector,
  97                           long quantity, BigDecimal averageCost, BigDecimal lastPrice,
  98                           BigDecimal marketValue, BigDecimal unrealizedPnl,
  99                           BigDecimal unrealizedPnlPercent, BigDecimal portfolioWeight) {
 100    }
 101
 102    /**
 103     * One tax lot. This exists because "sell my Apple" is not one decision but two, and the second
 104     * one — which shares — is worth real money to the customer. An agent that can see lots can
 105     * ask the useful question; an agent that cannot will silently sell the oldest.
 106     */
 107    public record TaxLot(String lotId, String accountId, String symbol, long quantity,
 108                         BigDecimal costBasisPerShare, LocalDate acquiredOn, boolean longTerm,
 109                         BigDecimal unrealizedPnl, boolean washSaleRisk) {
 110    }
 111
 112    private final Map<String, Account> accounts = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 113    private final List<TaxLot> lots = new ArrayList<>();
 114    private final Instruments instruments;
 115    private final MarketData marketData;
 116    private final MarketClock clock;
 117
 118    public Accounts(Instruments instruments, MarketData marketData, MarketClock clock) {
 119        this.instruments = instruments;
 120        this.marketData = marketData;
 121        this.clock = clock;
 122        seed();
 123    }
 124
 125    public static final String DEMO_CUSTOMER = "cust_7QK3M8W2PR5NXVTZ";
 126
 127    private void seed() {
 128        String brokerage = add("Everyday brokerage", AccountType.MARGIN, "182430.55", "182430.55",
 129                "24000.00", null, 2);
 130        String cash = add("Cash account", AccountType.CASH, "15200.00", "9800.00", "0", null, 0);
 131        String roth = add("Roth IRA", AccountType.ROTH_IRA, "48110.12", "48110.12", "0", null, 0);
 132        add("Rollover IRA", AccountType.IRA_TRADITIONAL, "4300.00", "4300.00", "0",
 133                Restriction.FROZEN, 0);
 134
 135        lot(brokerage, "AAPL", 240, "148.22", LocalDate.of(2022, 3, 14), false);
 136        lot(brokerage, "AAPL", 60, "221.40", LocalDate.of(2026, 7, 2), true);
 137        lot(brokerage, "MSFT", 85, "398.10", LocalDate.of(2024, 1, 19), false);
 138        lot(brokerage, "NVDA", 400, "132.55", LocalDate.of(2025, 11, 7), false);
 139        lot(brokerage, "VOO", 150, "512.90", LocalDate.of(2023, 9, 1), false);
 140        lot(brokerage, "GME", 500, "28.90", LocalDate.of(2026, 8, 20), true);
 141        lot(cash, "SCHD", 300, "25.10", LocalDate.of(2025, 2, 11), false);
 142        lot(cash, "KO", 120, "63.44", LocalDate.of(2024, 6, 6), false);
 143        lot(roth, "VOO", 70, "440.15", LocalDate.of(2021, 4, 23), false);
 144        lot(roth, "QQQM", 180, "191.60", LocalDate.of(2024, 10, 30), false);
 145    }
 146
 147    private String add(String nickname, AccountType type, String cash, String settled,
 148                       String marginLoan, Restriction restriction, int dayTrades) {
 149        String id = Ids.account(accounts.size());
 150        accounts.put(id, new Account(id, nickname, type, Money.USD, DEMO_CUSTOMER,
 151                LocalDate.of(2019, 5, 2), restriction, Money.of(cash), Money.of(settled),
 152                Money.of(marginLoan), dayTrades));
 153        return id;
 154    }
 155
 156    private void lot(String accountId, String symbol, long quantity, String costBasis,
 157                     LocalDate acquiredOn, boolean washSaleRisk) {
 158        lots.add(new TaxLot(Ids.lot(lots.size()), accountId, symbol, quantity, Money.of(costBasis),
 159                acquiredOn, false, BigDecimal.ZERO, washSaleRisk));
 160    }
 161
 162    public List<Account> forCustomer(String customerId) {
 163        return accounts.values().stream().filter(a -> a.customerId().equals(customerId)).toList();
 164    }
 165
 166    public Optional<Account> find(String accountId) {
 167        return Optional.ofNullable(accounts.get(accountId));
 168    }
 169
 170    public void replace(Account account) {
 171        accounts.put(account.accountId(), account);
 172    }
 173
 174    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ derived views
 175
 176    public List<TaxLot> lotsOf(String accountId, String symbol) {
 177        LocalDate today = clock.now().atZone(MarketClock.EXCHANGE).toLocalDate();
 178        return lots.stream()
 179                .filter(lot -> lot.accountId().equals(accountId))
 180                .filter(lot -> symbol == null || lot.symbol().equals(symbol))
 181                .map(lot -> {
 182                    BigDecimal last = marketData.quote(lot.symbol()).last();
 183                    boolean longTerm = lot.acquiredOn().plusYears(1).isBefore(today);
 184                    BigDecimal pnl = last.subtract(lot.costBasisPerShare())
 185                            .multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(lot.quantity()));
 186                    return new TaxLot(lot.lotId(), lot.accountId(), lot.symbol(), lot.quantity(),
 187                            lot.costBasisPerShare(), lot.acquiredOn(), longTerm,
 188                            Money.cents(pnl), lot.washSaleRisk());
 189                })
 190                .toList();
 191    }
 192
 193    public List<Position> positionsOf(String accountId) {
 194        Map<String, List<TaxLot>> bySymbol = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 195        for (TaxLot lot : lotsOf(accountId, null)) {
 196            bySymbol.computeIfAbsent(lot.symbol(), ignored -> new ArrayList<>()).add(lot);
 197        }
 198        BigDecimal total = BigDecimal.ZERO;
 199        Map<String, BigDecimal> values = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 200        for (var entry : bySymbol.entrySet()) {
 201            BigDecimal last = marketData.quote(entry.getKey()).last();
 202            long quantity = entry.getValue().stream().mapToLong(TaxLot::quantity).sum();
 203            BigDecimal value = Money.times(last, quantity);
 204            values.put(entry.getKey(), value);
 205            total = total.add(value);
 206        }
 207        List<Position> positions = new ArrayList<>();
 208        for (var entry : bySymbol.entrySet()) {
 209            String symbol = entry.getKey();
 210            Instrument instrument = instruments.require(symbol);
 211            long quantity = entry.getValue().stream().mapToLong(TaxLot::quantity).sum();
 212            BigDecimal cost = entry.getValue().stream()
 213                    .map(lot -> Money.times(lot.costBasisPerShare(), lot.quantity()))
 214                    .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
 215            BigDecimal average = cost.divide(BigDecimal.valueOf(quantity), 4, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
 216            BigDecimal last = marketData.quote(symbol).last();
 217            BigDecimal value = values.get(symbol);
 218            BigDecimal pnl = value.subtract(cost);
 219            BigDecimal pnlPercent = cost.signum() == 0 ? BigDecimal.ZERO
 220                    : pnl.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(100)).divide(cost, 2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
 221            BigDecimal weight = total.signum() == 0 ? BigDecimal.ZERO
 222                    : value.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(100)).divide(total, 2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
 223            positions.add(new Position(accountId, symbol, instrument.name(), instrument.sector(),
 224                    quantity, average, last, Money.cents(value), Money.cents(pnl), pnlPercent,
 225                    weight));
 226        }
 227        return positions;
 228    }
 229
 230    public long sharesHeld(String accountId, String symbol) {
 231        return lotsOf(accountId, symbol).stream().mapToLong(TaxLot::quantity).sum();
 232    }
 233
 234    public Balances balancesOf(String accountId, BigDecimal reservedForOrders) {
 235        Account account = find(accountId).orElseThrow();
 236        BigDecimal marketValue = positionsOf(accountId).stream()
 237                .map(Position::marketValue).reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
 238        BigDecimal equity = account.cash().add(marketValue).subtract(account.marginLoan());
 239        BigDecimal maintenance = marketValue.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(0.25));
 240        BigDecimal buyingPower = account.type().marginAllowed()
 241                ? equity.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(2)).subtract(marketValue).max(BigDecimal.ZERO)
 242                : account.settledCash();
 243        if (account.restriction() == Restriction.UNSETTLED_FUNDS) {
 244            buyingPower = buyingPower.min(account.settledCash());
 245        }
 246        if (account.restriction() == Restriction.FROZEN) {
 247            buyingPower = BigDecimal.ZERO;
 248        }
 249        return new Balances(accountId, account.currency(), Money.cents(account.cash()),
 250                Money.cents(account.settledCash()), Money.cents(reservedForOrders),
 251                Money.cents(buyingPower.subtract(reservedForOrders).max(BigDecimal.ZERO)),
 252                Money.cents(marketValue), Money.cents(equity), Money.cents(account.marginLoan()),
 253                Money.cents(maintenance), Money.cents(equity.subtract(maintenance)),
 254                account.dayTradesUsed());
 255    }
 256}

   3import java.util.List;

   5import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

   7/**
   8 * One door into the domain, so that a tool handler depends on the brokerage rather than on seven
   9 * of its parts.
  10 *
  11 * <p>This is not an abstraction for its own sake. A handler is the one place in the system where
  12 * the firm's own correctness and a language model's improvisation meet, and it should be short
  13 * enough to read in one sitting. Every line a handler spends wiring domain services together is a
  14 * line nobody reviews carefully.
  15 */
  16@Component
  17public class Brokerage {
  18
  19    private final Accounts accounts;
  20    private final Instruments instruments;
  21    private final MarketData marketData;
  22    private final Orders orders;
  23    private final RiskEngine risk;
  24    private final ConfirmationTokens confirmations;
  25    private final MarketClock clock;

  27    public Brokerage(Accounts accounts, Instruments instruments, MarketData marketData,
  28                     Orders orders, RiskEngine risk, ConfirmationTokens confirmations,
  29                     MarketClock clock) {
  30        this.accounts = accounts;
  31        this.instruments = instruments;
  32        this.marketData = marketData;
  33        this.orders = orders;
  34        this.risk = risk;
  35        this.confirmations = confirmations;
  36        this.clock = clock;
  37        seedOrders();
  38    }
  39
  40    /** Put some working orders in the demonstration account, so the read tools have something to say. */
  41    private void seedOrders() {
  42        List<Accounts.Account> demo = accounts.forCustomer(Accounts.DEMO_CUSTOMER);
  43        if (!demo.isEmpty()) {
  44            orders.seed(demo.getFirst().accountId());
  45        }
  46    }
  47
  48    public Accounts accounts() {
  49        return accounts;
  50    }
  51
  52    public Instruments instruments() {

  54    }

  58    }
  59
  60    public Orders orders() {

  62    }

  66    }

  68    public ConfirmationTokens confirmations() {

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.time.Duration;
   4import java.time.Instant;
   5import java.util.Map;
   6import java.util.Optional;
   7import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
   8
   9import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  10
  11/**
  12 * Single-use tokens that bind an approval to one exact order.
  13 *
  14 * <p>This is the mechanism that turns "the agent should preview before it places" from a hope into
  15 * a fact. {@code brokerage_order_place} requires a token; only
  16 * {@code brokerage_order_preview} issues one; the token carries the fingerprint of the ticket it
  17 * was issued for; and it is spent on first use. An agent cannot place an order it has not priced,
  18 * cannot place a different order than the one the customer saw, and cannot place the same order
  19 * twice by retrying.
  20 *
  21 * <p>Compare the usual alternative, a {@code confirmed: true} parameter on the place tool. A
  22 * boolean the model sets is a boolean the model can set — it will be set, eventually, by a model
  23 * that has convinced itself the customer already agreed three turns ago. The token cannot be
  24 * guessed, cannot be reused, and expires, so the guarantee does not depend on the model's judgment.
  25 *
  26 * <p>The window is deliberately short. Two minutes is long enough for a customer to read a summary
  27 * and say yes, and short enough that the price they agreed to is still roughly the price they get.
  28 */
  29@Component
  30public class ConfirmationTokens {
  31
  32    public static final Duration DEFAULT_TTL = Duration.ofSeconds(120);
  33
  34    /**
  35     * @param fingerprint the ticket this token authorizes, exactly
  36     * @param issuedTo    the principal the preview was run for; another principal's token is no token
  37     */
  38    public record Issued(String token, String fingerprint, String issuedTo, Instant expiresAt) {
  39    }
  40
  41    /** Why a token was refused, in the words the error's remediation will use. */
  42    public enum Rejection {
  43        UNKNOWN("That confirmation token was not issued by this service."),
  44        EXPIRED("The confirmation has expired. Preview the order again to get a fresh one."),
  45        SPENT("That confirmation was already used to place an order. Preview again if the "
  46                + "customer wants a second one."),
  47        WRONG_PRINCIPAL("That confirmation was issued for a different session."),
  48        CHANGED("The order does not match the one that was confirmed. Preview the new terms and "
  49                + "have the customer approve them.");
  50
  51        private final String explanation;
  52
  53        Rejection(String explanation) {
  54            this.explanation = explanation;
  55        }
  56
  57        public String explanation() {
  58            return explanation;
  59        }
  60    }
  61
  62    public sealed interface Redemption {
  63        record Accepted(Issued issued) implements Redemption {
  64        }
  65
  66        record Refused(Rejection rejection) implements Redemption {
  67        }
  68    }
  69
  70    private final Map<String, Issued> live = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
  71    private final Map<String, Instant> spent = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
  72    private final MarketClock clock;
  73
  74    public ConfirmationTokens(MarketClock clock) {
  75        this.clock = clock;
  76    }
  77
  78    public Issued issue(Orders.Ticket ticket, String principal, Duration ttl) {
  79        Issued issued = new Issued(Ids.random("cnf_", 24), ticket.fingerprint(), principal,
  80                clock.now().plus(ttl));
  81        live.put(issued.token(), issued);
  82        return issued;
  83    }
  84
  85    public Issued issue(Orders.Ticket ticket, String principal) {
  86        return issue(ticket, principal, DEFAULT_TTL);
  87    }
  88
  89    /**
  90     * Spend a token for a ticket. Every refusal path returns a {@link Rejection} rather than
  91     * throwing, because each one is something the agent can act on and the customer can be told.
  92     */
  93    public Redemption redeem(String token, Orders.Ticket ticket, String principal) {
  94        if (token == null || token.isBlank()) {
  95            return new Redemption.Refused(Rejection.UNKNOWN);
  96        }
  97        if (spent.containsKey(token)) {
  98            return new Redemption.Refused(Rejection.SPENT);
  99        }
 100        Issued issued = live.get(token);
 101        if (issued == null) {
 102            return new Redemption.Refused(Rejection.UNKNOWN);
 103        }
 104        if (!issued.expiresAt().isAfter(clock.now())) {
 105            live.remove(token);
 106            return new Redemption.Refused(Rejection.EXPIRED);
 107        }
 108        if (!issued.issuedTo().equals(principal)) {
 109            return new Redemption.Refused(Rejection.WRONG_PRINCIPAL);
 110        }
 111        if (!issued.fingerprint().equals(ticket.fingerprint())) {
 112            return new Redemption.Refused(Rejection.CHANGED);
 113        }
 114        live.remove(token);
 115        spent.put(token, clock.now());
 116        return new Redemption.Accepted(issued);
 117    }
 118
 119    public Optional<Issued> peek(String token) {
 120        return Optional.ofNullable(live.get(token));
 121    }
 122
 123    public int outstanding() {
 124        return live.size();
 125    }
 126}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.security.SecureRandom;
   4
   5/**
   6 * Identifier minting. Three properties, each of which a model-facing identifier needs.
   7 *
   8 * <p>They are prefixed, so a misrouted identifier fails at the schema instead of in the handler:
   9 * {@code acct_} can never be mistaken for {@code ord_}, and the input schema's pattern says which
  10 * one a parameter wants. They use Crockford base32, which has no {@code I}, {@code L}, {@code O}
  11 * or {@code U}, so an identifier a customer reads aloud and an agent types back survives the round
  12 * trip. And they are opaque: nothing downstream may parse one for a date, a branch code or a
  13 * customer number, because the day somebody does is the day the format can never change.
  14 *
  15 * <p>The seeded identifiers are derived from an index rather than from a counter, and that detail
  16 * matters more than it looks. A counter advances with every object ever created in the process, so
  17 * the demonstration customer's first account would have a different identifier in the second test
  18 * of a run than in the first. Deriving from the index means the four demonstration accounts have
  19 * the same four identifiers on every machine, in every test, and in every figure printed in the
  20 * book — which is what makes a recorded evaluation cassette replayable at all.
  21 */
  22public final class Ids {
  23
  24    private static final String ALPHABET = "0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ";
  25    private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom();
  26
  27    private Ids() {
  28    }
  29
  30    /** A genuinely random identifier, for anything created while the service is running. */
  31    public static String random(String prefix, int length) {
  32        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder(prefix);
  33        for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
  34            out.append(ALPHABET.charAt(RANDOM.nextInt(ALPHABET.length())));
  35        }
  36        return out.toString();
  37    }
  38
  39    /**
  40     * A repeatable identifier for the seeded book of business. Derived from the kind and the index
  41     * only, so it is stable across runs, machines and JVM restarts.
  42     */
  43    public static String seeded(String prefix, int index, int length) {
  44        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder(prefix);
  45        long seed = (prefix.hashCode() * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15L) ^ ((index + 1L) * 0x165667B19E3779F9L);
  46        for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
  47            long mixed = seed ^ ((i + 1L) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9L);
  48            mixed ^= mixed >>> 29;
  49            mixed *= 0x94D049BB133111EBL;
  50            mixed ^= mixed >>> 32;
  51            out.append(ALPHABET.charAt((int) Math.floorMod(mixed, 32L)));
  52        }
  53        return out.toString();
  54    }
  55
  56    public static String account(int index) {
  57        return seeded("acct_", index, 16);
  58    }
  59
  60    public static String lot(int index) {
  61        return seeded("lot_", index, 12);
  62    }
  63
  64    /** A seeded order, for the working orders the demonstration account starts with. */
  65    public static String seededOrder(int index) {
  66        return seeded("ord_", index, 16);
  67    }
  68
  69    public static String order() {
  70        return random("ord_", 16);
  71    }
  72
  73    public static String execution() {
  74        return random("exec_", 16);
  75    }
  76}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.util.Comparator;
   4import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
   5import java.util.List;
   6import java.util.Locale;
   7import java.util.Map;
   8import java.util.Optional;
   9
  10import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  11
  12/**
  13 * The instrument master, small enough to read and large enough to be ambiguous on purpose.
  14 *
  15 * <p>Several entries exist only to make the agent behave correctly. {@code APLE} and {@code AAPL}
  16 * are both real tickers and both match the word "apple", which is the case that separates an agent
  17 * that asks from an agent that guesses. {@code GOOGL} and {@code GOOG} are the same company with
  18 * different voting rights, so "buy Google" has no single right answer. And {@code BRK.B} has a
  19 * dot in it, which is how you find out whether a tool's symbol pattern was written from the
  20 * specification or from the first five symbols the author happened to try.
  21 */
  22@Component
  23public class Instruments {
  24
  25    private final Map<String, Instrument> bySymbol = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  26
  27    public Instruments() {
  28        add("AAPL", "Apple Inc.", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Information Technology",
  29                "234.50", true, true);
  30        add("APLE", "Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc.", "NYSE", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Real Estate",
  31                "13.82", true, false);
  32        add("MSFT", "Microsoft Corporation", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.EQUITY,
  33                "Information Technology", "512.18", true, true);
  34        add("GOOGL", "Alphabet Inc. Class A", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.EQUITY,
  35                "Communication Services", "248.90", true, true);
  36        add("GOOG", "Alphabet Inc. Class C", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.EQUITY,
  37                "Communication Services", "250.11", true, true);
  38        add("AMZN", "Amazon.com, Inc.", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Consumer Discretionary",
  39                "231.44", true, true);
  40        add("NVDA", "NVIDIA Corporation", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.EQUITY,
  41                "Information Technology", "184.62", true, true);
  42        add("TSLA", "Tesla, Inc.", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Consumer Discretionary",
  43                "412.07", true, true);
  44        add("JPM", "JPMorgan Chase & Co.", "NYSE", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Financials",
  45                "312.55", true, false);
  46        add("KO", "The Coca-Cola Company", "NYSE", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Consumer Staples",
  47                "71.20", true, false);
  48        add("XOM", "Exxon Mobil Corporation", "NYSE", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Energy",
  49                "118.73", true, false);
  50        add("BRK.B", "Berkshire Hathaway Inc. Class B", "NYSE", Instrument.Type.EQUITY,
  51                "Financials", "498.30", true, false);
  52        add("VOO", "Vanguard S&P 500 ETF", "NYSEARCA", Instrument.Type.ETF, "Broad Market",
  53                "604.15", true, true);
  54        add("QQQM", "Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF", "NASDAQ", Instrument.Type.ETF, "Broad Market",
  55                "248.03", true, true);
  56        add("SCHD", "Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF", "NYSEARCA", Instrument.Type.ETF, "Dividend",
  57                "27.94", true, true);
  58        add("GME", "GameStop Corp.", "NYSE", Instrument.Type.EQUITY, "Consumer Discretionary",
  59                "22.41", false, false);
  60        add("TSM", "Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ADR", "NYSE", Instrument.Type.ADR,
  61                "Information Technology", "288.60", true, false);
  62    }
  63
  64    private void add(String symbol, String name, String exchange, Instrument.Type type,
  65                     String sector, String price, boolean marginEligible, boolean fractionable) {
  66        bySymbol.put(symbol, new Instrument(symbol, name, exchange, type, sector,
  67                Money.of(price), marginEligible, fractionable));
  68    }
  69
  70    public Optional<Instrument> find(String symbol) {
  71        return Optional.ofNullable(bySymbol.get(symbol == null ? "" : symbol.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)));
  72    }
  73
  74    public Instrument require(String symbol) {
  75        return find(symbol).orElseThrow(() ->
  76                new IllegalArgumentException("no instrument " + symbol));
  77    }
  78
  79    public List<Instrument> all() {
  80        return List.copyOf(bySymbol.values());
  81    }
  82
  83    /**
  84     * Candidates for a free-text query, best first. The score is deliberately crude — an exact
  85     * ticker beats a name prefix, which beats a name containing the words — because the tool's job
  86     * is not to pick but to hand the agent a short list with enough on each row to ask a sensible
  87     * question.
  88     */
  89    public List<Instrument> search(String query, int limit) {
  90        String q = query == null ? "" : query.trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
  91        if (q.isEmpty()) {
  92            return List.of();
  93        }
  94        return bySymbol.values().stream()
  95                .map(instrument -> Map.entry(instrument, score(instrument, q)))
  96                .filter(entry -> entry.getValue() > 0)
  97                .sorted(Comparator.<Map.Entry<Instrument, Integer>>comparingInt(Map.Entry::getValue)
  98                        .reversed()
  99                        .thenComparing(entry -> entry.getKey().symbol()))
 100                .limit(limit)
 101                .map(Map.Entry::getKey)
 102                .toList();
 103    }
 104
 105    private static int score(Instrument instrument, String query) {
 106        String name = instrument.name().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
 107        if (instrument.symbol().equals(query)) {
 108            return 100;
 109        }
 110        if (name.startsWith(query)) {
 111            return 60;
 112        }
 113        if (instrument.symbol().startsWith(query)) {
 114            return 50;
 115        }
 116        if (name.contains(query)) {
 117            return 40;
 118        }
 119        String firstWord = query.split("\\s+")[0];
 120        return firstWord.length() >= 3 && name.contains(firstWord) ? 20 : 0;
 121    }
 122}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.time.DayOfWeek;
   4import java.time.Duration;
   5import java.time.Instant;
   6import java.time.LocalTime;
   7import java.time.ZoneId;
   8import java.time.ZonedDateTime;
   9
  10import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  11
  12/**
  13 * What time it is, as a trading venue understands the question.
  14 *
  15 * <p>The clock is a component rather than a static call because "is the market open" is the single
  16 * most common reason a correct-looking order is refused, and a test that cannot move the clock
  17 * cannot cover that path. Every tool that asks about the session asks here.
  18 */
  19@Component
  20public class MarketClock {
  21
  22    public static final ZoneId EXCHANGE = ZoneId.of("America/New_York");
  23    private static final LocalTime PREMARKET_OPEN = LocalTime.of(4, 0);
  24    private static final LocalTime REGULAR_OPEN = LocalTime.of(9, 30);
  25    private static final LocalTime REGULAR_CLOSE = LocalTime.of(16, 0);
  26    private static final LocalTime AFTERHOURS_CLOSE = LocalTime.of(20, 0);
  27
  28    /** Which session the venue is in. The model is told this in words, never left to infer it. */
  29    public enum Session {
  30        CLOSED("closed"),
  31        PRE_MARKET("pre-market"),
  32        REGULAR("regular"),
  33        AFTER_HOURS("after-hours");
  34
  35        private final String label;
  36
  37        Session(String label) {
  38            this.label = label;
  39        }
  40
  41        public String label() {
  42            return label;
  43        }
  44
  45        public boolean tradeable() {
  46            return this != CLOSED;
  47        }
  48    }
  49
  50    private Instant now = Instant.parse("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z");
  51
  52    /** Freeze the clock. Used by the seeded demonstration and by every test that cares. */
  53    public void set(Instant instant) {
  54        this.now = instant;
  55    }
  56
  57    public void advance(Duration amount) {
  58        this.now = now.plus(amount);
  59    }
  60
  61    public Instant now() {
  62        return now;
  63    }
  64
  65    public Session session() {
  66        ZonedDateTime local = now.atZone(EXCHANGE);
  67        if (local.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY || local.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY) {
  68            return Session.CLOSED;
  69        }
  70        LocalTime time = local.toLocalTime();
  71        if (time.isBefore(PREMARKET_OPEN) || !time.isBefore(AFTERHOURS_CLOSE)) {
  72            return Session.CLOSED;
  73        }
  74        if (time.isBefore(REGULAR_OPEN)) {
  75            return Session.PRE_MARKET;
  76        }
  77        return time.isBefore(REGULAR_CLOSE) ? Session.REGULAR : Session.AFTER_HOURS;
  78    }
  79
  80    /**
  81     * When the regular session next opens, in words a model can relay. "The market is closed" is
  82     * half an answer; a customer wants to know whether to wait twenty minutes or until Monday.
  83     */
  84    public Instant nextRegularOpen() {
  85        ZonedDateTime local = now.atZone(EXCHANGE);
  86        ZonedDateTime candidate = local.with(REGULAR_OPEN);
  87        if (!candidate.toInstant().isAfter(now)) {
  88            candidate = candidate.plusDays(1);
  89        }
  90        while (candidate.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY
  91                || candidate.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY) {
  92            candidate = candidate.plusDays(1);
  93        }
  94        return candidate.toInstant();
  95    }
  96}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.math.BigDecimal;
   4import java.math.RoundingMode;
   5import java.time.Duration;
   6import java.time.Instant;
   7import java.time.LocalDate;
   8import java.util.ArrayList;
   9import java.util.List;
  10
  11import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  12
  13/**
  14 * Quotes and bars, generated deterministically.
  15 *
  16 * <p>Determinism is not laziness here, it is the point. The book prints quotes, the test harness
  17 * asserts on them, and the evaluation suite compares one run of an agent against another. If the
  18 * price moved because a random number generator felt like it, none of those three would be
  19 * readable. Every figure comes from a hash of the symbol and the day, so the same symbol on the
  20 * same day is the same price on every machine, and moving the clock moves the price.
  21 */
  22@Component
  23public class MarketData {
  24
  25    private final Instruments instruments;
  26    private final MarketClock clock;
  27
  28    public MarketData(Instruments instruments, MarketClock clock) {
  29        this.instruments = instruments;
  30        this.clock = clock;
  31    }
  32
  33    /**
  34     * A two-sided quote. {@code spreadBasisPoints} is carried explicitly because a wide spread is
  35     * the most common reason a market order fills somewhere the customer did not expect, and the
  36     * agent should be able to warn about it without doing arithmetic.
  37     */
  38    public record Quote(String symbol, BigDecimal last, BigDecimal bid, BigDecimal ask,
  39                        long bidSize, long askSize, BigDecimal previousClose, BigDecimal change,
  40                        BigDecimal changePercent, long volume, int spreadBasisPoints,
  41                        Instant asOf, MarketClock.Session session) {
  42    }
  43
  44    /** One OHLCV bar. */
  45    public record Bar(LocalDate date, BigDecimal open, BigDecimal high, BigDecimal low,
  46                      BigDecimal close, long volume) {
  47    }
  48
  49    public Quote quote(String symbol) {
  50        Instrument instrument = instruments.require(symbol);
  51        Instant now = clock.now();
  52        BigDecimal previousClose = priceOn(instrument, now.minus(Duration.ofDays(1)));
  53        BigDecimal last = priceOn(instrument, now);
  54        int spread = spreadBasisPoints(instrument);
  55        BigDecimal half = last.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(spread))
  56                .divide(BigDecimal.valueOf(20_000), 4, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
  57        BigDecimal change = last.subtract(previousClose);
  58        BigDecimal changePercent = previousClose.signum() == 0 ? BigDecimal.ZERO
  59                : change.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(100))
  60                        .divide(previousClose, 2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
  61        long volume = 250_000L + Math.abs(hash(instrument.symbol(), now, 7)) % 40_000_000L;
  62        return new Quote(instrument.symbol(), last, last.subtract(half), last.add(half),
  63                roundLot(instrument, now, 1), roundLot(instrument, now, 2), previousClose,
  64                change, changePercent, volume, spread, now, clock.session());
  65    }
  66
  67    /**
  68     * Daily bars, newest last. The series is generated from the same hash as the quote, so the
  69     * last bar's close and the current quote agree — a small consistency that an agent reading
  70     * both in one turn will otherwise notice and comment on.
  71     */
  72    public List<Bar> history(String symbol, int days) {
  73        Instrument instrument = instruments.require(symbol);
  74        List<Bar> bars = new ArrayList<>();
  75        LocalDate today = clock.now().atZone(MarketClock.EXCHANGE).toLocalDate();
  76        for (int back = days - 1; back >= 0; back--) {
  77            LocalDate date = today.minusDays(back);
  78            if (date.getDayOfWeek().getValue() > 5) {
  79                continue;
  80            }
  81            Instant at = date.atStartOfDay(MarketClock.EXCHANGE).toInstant();
  82            BigDecimal close = priceOn(instrument, at);
  83            BigDecimal open = priceOn(instrument, at.minus(Duration.ofDays(1)));
  84            BigDecimal swing = close.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(
  85                    Math.abs(hash(instrument.symbol(), at, 3)) % 15 + 2))
  86                    .divide(BigDecimal.valueOf(1000), 2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
  87            BigDecimal high = close.max(open).add(swing);
  88            BigDecimal low = close.min(open).subtract(swing).max(BigDecimal.valueOf(0.01));
  89            long volume = 100_000L + Math.abs(hash(instrument.symbol(), at, 11)) % 20_000_000L;
  90            bars.add(new Bar(date, Money.cents(open), Money.cents(high), Money.cents(low),
  91                    Money.cents(close), volume));
  92        }
  93        return bars;
  94    }
  95
  96    /**
  97     * The price of an instrument on a given day.
  98     *
  99     * <p>Two properties are required of this function and neither is obvious until it is got
 100     * wrong. It has to be <em>bounded</em>, because an unbounded walk eventually produces a
 101     * negative price and the first person to find that will be a reader following the book's
 102     * examples. And consecutive days have to be <em>close together</em>, because the day-over-day
 103     * change is published in every quote: draw each day independently from a wide band and the
 104     * demonstration account shows a blue chip down sixteen percent, which makes every figure in
 105     * the book look like a bug.
 106     *
 107     * <p>So the shape is a slow trend, phased per symbol so instruments do not move in lockstep,
 108     * plus a bounded daily jitter of at most eight tenths of a percent. The worst day-over-day
 109     * move that can come out of it is under two percent, which is a believable day.
 110     */
 111    private BigDecimal priceOn(Instrument instrument, Instant at) {
 112        long day = at.atZone(MarketClock.EXCHANGE).toLocalDate().toEpochDay();
 113        double phase = (Math.abs(instrument.symbol().hashCode()) % 360) * Math.PI / 180.0;
 114        double trend = Math.sin(day / 180.0 + phase) * 0.09 + Math.sin(day / 41.0 + phase) * 0.025;
 115        double jitter = (Math.floorMod(hash(instrument.symbol(), at, 1), 161L) - 80) / 10_000.0;
 116        BigDecimal factor = BigDecimal.valueOf(1 + trend + jitter)
 117                .setScale(6, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
 118        return Money.cents(instrument.basePrice().multiply(factor));
 119    }
 120
 121    private int spreadBasisPoints(Instrument instrument) {
 122        int base = switch (instrument.type()) {
 123            case ETF -> 2;
 124            case EQUITY -> instrument.basePrice().compareTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(50)) < 0 ? 12 : 4;
 125            case ADR -> 8;
 126        };
 127        return clock.session() == MarketClock.Session.REGULAR ? base : base * 6;
 128    }
 129
 130    private long roundLot(Instrument instrument, Instant at, int salt) {
 131        return 100L * (1 + Math.abs(hash(instrument.symbol(), at, salt)) % 40);
 132    }
 133
 134    private static long hash(String symbol, Instant at, int salt) {
 135        long day = at.atZone(MarketClock.EXCHANGE).toLocalDate().toEpochDay();
 136        long mixed = (symbol.hashCode() * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15L) ^ (day * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9L)
 137                ^ (salt * 0x94D049BB133111EBL);
 138        mixed ^= mixed >>> 31;
 139        mixed *= 0xD6E8FEB86659FD93L;
 140        mixed ^= mixed >>> 32;
 141        return mixed % 10_000_019L;
 142    }
 143}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.math.BigDecimal;
   4import java.math.RoundingMode;
   5
   6/**
   7 * Money, as the only two representations a brokerage may use: {@link BigDecimal} inside the
   8 * process and a decimal <em>string</em> at every boundary.
   9 *
  10 * <p>There is no third option. A JSON number for money is a defect waiting for a volume large
  11 * enough to show it: IEEE-754 binary doubles cannot represent 0.1, so a thousand-share order at
  12 * $10.10 can total $10099.999999999998, and the model will dutifully read that back to a
  13 * customer. Every amount this domain hands to a tool goes through {@link #string}.
  14 */
  15public final class Money {
  16
  17    public static final int SCALE = 2;
  18    public static final String USD = "USD";
  19
  20    private Money() {
  21    }
  22
  23    public static BigDecimal of(String amount) {
  24        return new BigDecimal(amount);
  25    }
  26
  27    public static BigDecimal of(double amount) {
  28        return BigDecimal.valueOf(amount).setScale(SCALE, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
  29    }
  30
  31    /** Round half-up to cents, the convention a customer statement uses. */
  32    public static BigDecimal cents(BigDecimal amount) {
  33        return amount.setScale(SCALE, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
  34    }
  35
  36    /** The wire form: a plain decimal string, never scientific notation, never a float. */
  37    public static String string(BigDecimal amount) {
  38        return cents(amount).toPlainString();
  39    }
  40
  41    /** The wire form at a wider scale, for per-share prices quoted in sub-cents. */
  42    public static String price(BigDecimal amount) {
  43        return amount.setScale(4, RoundingMode.HALF_UP).stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString();
  44    }
  45
  46    public static BigDecimal times(BigDecimal amount, long quantity) {
  47        return amount.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(quantity));
  48    }
  49}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.math.BigDecimal;
   4import java.time.Instant;
   5import java.time.LocalDate;
   6import java.util.ArrayList;
   7import java.util.Comparator;
   8import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
   9import java.util.List;
  10import java.util.Map;
  11import java.util.Optional;
  12
  13import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  14
  15/**
  16 * The order book: tickets, orders, state transitions and fills.
  17 *
  18 * <p>Two things in here exist only because an agent is the caller.
  19 *
  20 * <p>The first is the idempotency store. An agent retries. It retries because a socket closed,
  21 * because a runtime timed out, because the model decided the first answer looked incomplete. A
  22 * REST API that double-books an order under retry is a bug; a tool that double-books one is a
  23 * customer complaint and a regulatory finding. So {@link #place} is keyed, and a repeat of the
  24 * same key returns the original order rather than a second one.
  25 *
  26 * <p>The second is that cancellation is a <em>request</em>, not a result. A working order may fill
  27 * in the moment between the agent deciding to cancel it and the venue hearing about it, and an
  28 * agent told "cancelled" when the order actually filled will tell the customer something false.
  29 * {@link #cancel} returns the order's real state and says whether the request was accepted.
  30 */
  31@Component
  32public class Orders {
  33
  34    public enum Side { BUY, SELL, SELL_SHORT, BUY_TO_COVER }
  35
  36    public enum OrderType { MARKET, LIMIT, STOP, STOP_LIMIT }
  37
  38    public enum TimeInForce { DAY, GTC, IOC, FOK }
  39
  40    /**
  41     * Order status. {@code CANCELLED} keeps its double-L spelling because that is how it is
  42     * written in the systems of record this book's domain borrows from, and an enumeration member
  43     * is a name rather than prose: renaming it to match the surrounding US English would break
  44     * every consumer that already matches on the string.
  45     */
  46    public enum Status {
  47        PENDING_NEW, WORKING, PARTIALLY_FILLED, FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, EXPIRED;
  48
  49        public boolean working() {
  50            return this == PENDING_NEW || this == WORKING || this == PARTIALLY_FILLED;
  51        }
  52
  53        public boolean terminal() {
  54            return !working();
  55        }
  56    }
  57
  58    /** What the customer asked for. Separate from the order so a preview can exist without one. */
  59    public record Ticket(String accountId, String symbol, Side side, long quantity,
  60                         OrderType orderType, BigDecimal limitPrice, BigDecimal stopPrice,
  61                         TimeInForce timeInForce, boolean extendedHours) {
  62
  63        /** The fingerprint a confirmation token is bound to. Change anything, preview again. */
  64        public String fingerprint() {
  65            return String.join("|", accountId, symbol, side.name(), String.valueOf(quantity),
  66                    orderType.name(), String.valueOf(limitPrice), String.valueOf(stopPrice),
  67                    timeInForce.name(), String.valueOf(extendedHours));
  68        }
  69
  70        public String describe() {
  71            String price = switch (orderType) {
  72                case MARKET -> "at market";
  73                case LIMIT -> "limit " + Money.price(limitPrice);
  74                case STOP -> "stop " + Money.price(stopPrice);
  75                case STOP_LIMIT -> "stop " + Money.price(stopPrice)
  76                        + " limit " + Money.price(limitPrice);
  77            };
  78            return "%s %d %s %s, %s".formatted(side, quantity, symbol, price, timeInForce);
  79        }
  80    }
  81
  82    public record Order(String orderId, String accountId, String symbol, Side side, long quantity,
  83                        long filledQuantity, OrderType orderType, BigDecimal limitPrice,
  84                        BigDecimal stopPrice, TimeInForce timeInForce, Status status,
  85                        BigDecimal averageFillPrice, BigDecimal commission, String rejectReason,
  86                        Instant placedAt, Instant updatedAt, String idempotencyKey) {
  87
  88        public long remainingQuantity() {
  89            return quantity - filledQuantity;
  90        }
  91    }
  92
  93    public record Execution(String executionId, String orderId, String accountId, String symbol,
  94                            Side side, long quantity, BigDecimal price, BigDecimal commission,
  95                            Instant executedAt, LocalDate settlesOn, String venue) {
  96    }
  97
  98    /** The outcome of a cancellation request, which is not the same thing as a cancellation. */
  99    public record CancelOutcome(boolean accepted, Order order, String explanation) {
 100    }
 101
 102    private final Map<String, Order> orders = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 103    private final List<Execution> executions = new ArrayList<>();
 104    private final Map<String, String> byIdempotencyKey = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 105    private final MarketClock clock;
 106    private final MarketData marketData;
 107
 108    public Orders(MarketClock clock, MarketData marketData) {
 109        this.clock = clock;
 110        this.marketData = marketData;
 111    }
 112
 113    public void seed(String accountId) {
 114        Instant now = clock.now();
 115        record(new Order(Ids.seededOrder(0), accountId, "MSFT", Side.BUY, 25, 0, OrderType.LIMIT,
 116                Money.of("495.00"), null, TimeInForce.GTC, Status.WORKING, null,
 117                Money.of("0.00"), null, now.minusSeconds(7200), now.minusSeconds(7200), null));
 118        record(new Order(Ids.seededOrder(1), accountId, "TSLA", Side.BUY, 10, 4, OrderType.LIMIT,
 119                Money.of("405.00"), null, TimeInForce.DAY, Status.PARTIALLY_FILLED,
 120                Money.of("404.88"), Money.of("0.00"), null, now.minusSeconds(3600),
 121                now.minusSeconds(900), null));
 122        Order filled = new Order(Ids.seededOrder(2), accountId, "NVDA", Side.BUY, 100, 100,
 123                OrderType.MARKET, null, null, TimeInForce.DAY, Status.FILLED,
 124                Money.of("181.44"), Money.of("0.00"), null, now.minusSeconds(86_400),
 125                now.minusSeconds(86_300), null);
 126        record(filled);
 127        executions.add(new Execution(Ids.seeded("exec_", 0, 16), filled.orderId(), accountId, "NVDA",
 128                Side.BUY, 100, Money.of("181.44"), Money.of("0.00"), now.minusSeconds(86_300),
 129                settlement(now.minusSeconds(86_300)), "NASDAQ"));
 130    }
 131
 132    private void record(Order order) {
 133        orders.put(order.orderId(), order);
 134    }
 135
 136    public Optional<Order> find(String orderId) {
 137        return Optional.ofNullable(orders.get(orderId));
 138    }
 139
 140    /**
 141     * The order a given idempotency key already produced, if any. This is what lets a retried
 142     * place be answered with "here is your order" instead of "that token is spent".
 143     */
 144    public Optional<Order> byIdempotencyKey(String key) {
 145        return Optional.ofNullable(byIdempotencyKey.get(key)).map(orders::get);
 146    }
 147
 148    public List<Order> of(String accountId, java.util.function.Predicate<Order> filter) {
 149        return orders.values().stream()
 150                .filter(order -> order.accountId().equals(accountId))
 151                .filter(filter)
 152                .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Order::placedAt).reversed())
 153                .toList();
 154    }
 155
 156    public List<Execution> executionsOf(String accountId, String symbol, Instant since) {
 157        return executions.stream()
 158                .filter(execution -> execution.accountId().equals(accountId))
 159                .filter(execution -> symbol == null || execution.symbol().equals(symbol))
 160                .filter(execution -> since == null || !execution.executedAt().isBefore(since))
 161                .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Execution::executedAt).reversed())
 162                .toList();
 163    }
 164
 165    public BigDecimal cashReservedFor(String accountId) {
 166        return of(accountId, order -> order.status().working()).stream()
 167                .filter(order -> order.side() == Side.BUY)
 168                .map(order -> Money.times(
 169                        order.limitPrice() != null ? order.limitPrice()
 170                                : marketData.quote(order.symbol()).ask(),
 171                        order.remainingQuantity()))
 172                .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
 173    }
 174
 175    /**
 176     * Place an order, once per idempotency key. The key is minted by the runtime from the
 177     * confirmation token, never by the model: a model asked to supply a unique key will
 178     * occasionally supply the same one twice, or a different one on a retry, and either way the
 179     * guarantee is gone.
 180     */
 181    public Order place(Ticket ticket, String idempotencyKey) {
 182        String existing = byIdempotencyKey.get(idempotencyKey);
 183        if (existing != null) {
 184            return orders.get(existing);
 185        }
 186        Instant now = clock.now();
 187        boolean fillsNow = ticket.orderType() == OrderType.MARKET
 188                && clock.session() == MarketClock.Session.REGULAR;
 189        String orderId = Ids.order();
 190        Order order;
 191        if (fillsNow) {
 192            MarketData.Quote quote = marketData.quote(ticket.symbol());
 193            BigDecimal fill = ticket.side() == Side.BUY || ticket.side() == Side.BUY_TO_COVER
 194                    ? quote.ask() : quote.bid();
 195            order = new Order(orderId, ticket.accountId(), ticket.symbol(), ticket.side(),
 196                    ticket.quantity(), ticket.quantity(), ticket.orderType(), ticket.limitPrice(),
 197                    ticket.stopPrice(), ticket.timeInForce(), Status.FILLED, Money.cents(fill),
 198                    Money.of("0.00"), null, now, now, idempotencyKey);
 199            executions.add(new Execution(Ids.execution(), orderId, ticket.accountId(),
 200                    ticket.symbol(), ticket.side(), ticket.quantity(), Money.cents(fill),
 201                    Money.of("0.00"), now, settlement(now), "NASDAQ"));
 202        } else {
 203            order = new Order(orderId, ticket.accountId(), ticket.symbol(), ticket.side(),
 204                    ticket.quantity(), 0, ticket.orderType(), ticket.limitPrice(),
 205                    ticket.stopPrice(), ticket.timeInForce(), Status.WORKING, null,
 206                    Money.of("0.00"), null, now, now, idempotencyKey);
 207        }
 208        record(order);
 209        byIdempotencyKey.put(idempotencyKey, orderId);
 210        return order;
 211    }
 212
 213    /**
 214     * Replace a working order. The replacement keeps the original identifier, because a customer
 215     * who was told "order ord_X is in" and then hears about ord_Y has lost the thread, and an
 216     * agent asked to "move my limit up a dollar" has no business creating a second order.
 217     */
 218    public Optional<Order> replace(String orderId, long quantity, BigDecimal limitPrice,
 219                                   BigDecimal stopPrice) {
 220        Order order = orders.get(orderId);
 221        if (order == null || order.status().terminal()) {
 222            return Optional.empty();
 223        }
 224        Order updated = new Order(order.orderId(), order.accountId(), order.symbol(), order.side(),
 225                quantity, order.filledQuantity(), order.orderType(), limitPrice, stopPrice,
 226                order.timeInForce(), order.status(), order.averageFillPrice(), order.commission(),
 227                null, order.placedAt(), clock.now(), order.idempotencyKey());
 228        record(updated);
 229        return Optional.of(updated);
 230    }
 231
 232    public CancelOutcome cancel(String orderId) {
 233        Order order = orders.get(orderId);
 234        if (order == null) {
 235            return new CancelOutcome(false, null, "No such order.");
 236        }
 237        if (order.status() == Status.FILLED) {
 238            return new CancelOutcome(false, order,
 239                    "The order filled in full before the cancellation reached the venue, so there "
 240                            + "is nothing to cancel. The customer now owns the shares.");
 241        }
 242        if (order.status().terminal()) {
 243            return new CancelOutcome(false, order,
 244                    "The order was already " + order.status() + "; no action was taken.");
 245        }
 246        Order cancelled = new Order(order.orderId(), order.accountId(), order.symbol(),
 247                order.side(), order.quantity(), order.filledQuantity(), order.orderType(),
 248                order.limitPrice(), order.stopPrice(), order.timeInForce(), Status.CANCELLED,
 249                order.averageFillPrice(), order.commission(), null, order.placedAt(), clock.now(),
 250                order.idempotencyKey());
 251        record(cancelled);
 252        String partial = order.filledQuantity() > 0
 253                ? " " + order.filledQuantity() + " of " + order.quantity()
 254                        + " shares had already filled and those remain."
 255                : "";
 256        return new CancelOutcome(true, cancelled, "Cancellation accepted." + partial);
 257    }
 258
 259    /** T+1, the convention since 2024. Weekend-aware, because settlement dates are quoted. */
 260    private static LocalDate settlement(Instant executedAt) {
 261        LocalDate date = executedAt.atZone(MarketClock.EXCHANGE).toLocalDate().plusDays(1);
 262        while (date.getDayOfWeek().getValue() > 5) {
 263            date = date.plusDays(1);
 264        }
 265        return date;
 266    }
 267}
