  12import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolHandler;
  13
  14import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  15
  16/**
  17 * {@code brokerage_positions_list}.
  18 *
  19 * <p>Sorted by market value, largest first, which is not a cosmetic choice. A model reads a list
  20 * from the top and a long list from the top only; putting the largest holdings first means that
  21 * whatever gets dropped from a truncated answer is the part that mattered least. Ordering a result
  22 * is the cheapest form of prioritization a tool has.
  23 */
  24@Component
  25public class PositionsListHandler implements ToolHandler {
  26
  27    record PositionView(String symbol, String name, String sector, long quantity,
  28                        String averageCost, String lastPrice, String marketValue,
  29                        String unrealizedPnl, String unrealizedPnlPercent,
  30                        String portfolioWeight) {
  31    }
  32
  33    record Payload(String accountId, String currency, String totalMarketValue,
  34                   List<PositionView> positions, Instant asOf) {
  35    }
  36
  37    private final Brokerage brokerage;
  38    private final AccountGuard guard;
  39
  40    public PositionsListHandler(Brokerage brokerage, AccountGuard guard) {
  41        this.brokerage = brokerage;
  42        this.guard = guard;
  43    }
  44
  45    @Override
  46    public String name() {
  47        return "brokerage_positions_list";
  48    }
  49
  50    @Override
  51    public Object handle(Invocation invocation) {
  52        Accounts.Account account = guard.require(invocation);
  53        String symbol = invocation.string("symbol");
  54        List<Accounts.Position> positions = brokerage.accounts().positionsOf(account.accountId())
  55                .stream()
  56                .filter(position -> symbol == null || position.symbol().equals(symbol))
  57                .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Accounts.Position::marketValue).reversed())
  58                .toList();
  59        BigDecimal total = positions.stream().map(Accounts.Position::marketValue)
  60                .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
  61        return new Payload(account.accountId(), account.currency(), Money.string(total),
  62                positions.stream().map(PositionsListHandler::view).toList(),
  63                brokerage.clock().now());
  64    }
  65
  66    private static PositionView view(Accounts.Position position) {
  67        return new PositionView(position.symbol(), position.name(), position.sector(),
  68                position.quantity(), Money.price(position.averageCost()),
  69                Money.price(position.lastPrice()), Money.string(position.marketValue()),
  70                Money.string(position.unrealizedPnl()),
  71                position.unrealizedPnlPercent().toPlainString(),
  72                position.portfolioWeight().toPlainString());
  73    }
  74}

   1package com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers;
   2
   3import java.math.BigDecimal;
   4import java.math.RoundingMode;
   5import java.time.LocalDate;
   6import java.util.Comparator;
   7import java.util.List;
   8
   9import com.example.brokerage.domain.Brokerage;
  10import com.example.brokerage.domain.MarketData;
  11import com.example.brokerage.domain.Money;
  12import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ErrorCode;
  13import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Invocation;
  14import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolFailure;
  15import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolHandler;
  16
  17import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  18
  19/**
  20 * {@code brokerage_price_history_get}.
  21 *
  22 * <p>The interesting work here is the three summary fields. A model given 120 rows of OHLCV will
  23 * read some of them, do arithmetic in its head, and occasionally get it wrong — and the arithmetic
  24 * it is most likely to get wrong is the one it is most likely to be asked for, the period return.
  25 * Computing the answer in the handler costs nothing and removes a whole class of error.
  26 *
  27 * <p>This is a general rule worth stating plainly: <em>if a model will have to compute something
  28 * from your payload, and the computation is deterministic, compute it yourself.</em> Payload size
  29 * and arithmetic error go down together.
  30 */
  31@Component
  32public class PriceHistoryGetHandler implements ToolHandler {
  33
  34    record BarView(LocalDate date, String open, String high, String low, String close,
  35                   long volume) {
  36    }
  37
  38    record Payload(String symbol, String currency, LocalDate from, LocalDate to,
  39                   String periodHigh, String periodLow, String totalReturnPercent,
  40                   List<BarView> bars) {
  41    }
  42
  43    private final Brokerage brokerage;
  44
  45    public PriceHistoryGetHandler(Brokerage brokerage) {
  46        this.brokerage = brokerage;
  47    }
  48
  49    @Override
  50    public String name() {
  51        return "brokerage_price_history_get";
  52    }
  53
  54    @Override
  55    public Object handle(Invocation invocation) {
  56        String symbol = invocation.string("symbol");
  57        if (brokerage.instruments().find(symbol).isEmpty()) {
  58            throw ToolFailure.notFound(symbol,
  59                    "Call brokerage_instruments_search with what the customer said to find the "
  60                            + "right ticker, then try again.");
  61        }
  62        List<MarketData.Bar> bars = brokerage.marketData().history(symbol,
  63                invocation.integer("days", 30));
  64        if (bars.isEmpty()) {
  65            throw ToolFailure.of(ErrorCode.PRECONDITION_FAILED,
  66                    "There are no trading days in that window.",
  67                    "Ask for a longer window, or tell the customer the market has not been open.");
  68        }
  69        BigDecimal first = bars.getFirst().close();
  70        BigDecimal last = bars.getLast().close();
  71        BigDecimal high = bars.stream().map(MarketData.Bar::close).max(Comparator.naturalOrder())
  72                .orElse(last);
  73        BigDecimal low = bars.stream().map(MarketData.Bar::close).min(Comparator.naturalOrder())
  74                .orElse(last);
  75        BigDecimal totalReturn = first.signum() == 0 ? BigDecimal.ZERO
  76                : last.subtract(first).multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(100))
  77                        .divide(first, 2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
  78        return new Payload(symbol, Money.USD, bars.getFirst().date(), bars.getLast().date(),
  79                Money.price(high), Money.price(low), totalReturn.toPlainString(),
  80                bars.stream().map(PriceHistoryGetHandler::view).toList());
  81    }
  82
  83    private static BarView view(MarketData.Bar bar) {
  84        return new BarView(bar.date(), Money.price(bar.open()), Money.price(bar.high()),
  85                Money.price(bar.low()), Money.price(bar.close()), bar.volume());
  86    }
  87}

   1package com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers;
   2
   3import java.time.Instant;

   5import java.util.List;
   6
   7import com.example.brokerage.domain.Brokerage;
   8import com.example.brokerage.domain.MarketData;
   9import com.example.brokerage.domain.Money;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Invocation;
  11import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolHandler;
  12
  13import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  14import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
  15
  16/**
  17 * {@code brokerage_quotes_get}.
  18 *
  19 * <p>Plural by design. An agent comparing three holdings will call a singular quote tool three
  20 * times, and three round trips cost three times the latency, three audit records and three
  21 * opportunities for one of them to fail on its own. Batching is the single cheapest performance
  22 * decision in a tool catalog and it is made in the descriptor, not in the handler.
  23 *
  24 * <p>The {@code unresolved} array matters more than it looks. A tool that quietly drops the
  25 * symbols it could not price leaves the agent to notice that it asked for three and got two, and
  26 * it will not notice. Naming the failures makes the agent's next move obvious.
  27 */
  28@Component
  29public class QuotesGetHandler implements ToolHandler {
  30
  31    record QuoteView(String symbol, String last, String bid, String ask, long bidSize,
  32                     long askSize, String previousClose, String change, String changePercent,
  33                     long volume, int spreadBasisPoints, String currency, Instant asOf) {
  34    }
  35
  36    record Payload(String session, List<QuoteView> quotes, List<String> unresolved) {
  37    }
  38
  39    private final Brokerage brokerage;
  40
  41    public QuotesGetHandler(Brokerage brokerage) {
  42        this.brokerage = brokerage;
  43    }
  44
  45    @Override
  46    public String name() {
  47        return "brokerage_quotes_get";
  48    }
  49
  50    @Override
  51    public Object handle(Invocation invocation) {
  52        List<QuoteView> quotes = new ArrayList<>();
  53        List<String> unresolved = new ArrayList<>();
  54        for (JsonNode node : invocation.node("symbols").values()) {
  55            String symbol = node.asString();
  56            if (brokerage.instruments().find(symbol).isEmpty()) {
  57                unresolved.add(symbol);
  58                continue;
  59            }
  60            quotes.add(view(brokerage.marketData().quote(symbol)));
  61        }
  62        return new Payload(brokerage.clock().session().name(), quotes, unresolved);
  63    }
  64
  65    private static QuoteView view(MarketData.Quote quote) {
  66        return new QuoteView(quote.symbol(), Money.price(quote.last()), Money.price(quote.bid()),
  67                Money.price(quote.ask()), quote.bidSize(), quote.askSize(),
  68                Money.price(quote.previousClose()), Money.string(quote.change()),
  69                Money.string(quote.changePercent()), quote.volume(), quote.spreadBasisPoints(),
  70                Money.USD, quote.asOf());
  71    }
  72}

   1package com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers;
   2
   3import java.math.BigDecimal;
   4
   5import com.example.brokerage.domain.Brokerage;
   6import com.example.brokerage.domain.Money;
   7import com.example.brokerage.domain.Orders;
   8import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Invocation;
   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolFailure;
  10
  11import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  12
  13/**
  14 * Builds an order ticket from validated arguments, and applies the rules a JSON Schema cannot.
  15 *
  16 * <p>This class is where the schema profile's ban on {@code if}/{@code then} is paid for, so it is
  17 * worth being explicit about the trade. "A limit price is required when the order type is LIMIT"
  18 * is expressible in JSON Schema, as a conditional. It is not reliably expressible to a model,
  19 * because most runtimes drop the conditional on the way through and the model is then shown a
  20 * schema in which {@code limitPrice} is simply optional. So the rule is stated twice, in the two
  21 * places that actually work: in the descriptor's prose, which the model does read, and here, where
  22 * a violation becomes an error the model can act on.
  23 *
  24 * <p>Writing a rule twice is a cost. The alternative — a conditional the model never sees and the
  25 * handler therefore has to enforce anyway — is the same cost plus a schema that lies.
  26 */
  27@Component
  28public class Tickets {
  29
  30    private final Brokerage brokerage;
  31
  32    public Tickets(Brokerage brokerage) {
  33        this.brokerage = brokerage;
  34    }
  35
  36    public Orders.Ticket from(Invocation invocation, String accountId) {
  37        String symbol = invocation.string("symbol");
  38        if (brokerage.instruments().find(symbol).isEmpty()) {
  39            throw ToolFailure.notFound(symbol,
  40                    "Call brokerage_instruments_search with what the customer said, confirm the "
  41                            + "ticker with them, and try again.");
  42        }
  43        Orders.OrderType type = Orders.OrderType.valueOf(invocation.string("orderType"));
  44        BigDecimal limit = decimal(invocation, "limitPrice");
  45        BigDecimal stop = decimal(invocation, "stopPrice");
  46
  47        requirePrice(type, limit, "limitPrice", Orders.OrderType.LIMIT, Orders.OrderType.STOP_LIMIT);
  48        requirePrice(type, stop, "stopPrice", Orders.OrderType.STOP, Orders.OrderType.STOP_LIMIT);
  49        rejectPrice(type, limit, "limitPrice", Orders.OrderType.MARKET, Orders.OrderType.STOP);
  50        rejectPrice(type, stop, "stopPrice", Orders.OrderType.MARKET, Orders.OrderType.LIMIT);
  51
  52        Orders.Side side = Orders.Side.valueOf(invocation.string("side"));
  53        long quantity = invocation.integer("quantity");
  54        Orders.TimeInForce tif = Orders.TimeInForce.valueOf(invocation.string("timeInForce", "DAY"));
  55        boolean extended = invocation.flag("extendedHours", false);
  56        return new Orders.Ticket(accountId, symbol, side, quantity, type, limit, stop, tif,
  57                extended);
  58    }
  59
  60    /** A decimal argument, parsed strictly. The schema already pinned the shape; this pins the value. */
  61    public static BigDecimal decimal(Invocation invocation, String field) {
  62        String raw = invocation.string(field);
  63        if (raw == null) {
  64            return null;
  65        }
  66        BigDecimal value = Money.of(raw);
  67        if (value.signum() <= 0) {
  68            throw ToolFailure.invalidArgument(field + " must be greater than zero.",
  69                    "Re-send with a positive price, or omit it if this order type does not take one.");
  70        }
  71        return value;
  72    }
  73
  74    private static void requirePrice(Orders.OrderType type, BigDecimal value, String field,
  75                                     Orders.OrderType... needsIt) {
  76        if (value == null && contains(needsIt, type)) {
  77            throw ToolFailure.invalidArgument(
  78                    "A " + type + " order requires " + field + ".",
  79                    "Ask the customer what price they want and re-send with " + field + " set.");
  80        }
  81    }
  82
  83    private static void rejectPrice(Orders.OrderType type, BigDecimal value, String field,
  84                                    Orders.OrderType... forbidsIt) {
  85        if (value != null && contains(forbidsIt, type)) {
  86            throw ToolFailure.invalidArgument(
  87                    "A " + type + " order must not carry " + field + ".",
  88                    "Re-send without " + field + ", or change orderType if the customer wants a "
  89                            + "price condition.");
  90        }
  91    }
  92
  93    private static boolean contains(Orders.OrderType[] types, Orders.OrderType type) {
  94        for (Orders.OrderType candidate : types) {
  95            if (candidate == type) {
  96                return true;
  97            }
  98        }
  99        return false;
 100    }
 101}

   3import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
   4import java.security.MessageDigest;
   5import java.time.Instant;
   6import java.util.HexFormat;
   7import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
   8import java.util.List;
   9import java.util.Map;
  10import java.util.Optional;
  11import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
  12
  13import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ApprovalContext;
  14import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
  15import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Governance;
  16import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Invocation;
  17import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolDescriptor;
  18
  19import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
  20
  21/**
  22 * Where a human says yes.
  23 *
  24 * <p>The mechanism is a reference rather than a flag, and that distinction is the whole design. A
  25 * flag — {@code confirmed: true}, or a boolean on a session — can be set by the thing being
  26 * checked. A reference is a hash of the tool name, the exact arguments and the session, so an
  27 * approval granted for "buy 50 AAPL at market" cannot be spent on "buy 500", and an approval from
  28 * one conversation cannot be spent in another.
  29 *
  30 * <p>The flow is three steps and survives the agent restarting in the middle of it:
  31 *
  32 * <ol>
  33 *   <li>The agent calls a tool that needs approval. The gate has no grant for that reference, so
  34 *       the pipeline returns {@code APPROVAL_REQUIRED} with the reference and a rendered summary
  35 *       of what is about to happen.</li>
  36 *   <li>Something outside the model shows the summary to a human and records their answer against
  37 *       the reference. In this reference implementation that is the Angular console; in production
  38 *       it is whatever surface the customer is actually on.</li>
  39 *   <li>The agent calls the tool again, byte for byte. Now the grant matches and it runs.</li>
  40 * </ol>
  41 *
  42 * <p>Grants expire. An approval with no window is a standing instruction, and nobody means to give
  43 * one of those.
  44 */
  45public class ApprovalGate {
  46
  47    /** What the human is shown and what their answer is recorded against. */
  48    public record Pending(String reference, String tool, String title, String summary,
  49                          int riskTier, Governance.ApprovalMode mode, Instant requestedAt,
  50                          Instant expiresAt, JsonNode arguments, String sessionId) {
  51    }
  52
  53    public record Grant(String reference, String grantedBy, Instant grantedAt, Instant expiresAt) {
  54    }
  55
  56    private final Map<String, Pending> pending = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
  57    private final Map<String, Grant> grants = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
  58    private volatile String standIn;
  59
  60    /**
  61     * The stable reference for this exact call. Canonical JSON, so that a re-ordered argument
  62     * object is still the same approval and a changed value is not.
  63     */
  64    public static String referenceFor(Invocation invocation) {
  65        String canonical = invocation.descriptor().name() + "|"
  66                + invocation.principal().sessionId() + "|"
  67                + canonicalize(invocation.arguments());
  68        return "apr_" + hash(canonical);
  69    }
  70
  71    static String canonicalize(JsonNode node) {
  72        if (node == null || node.isNull()) {
  73            return "null";
  74        }
  75        if (node.isObject()) {
  76            Map<String, String> sorted = new java.util.TreeMap<>();
  77            node.properties().forEach(entry ->
  78                    sorted.put(entry.getKey(), canonicalize(entry.getValue())));
  79            StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder("{");
  80            sorted.forEach((key, value) -> out.append(key).append(':').append(value).append(','));
  81            return out.append('}').toString();
  82        }
  83        if (node.isArray()) {
  84            StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder("[");
  85            node.values().forEach(child -> out.append(canonicalize(child)).append(','));
  86            return out.append(']').toString();
  87        }
  88        return node.asString();
  89    }
  90
  91    private static String hash(String input) {
  92        try {
  93            MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
  94            byte[] bytes = digest.digest(input.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
  95            return HexFormat.of().formatHex(bytes).substring(0, 24);
  96        } catch (Exception e) {
  97            throw new IllegalStateException("SHA-256 is not available", e);
  98        }
  99    }
 100
 101    /**
 102     * Let the harness answer yes on the human's behalf.
 103     *
 104     * <p>This is a test affordance and it is a named, visible method rather than a quiet default,
 105     * because the two things it makes possible are both easy to get wrong. A trading scenario
 106     * that never gets past the approval gate is not testing the place tool at all; and a suite
 107     * that approves everything without saying so is not testing the gate. So the trading suite
 108     * turns this on explicitly and the refusal suite leaves it off, which is how both get covered.
 109     *
 110     * <p>It must never be reachable in a deployed service. In this project the only callers are in
 111     * the harness, and the gate the agent service builds is a different instance.
 112     */
 113    public void standInForTheHuman(String who) {
 114        this.standIn = who;
 115    }
 116
 117    public String standingInForTheHuman() {
 118        return standIn;
 119    }
 120
 121    /** True when a live grant exists for this reference. Consumed on use. */
 122    public boolean consume(String reference, Instant now) {
 123        if (standIn != null) {
 124            grants.put(reference, new Grant(reference, standIn, now, now.plusSeconds(120)));
 125        }
 126        Grant grant = grants.get(reference);
 127        if (grant == null) {
 128            return false;
 129        }
 130        grants.remove(reference);
 131        pending.remove(reference);
 132        return grant.expiresAt().isAfter(now);
 133    }
 134
 135    /**
 136     * Record what needs approving, and what the human should be shown.
 137     *
 138     * @param extra values from the domain that the arguments do not carry — the account's
 139     *              nickname, the priced cost, the warnings. See {@link ApprovalContext} for why
 140     *              rendering from the arguments alone is not good enough.
 141     */
 142    public Pending request(Invocation invocation, String reference, Map<String, String> extra,
 143                           Instant now) {
 144        ToolDescriptor descriptor = invocation.descriptor();
 145        Governance governance = descriptor.governance();
 146        int window = governance.approval().expiresInSeconds() == null
 147                ? 120 : governance.approval().expiresInSeconds();
 148        Pending request = new Pending(reference, descriptor.name(), descriptor.title(),
 149                render(governance.approval().confirmationTemplate(), invocation.arguments(), extra),
 150                governance.riskTier(), governance.approval().mode(), now,
 151                now.plusSeconds(window), invocation.arguments(),
 152                invocation.principal().sessionId());
 153        pending.put(reference, request);
 154        return request;
 155    }
 156
 157    public void grant(String reference, String grantedBy, Instant now) {
 158        Pending request = pending.get(reference);
 159        Instant expiry = request == null ? now.plusSeconds(120) : request.expiresAt();
 160        grants.put(reference, new Grant(reference, grantedBy, now, expiry));
 161    }
 162
 163    public void deny(String reference) {
 164        grants.remove(reference);
 165        pending.remove(reference);
 166    }
 167
 168    public Optional<Pending> peek(String reference) {
 169        return Optional.ofNullable(pending.get(reference));
 170    }
 171
 172    public List<Pending> awaiting(String sessionId) {
 173        return pending.values().stream()
 174                .filter(request -> sessionId == null || request.sessionId().equals(sessionId))
 175                .toList();
 176    }
 177
 178    /**
 179     * Fill a confirmation template from the arguments. Any placeholder with no argument is left
 180     * visible as {@code (not given)} rather than blanked, because a dialog with a quietly empty
 181     * field is how somebody approves an order whose quantity they never saw.
 182     */
 183    public static String render(String template, JsonNode arguments, Map<String, String> extra) {
 184        if (template == null) {
 185            return "";
 186        }
 187        Map<String, String> values = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 188        if (arguments != null && arguments.isObject()) {
 189            arguments.properties().forEach(entry ->
 190                    values.put(entry.getKey(), text(entry.getValue())));
 191        }
 192        if (extra != null) {
 193            values.putAll(extra);          // the domain's figures win over a raw argument
 194        }
 195        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
 196        int index = 0;
 197        while (index < template.length()) {
 198            int open = template.indexOf("{{", index);
 199            if (open < 0) {
 200                out.append(template, index, template.length());
 201                break;
 202            }
 203            int close = template.indexOf("}}", open);
 204            if (close < 0) {
 205                out.append(template, index, template.length());
 206                break;
 207            }
 208            out.append(template, index, open);
 209            String key = template.substring(open + 2, close).trim();
 210            out.append(values.getOrDefault(key, "(not given)"));
 211            index = close + 2;
 212        }
 213        // A placeholder that resolved to nothing — no warnings, say — leaves a hole in the middle
 214        // of the dialog, and a dialog with a gap in it reads as broken rather than as reassuring.
 215        return out.toString().replaceAll("\n{3,}", "\n\n").trim();
 216    }
 217
 218    private static String text(JsonNode node) {
 219        return node.isValueNode() ? node.asString() : DescriptorCodec.json(node);
 220    }
 221}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.time.Instant;
   4import java.util.ArrayDeque;
   5import java.util.ArrayList;
   6import java.util.Deque;
   7import java.util.List;
   8
   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ErrorCode;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Governance;
  11
  12/**
  13 * The audit record for every invocation, successful or not.
  14 *
  15 * <p>A record is written before the handler runs and completed after, so that a call which hangs
  16 * or crashes the process still leaves evidence it was attempted. The alternative — logging on the
  17 * way out — loses exactly the invocations an incident review cares about.
  18 *
  19 * <p>What is deliberately absent is as important as what is present. Arguments are recorded as a
  20 * hash and a list of field names, never as values. The reasoning: the record has to prove which
  21 * call was made and let a reviewer match it against an approval, and a hash does both. Storing the
  22 * values themselves would put account identifiers, order sizes and whatever the customer typed
  23 * into a log with a six-year retention and a much wider readership than the account itself.
  24 *
  25 * <p>In production this writes to the firm's immutable store. Here it keeps the last few thousand
  26 * in memory so the console can show them and the tests can assert on them.
  27 */
  28public class AuditLog {
  29
  30    /**
  31     * @param outcome  OK, or the error code returned
  32     * @param approval the approval reference, when a human had to agree
  33     */
  34    public record Record(String requestId, Instant at, String tool, String toolVersion,
  35                         int riskTier, String auditEvent, String retention, String subject,
  36                         String sessionId, List<String> argumentFields, String argumentHash,
  37                         String outcome, Long latencyMs, String approval,
  38                         Governance.ApprovalMode approvalMode) {
  39    }
  40
  41    private static final int CAPACITY = 5000;
  42
  43    private final Deque<Record> records = new ArrayDeque<>();
  44
  45    public synchronized void write(Record record) {
  46        records.addLast(record);
  47        while (records.size() > CAPACITY) {
  48            records.removeFirst();
  49        }
  50    }
  51
  52    public synchronized List<Record> recent(int limit) {
  53        List<Record> out = new ArrayList<>(records);
  54        java.util.Collections.reverse(out);
  55        return out.subList(0, Math.min(limit, out.size()));
  56    }
  57
  58    public synchronized List<Record> forSession(String sessionId) {
  59        return records.stream().filter(record -> sessionId.equals(record.sessionId())).toList();
  60    }
  61
  62    public synchronized long count(ErrorCode code) {
  63        return records.stream().filter(record -> code.name().equals(record.outcome())).count();
  64    }
  65
  66    public synchronized void clear() {
  67        records.clear();
  68    }
  69}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
   4import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Principal;
   5import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolDescriptor;
   6
   7import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ToolContext;
   8import org.springframework.ai.tool.ToolCallback;
   9import org.springframework.ai.tool.definition.DefaultToolDefinition;
  10import org.springframework.ai.tool.definition.ToolDefinition;
  11import org.springframework.ai.tool.metadata.ToolMetadata;
  12
  13/**
  14 * One descriptor, presented to Spring AI as a tool.
  15 *
  16 * <p>This class is the whole binding between the specification and the framework, and its size is
  17 * the argument for writing descriptors as data. There is no {@code @Tool} annotation anywhere in
  18 * this project. The model's view of a tool is a JSON file that a linter checks, a reviewer reads
  19 * and a desktop client can be handed; Spring AI gets the same three strings it would have derived
  20 * from an annotation, and every other runtime gets them too, from an adapter about this long.
  21 *
  22 * <p>Contrast the annotated approach. {@code @Tool(description = "...")} puts the model-facing
  23 * contract inside a Java method signature, where the schema is inferred from parameter types, the
  24 * description is a string literal nobody lints, and the only way to see what the model is being
  25 * shown is to start the application. It is faster for the first three tools and it does not scale
  26 * past a dozen.
  27 *
  28 * <p>The callback is deliberately dumb: it hands the raw argument string to
  29 * {@link InvocationPipeline} and returns whatever JSON comes back. It does not validate, authorize,
  30 * catch or format, because doing any of those here would mean they happened only for callers who
  31 * came through Spring AI.
  32 */
  33public class DescriptorToolCallback implements ToolCallback {
  34
  35    private final ToolDescriptor descriptor;
  36    private final InvocationPipeline pipeline;
  37    private final Principal principal;
  38    private final ToolTrace trace;
  39
  40    public DescriptorToolCallback(ToolDescriptor descriptor, InvocationPipeline pipeline,
  41                                  Principal principal, ToolTrace trace) {
  42        this.descriptor = descriptor;
  43        this.pipeline = pipeline;
  44        this.principal = principal;
  45        this.trace = trace;
  46    }
  47
  48    @Override
  49    public ToolDefinition getToolDefinition() {
  50        return DefaultToolDefinition.builder()
  51                .name(descriptor.name())
  52                .description(descriptor.description())
  53                .inputSchema(DescriptorCodec.json(descriptor.inputSchema()))
  54                .build();
  55    }
  56
  57    @Override
  58    public ToolMetadata getToolMetadata() {
  59        // returnDirect is false for every tool in this catalog: the model must always get a turn
  60        // to read the result, because every result can carry a blocker or an error it has to relay.
  61        return ToolMetadata.builder().returnDirect(false).build();
  62    }
  63
  64    @Override
  65    public String call(String arguments) {
  66        InvocationPipeline.Outcome outcome = pipeline.invoke(descriptor.name(), arguments,
  67                principal);
  68        if (trace != null) {
  69            trace.record(outcome, arguments);
  70        }
  71        return outcome.json();
  72    }
  73
  74    @Override
  75    public String call(String arguments, ToolContext context) {
  76        return call(arguments);
  77    }
  78
  79    public ToolDescriptor descriptor() {
  80        return descriptor;
  81    }
  82
  83    /**
  84     * Route a name this session does not have through the pipeline anyway, so that a model's
  85     * invented tool name produces a real UNKNOWN_TOOL envelope and a real audit record. An agent
  86     * guessing at names is worth knowing about.
  87     */
  88    String callUnknown(String tool, String arguments) {
  89        InvocationPipeline.Outcome outcome = pipeline.invoke(tool, arguments, principal);
  90        if (trace != null) {
  91            trace.record(outcome, arguments);
  92        }
  93        return outcome.json();
  94    }
  95}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.time.Duration;
   4import java.time.Instant;
   5import java.util.List;
   6import java.util.UUID;
   7
   8import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ApprovalContext;
   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ArgumentValidator;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
  11import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ErrorCode;
  12import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Governance;
  13import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Invocation;
  14import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Principal;
  15import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolFailure;
  16import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolResult;
  17
  18import org.slf4j.Logger;
  19import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
  20import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
  21
  22/**
  23 * Everything that happens around a handler.
  24 *
  25 * <p>The ten steps below are the system. A handler is domain code; this is the part that makes a
  26 * tool catalog safe to point a language model at, and it is identical for all fourteen tools,
  27 * which is precisely why it belongs here and not in any of them.
  28 *
  29 * <pre>
  30 *    1  resolve      the name must be in this principal's catalog        UNKNOWN_TOOL
  31 *    2  kill switch  the tool must not be out of service                 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE
  32 *    3  parse        the arguments must be a JSON object                 INVALID_ARGUMENT
  33 *    4  validate     they must satisfy the input schema                  INVALID_ARGUMENT
  34 *    5  entitle      the principal must hold every scope                 NOT_ENTITLED
  35 *    6  rate limit   within the per-principal budget for this tool       RATE_LIMITED
  36 *    7  approve      a human must have agreed, for tier 2 and above      APPROVAL_REQUIRED
  37 *    8  execute      the handler runs, and only now
  38 *    9  verify       the payload must satisfy the output schema          INTERNAL_ERROR
  39 *   10  envelope     wrap, stamp provenance, and audit
  40 * </pre>
  41 *
  42 * <p>Two of these are the ones people leave out, so they get their own note.
  43 *
  44 * <p><b>Step 5 after step 4.</b> Arguments are validated before entitlements are checked, which
  45 * looks backwards — surely you refuse the unauthorized caller first? For a human API, yes. For a
  46 * model, no: the useful answer to a malformed call is "your third argument is wrong", and giving
  47 * it a bare {@code NOT_ENTITLED} teaches it to retry the same malformed call against a different
  48 * tool. Nothing leaks, because the tool was already in the principal's visible catalog before the
  49 * pipeline ran.
  50 *
  51 * <p><b>Step 9 at all.</b> Validating the handler's own output sounds like distrust of your
  52 * colleagues. It is distrust of drift. The output schema is the only description of the payload
  53 * the model will ever see, and the day a handler adds a field or renames one, the model is being
  54 * misled by a document the firm published. Failing closed here makes that a caught bug rather than
  55 * a confusing conversation.
  56 */
  57public class InvocationPipeline {
  58
  59    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(InvocationPipeline.class);
  60
  61    private final ToolRegistry registry;
  62    private final ArgumentValidator validator = new ArgumentValidator();
  63    private final ApprovalGate approvals;
  64    private final RateLimiter rateLimiter;
  65    private final KillSwitches killSwitches;
  66    private final AuditLog audit;
  67    private final ApprovalContext approvalContext;
  68    private final java.util.function.Supplier<Instant> clock;
  69
  70    public InvocationPipeline(ToolRegistry registry, ApprovalGate approvals,
  71                              RateLimiter rateLimiter, KillSwitches killSwitches, AuditLog audit,
  72                              ApprovalContext approvalContext,
  73                              java.util.function.Supplier<Instant> clock) {
  74        this.registry = registry;
  75        this.approvals = approvals;
  76        this.rateLimiter = rateLimiter;
  77        this.killSwitches = killSwitches;
  78        this.audit = audit;
  79        this.approvalContext = approvalContext == null ? ApprovalContext.NONE : approvalContext;
  80        this.clock = clock;
  81    }
  82
  83    /** The result, plus what the console and the harness need to explain it. */
  84    public record Outcome(String tool, ToolResult<Object> result, String json, long latencyMs,
  85                          String approvalReference) {
  86
  87        public boolean ok() {
  88            return result.ok();
  89        }
  90
  91        public ErrorCode errorCode() {
  92            return result.error() == null ? null : result.error().code();
  93        }
  94    }
  95
  96    public Outcome invoke(String tool, String argumentsJson, Principal principal) {
  97        Instant started = clock.get();
  98        String requestId = "req_" + UUID.randomUUID().toString().replace("-", "").substring(0, 20);
  99
 100        ToolRegistry.Entry entry = registry.find(tool).orElse(null);
 101        if (entry == null || !principal.holdsAll(entry.governance().entitlements())) {
 102            return failure(tool, null, requestId, started, ErrorCode.UNKNOWN_TOOL,
 103                    "There is no tool called " + tool + " available in this session.",
 104                    "Use one of the tools you were given. Do not guess at names.", principal, null);
 105        }
 106        Governance governance = entry.governance();
 107
 108        if (governance.availability() != null
 109                && killSwitches.isOff(governance.availability().killSwitch())) {
 110            return failure(tool, governance, requestId, started, ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE,
 111                    "This tool is temporarily out of service.",
 112                    "Tell the customer the feature is unavailable right now and do not retry in "
 113                            + "this conversation.", principal, null);
 114        }
 115
 116        JsonNode arguments;
 117        try {
 118            arguments = argumentsJson == null || argumentsJson.isBlank()
 119                    ? DescriptorCodec.mapper().createObjectNode()
 120                    : DescriptorCodec.tree(argumentsJson);
 121        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
 122            return failure(tool, governance, requestId, started, ErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT,
 123                    "The arguments were not valid JSON.",
 124                    "Re-send the call with a JSON object matching the tool's input schema.",
 125                    principal, null);
 126        }
 127        if (!arguments.isObject()) {
 128            return failure(tool, governance, requestId, started, ErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT,
 129                    "Arguments must be a JSON object.",
 130                    "Re-send the call with a JSON object matching the tool's input schema.",
 131                    principal, null);
 132        }
 133
 134        List<ArgumentValidator.Violation> violations =
 135                validator.validateArguments(entry.descriptor(), arguments);
 136        if (!violations.isEmpty()) {
 137            return failure(tool, governance, requestId, started, ErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT,
 138                    "The arguments do not match this tool's input schema: "
 139                            + ArgumentValidator.explain(violations),
 140                    "Fix the fields named above and call the tool again. Do not try a different "
 141                            + "tool.", principal, arguments);
 142        }
 143
 144        Integer wait = rateLimiter.retryAfter(principal.subject(), tool,
 145                governance.rateLimit() == null ? null : governance.rateLimit().perPrincipalPerMinute(),
 146                started);
 147        if (wait != null) {
 148            ToolResult.Failure error = ToolResult.Failure.of(ErrorCode.RATE_LIMITED,
 149                    "This tool has been called too often in this session.",
 150                    "Wait " + wait + " seconds before calling it again, and tell the customer "
 151                            + "there is a short delay.").retryAfter(wait);
 152            return record(tool, governance, requestId, started, principal, arguments,
 153                    ToolResult.failure(error, meta(governance, requestId, started, false)), null);
 154        }
 155
 156        Invocation invocation = new Invocation(entry.descriptor(), arguments, principal, requestId,
 157                started);
 158        String approvalReference = null;
 159        if (governance.requiresApproval()) {
 160            approvalReference = ApprovalGate.referenceFor(invocation);
 161            if (!approvals.consume(approvalReference, started)) {
 162                ApprovalGate.Pending request = approvals.request(invocation, approvalReference,
 163                        enrich(invocation), started);
 164                ToolResult.Failure error = ToolResult.Failure.of(ErrorCode.APPROVAL_REQUIRED,
 165                        "This action needs the customer's explicit approval before it can run. "
 166                                + "They have been shown: " + request.summary(),
 167                        "Wait for the customer to approve. If they say yes, call this tool again "
 168                                + "with exactly the same arguments. If they say no, stop and do "
 169                                + "not look for another way.").withApprovalReference(approvalReference);
 170                return record(tool, governance, requestId, started, principal, arguments,
 171                        ToolResult.failure(error, meta(governance, requestId, started, false)),
 172                        approvalReference);
 173            }
 174        }
 175
 176        try {
 177            Object payload = entry.handler().handle(invocation);
 178            JsonNode tree = DescriptorCodec.tree(payload);
 179            List<ArgumentValidator.Violation> output =
 180                    validator.validatePayload(entry.descriptor(), tree);
 181            if (!output.isEmpty()) {
 182                log.error("{} returned a payload that does not match its own output schema: {}",
 183                        tool, ArgumentValidator.explain(output));
 184                return failure(tool, governance, requestId, started, ErrorCode.INTERNAL_ERROR,
 185                        "This tool could not complete.",
 186                        "Tell the customer the request failed and quote " + requestId
 187                                + ". Do not retry.", principal, arguments);
 188            }
 189            return record(tool, governance, requestId, started, principal, arguments,
 190                    ToolResult.success(payload, meta(governance, requestId, started, true)),
 191                    approvalReference);
 192        } catch (ToolFailure failure) {
 193            return record(tool, governance, requestId, started, principal, arguments,
 194                    ToolResult.failure(failure.failure(),
 195                            meta(governance, requestId, started, false)), approvalReference);
 196        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
 197            log.error("{} threw {}; request {}", tool, e.getClass().getName(), requestId, e);
 198            return failure(tool, governance, requestId, started, ErrorCode.INTERNAL_ERROR,
 199                    "This tool could not complete.",
 200                    "Tell the customer the request failed and quote " + requestId
 201                            + ". Do not retry.", principal, arguments);
 202        }
 203    }
 204
 205    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
 206
 207    /**
 208     * Ask the domain for the figures a confirmation needs. Failure here must never block an
 209     * approval, so a broken enricher degrades the dialog rather than the trade.
 210     */
 211    private java.util.Map<String, String> enrich(Invocation invocation) {
 212        try {
 213            return approvalContext.enrich(invocation);
 214        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
 215            log.warn("approval context failed for {}: {}", invocation.descriptor().name(),
 216                    e.toString());
 217            return java.util.Map.of();
 218        }
 219    }
 220
 221    private ToolResult.Meta meta(Governance governance, String requestId, Instant started,
 222                                 boolean complete) {
 223        return new ToolResult.Meta(clock.get(), governance == null ? null : governance.version(),
 224                requestId, complete, null, null,
 225                Duration.between(started, clock.get()).toMillis());
 226    }
 227
 228    private Outcome failure(String tool, Governance governance, String requestId, Instant started,
 229                            ErrorCode code, String message, String remediation,
 230                            Principal principal, JsonNode arguments) {
 231        return record(tool, governance, requestId, started, principal, arguments,
 232                ToolResult.failure(code, message, remediation,
 233                        meta(governance, requestId, started, false)), null);
 234    }
 235
 236    private Outcome record(String tool, Governance governance, String requestId, Instant started,
 237                           Principal principal, JsonNode arguments, ToolResult<Object> result,
 238                           String approvalReference) {
 239        long latency = Duration.between(started, clock.get()).toMillis();
 240        audit.write(new AuditLog.Record(requestId, started, tool,
 241                governance == null ? null : governance.version(),
 242                governance == null ? -1 : governance.riskTier(),
 243                governance == null ? null : governance.recordKeeping().auditEvent(),
 244                governance == null ? null : governance.recordKeeping().retention(),
 245                principal.subject(), principal.sessionId(), fields(arguments),
 246                ApprovalGate.canonicalize(arguments).hashCode() == 0 ? "0"
 247                        : Integer.toHexString(ApprovalGate.canonicalize(arguments).hashCode()),
 248                result.ok() ? "OK" : result.error().code().name(), latency, approvalReference,
 249                governance == null || governance.approval() == null
 250                        ? null : governance.approval().mode()));
 251        return new Outcome(tool, result, DescriptorCodec.json(result), latency, approvalReference);
 252    }
 253
 254    /** Field names only. The values are the customer's business and do not belong in a log. */
 255    private static List<String> fields(JsonNode arguments) {
 256        return arguments == null || !arguments.isObject()
 257                ? List.of() : List.copyOf(arguments.propertyNames());
 258    }
 259}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.util.Map;
   4import java.util.Set;
   5import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
   6
   7/**
   8 * Named switches that take tools out of service without a deployment.
   9 *
  10 * <p>Every tool at tier 2 or above must name one, and the linter enforces that, for a reason that
  11 * only becomes obvious the first time you need it. When a tool starts behaving badly at two in the
  12 * morning, the options are: turn it off, or roll back. Rolling back takes a build. Turning it off
  13 * takes a configuration change, and the agent's next turn simply does not see the tool — no error,
  14 * no retry loop, no half-working catalog.
  15 *
  16 * <p>Switches are hierarchical by prefix, so {@code tools.brokerage.trading} disables
  17 * {@code tools.brokerage.trading.place} and {@code tools.brokerage.trading.cancel} with it. That
  18 * matters when the thing misbehaving is a dependency rather than a tool.
  19 */
  20public class KillSwitches {
  21
  22    private final Set<String> tripped = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
  23
  24    public void trip(String switchName) {
  25        tripped.add(switchName);
  26    }
  27
  28    public void reset(String switchName) {
  29        tripped.remove(switchName);
  30    }
  31
  32    public Set<String> tripped() {
  33        return Set.copyOf(tripped);
  34    }
  35
  36    /** True when this switch, or any switch it sits under, has been tripped. */
  37    public boolean isOff(String switchName) {
  38        if (switchName == null) {
  39            return false;
  40        }
  41        if (tripped.contains(switchName)) {
  42            return true;
  43        }
  44        int dot = switchName.lastIndexOf('.');
  45        return dot > 0 && isOff(switchName.substring(0, dot));
  46    }
  47
  48    public Map<String, Boolean> status(Iterable<String> switchNames) {
  49        Map<String, Boolean> status = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();
  50        switchNames.forEach(name -> status.put(name, !isOff(name)));
  51        return status;
  52    }
  53}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.time.Duration;
   4import java.time.Instant;
   5import java.util.ArrayDeque;
   6import java.util.Deque;
   7import java.util.Map;
   8import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
   9
  10/**
  11 * A per-principal, per-tool sliding-window limiter.
  12 *
  13 * <p>Rate limiting a tool catalog is not about load. It is about the one failure mode a language
  14 * model has that a human caller does not: a loop. An agent that misreads an error as transient
  15 * will retry it, and if the retry produces the same error it will retry again, politely, as many
  16 * times as the turn budget allows. The limit is what turns an expensive loop into a clear
  17 * {@code RATE_LIMITED} with a wait, which the agent can relay.
  18 *
  19 * <p>The window is counted per tool rather than per catalog, because the limits that matter are
  20 * different by two orders of magnitude: 180 quote calls a minute is normal and 180 order
  21 * placements a minute is an incident.
  22 */
  23public class RateLimiter {
  24
  25    private static final Duration WINDOW = Duration.ofMinutes(1);
  26
  27    private final Map<String, Deque<Instant>> calls = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
  28
  29    /** Null when the call is allowed, or the seconds to wait when it is not. */
  30    public Integer retryAfter(String principal, String tool, Integer perMinute, Instant now) {
  31        if (perMinute == null || perMinute <= 0) {
  32            return null;
  33        }
  34        Deque<Instant> window = calls.computeIfAbsent(principal + "|" + tool,
  35                ignored -> new ArrayDeque<>());
  36        synchronized (window) {
  37            Instant cutoff = now.minus(WINDOW);
  38            while (!window.isEmpty() && window.peekFirst().isBefore(cutoff)) {
  39                window.removeFirst();
  40            }
  41            if (window.size() >= perMinute) {
  42                long wait = WINDOW.minus(Duration.between(window.peekFirst(), now)).toSeconds();
  43                return (int) Math.max(1, wait);
  44            }
  45            window.addLast(now);
  46            return null;
  47        }
  48    }
  49
  50    public void clear() {
  51        calls.clear();
  52    }
  53}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
   4import java.util.Map;
   5import java.util.Set;
   6
   7import org.springframework.ai.tool.ToolCallback;
   8
   9/**
  10 * A published toolset, callable by name.
  11 *
  12 * <p>The test harness needs this, and so does anything else that drives tools without a model in
  13 * the loop — a batch job replaying a trace, an operator reproducing a customer's conversation, the
  14 * desktop connector. Spring AI hands out a list of callbacks because that is what a chat model
  15 * wants; everything else wants a map.
  16 *
  17 * <p>Calling a name that is not in the set returns the pipeline's own {@code UNKNOWN_TOOL}
  18 * envelope rather than throwing, because that is what a model would have received, and a harness
  19 * that threw here would be testing something the model never experiences.
  20 */
  21public class ToolCallbackHolder {
  22
  23    private final Map<String, ToolCallback> byName = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  24    private final ToolCallback unknown;
  25
  26    public ToolCallbackHolder(java.util.List<ToolCallback> callbacks) {
  27        for (ToolCallback callback : callbacks) {
  28            byName.put(callback.getToolDefinition().name(), callback);
  29        }
  30        this.unknown = callbacks.isEmpty() ? null : callbacks.getFirst();
  31    }
  32
  33    public Set<String> names() {
  34        return byName.keySet();
  35    }
  36
  37    /** Invoke by name. An unknown name is routed through the pipeline so it is audited too. */
  38    public String call(String tool, String arguments) {
  39        ToolCallback callback = byName.get(tool);
  40        if (callback == null) {
  41            if (unknown instanceof DescriptorToolCallback descriptor) {
  42                return descriptor.callUnknown(tool, arguments);
  43            }
  44            return "{\"ok\":false,\"error\":{\"code\":\"UNKNOWN_TOOL\",\"message\":\"There is no "
  45                    + "tool called " + tool + " available in this session.\"}}";
  46        }
  47        return callback.call(arguments);
  48    }
  49}

   9/**
  10 * Turns the registry into the list of tools one session is allowed to see.
  11 *
  12 * <p>Publishing per principal rather than once at startup is the difference between a toolset and
  13 * a configuration. The same application serves a read-only analytics session, a customer session
  14 * that may trade, and an operations session that may neither — and each of them is shown a
  15 * different catalog, not the same catalog with different outcomes.
  16 */
  17public class ToolPublisher {
  18
  19    private final ToolRegistry registry;
  20    private final InvocationPipeline pipeline;
  21
  22    public ToolPublisher(ToolRegistry registry, InvocationPipeline pipeline) {
  23        this.registry = registry;
  24        this.pipeline = pipeline;
  25    }
  26
  27    public List<ToolCallback> publish(Principal principal, ToolTrace trace) {
  28        return registry.visibleTo(principal).stream()
  29                .map(entry -> (ToolCallback) new DescriptorToolCallback(entry.descriptor(),
  30                        pipeline, principal, trace))
  31                .toList();
  32    }
  33
  34    public String briefing(Principal principal) {
  35        return ToolsetBriefing.forPrincipal(registry, principal);
  36    }
  37
  38    public ToolRegistry registry() {
  39        return registry;
  40    }
  41
  42    public InvocationPipeline pipeline() {
  43        return pipeline;
  44    }
  45}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.util.ArrayList;
   4import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
   5import java.util.List;
   6import java.util.Map;
   7import java.util.Optional;
   8
   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ConformanceLinter;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Finding;
  11import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Governance;
  12import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Ontology;
  13import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Principal;
  14import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolDescriptor;
  15import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolHandler;
  16
  17/**
  18 * The tool registry: the one place that knows what tools exist, what each one promises, who may
  19 * call it, and what code is behind it.
  20 *
  21 * <p>A registry sounds like plumbing and is in fact the main architectural decision in a tool
  22 * system. Without one, the set of tools a model sees is whatever beans happened to be on the
  23 * classpath, which means nobody can answer four questions that get asked constantly: what is the
  24 * model being shown right now, who is allowed to call each of these, which of them have been
  25 * reviewed, and what happens if we turn one off. With one, all four are lookups.
  26 *
  27 * <p>Three rules are enforced at construction, deliberately early, so that a misconfigured
  28 * catalog fails at startup rather than in a conversation.
  29 *
  30 * <ol>
  31 *   <li>Every descriptor has a handler and every handler has a descriptor. A handler with no
  32 *       descriptor is dead code; a descriptor with no handler is a tool the model will choose and
  33 *       then be told does not work.</li>
  34 *   <li>Every descriptor passes the conformance linter. A registry that serves a non-conformant
  35 *       descriptor has made the specification advisory.</li>
  36 *   <li>Every descriptor is {@code active}. Draft and retired tools are not served, however
  37 *       complete they look.</li>
  38 * </ol>
  39 */
  40public class ToolRegistry {
  41
  42    /** One registered tool: its contract, its code, and its place in the ontology. */
  43    public record Entry(ToolDescriptor descriptor, ToolHandler handler,
  44                        Ontology.Capability capability) {
  45
  46        public Governance governance() {
  47            return descriptor.governance();
  48        }
  49
  50        public String name() {
  51            return descriptor.name();
  52        }
  53    }
  54
  55    private final Ontology ontology;
  56    private final Map<String, Entry> entries = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  57    private final List<Finding> findings;
  58
  59    /**
  60     * @param ontology the domain ontology, or null for a registry with no ontology discipline.
  61     *                 Null is permitted because the ontology is an additional constraint rather
  62     *                 than a prerequisite — a small catalog can be conformant without one, and an
  63     *                 isolated test of the pipeline should not have to invent one.
  64     */
  65    public ToolRegistry(Ontology ontology, List<ToolDescriptor> descriptors,
  66                        List<ToolHandler> handlers) {
  67        this.ontology = ontology;
  68        Map<String, ToolHandler> byName = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  69        for (ToolHandler handler : handlers) {
  70            byName.put(handler.name(), handler);
  71        }
  72        this.findings = new ConformanceLinter(ontology).lint(descriptors);
  73        if (ConformanceLinter.failed(findings)) {
  74            throw new IllegalStateException("the catalog does not conform:\n  "
  75                    + String.join("\n  ", findings.stream().map(Finding::toString).toList()));
  76        }
  77        for (ToolDescriptor descriptor : descriptors) {
  78            ToolHandler handler = byName.remove(descriptor.name());
  79            if (handler == null) {
  80                throw new IllegalStateException("no handler for " + descriptor.name()
  81                        + ": the model would choose a tool that cannot run");
  82            }
  83            if (descriptor.governance().lifecycle() != Governance.Lifecycle.ACTIVE) {
  84                continue;
  85            }
  86            entries.put(descriptor.name(), new Entry(descriptor, handler,
  87                    ontology == null ? null : ontology.capabilityOf(descriptor.name())));
  88        }
  89        if (!byName.isEmpty()) {
  90            throw new IllegalStateException("handlers with no descriptor: " + byName.keySet()
  91                    + ". Either publish a descriptor or delete the handler");
  92        }
  93    }
  94
  95    public Ontology ontology() {
  96        return ontology;
  97    }
  98
  99    /** Non-blocking findings from the startup lint, for the console to display. */
 100    public List<Finding> findings() {
 101        return List.copyOf(findings);
 102    }
 103
 104    public List<Entry> all() {
 105        return new ArrayList<>(entries.values());
 106    }
 107
 108    public Optional<Entry> find(String name) {
 109        return Optional.ofNullable(entries.get(name));
 110    }
 111
 112    public int size() {
 113        return entries.size();
 114    }
 115
 116    /**
 117     * The tools this principal may actually call.
 118     *
 119     * <p>Filtering here rather than at execution time is not an optimization, it is the whole
 120     * point. A tool the principal cannot use, published into the model's context, costs tokens and
 121     * buys a wrong turn: the model will choose it, be refused, apologize, and choose again. Showing
 122     * a model only what it can do is the cheapest accuracy improvement available.
 123     */
 124    public List<Entry> visibleTo(Principal principal) {
 125        return entries.values().stream()
 126                .filter(entry -> principal.holdsAll(entry.governance().entitlements()))
 127                .toList();
 128    }
 129
 130    /** Which tools would be hidden from this principal, and why. Used by the console, not the model. */
 131    public Map<String, List<String>> hiddenFrom(Principal principal) {
 132        Map<String, List<String>> hidden = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 133        for (Entry entry : entries.values()) {
 134            List<String> missing = entry.governance().entitlements().stream()
 135                    .filter(entitlement -> !principal.holds(entitlement)).toList();
 136            if (!missing.isEmpty()) {
 137                hidden.put(entry.name(), missing);
 138            }
 139        }
 140        return hidden;
 141    }
 142}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.util.ArrayList;
   4import java.util.List;
   5
   6import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ErrorCode;
   7
   8/**
   9 * What the model actually did, in order.
  10 *
  11 * <p>This is the single most useful artifact in the whole system and it is almost always missing.
  12 * When an agent gives a wrong answer, the question is never "what did the model say" — you have
  13 * that — it is "which tools did it call, with what arguments, in what order, and what came back".
  14 * Without a trace you are reduced to reading the final prose and guessing.
  15 *
  16 * <p>The trace is also what makes the test harness possible. Selection accuracy, argument
  17 * accuracy and trajectory assertions are all statements about this list, so the harness is a set
  18 * of expectations over a trace rather than a set of expectations over English.
  19 */
  20public class ToolTrace {
  21
  22    /**
  23     * @param step      1-based position in the turn
  24     * @param arguments the raw argument JSON as the model sent it, before any normalization
  25     */
  26    public record Step(int step, String tool, String arguments, boolean ok, ErrorCode errorCode,
  27                       long latencyMs, String approvalReference) {
  28    }
  29
  30    private final List<Step> steps = new ArrayList<>();
  31
  32    public synchronized void record(InvocationPipeline.Outcome outcome, String arguments) {
  33        steps.add(new Step(steps.size() + 1, outcome.tool(), arguments, outcome.ok(),
  34                outcome.errorCode(), outcome.latencyMs(), outcome.approvalReference()));
  35    }
  36
  37    public synchronized List<Step> steps() {
  38        return List.copyOf(steps);
  39    }
  40
  41    /** The tools called, in order, with repeats kept. The spine of a trajectory assertion. */
  42    public synchronized List<String> path() {
  43        return steps.stream().map(Step::tool).toList();
  44    }
  45
  46    public synchronized boolean called(String tool) {
  47        return steps.stream().anyMatch(step -> step.tool().equals(tool));
  48    }
  49
  50    /** Whether {@code first} was called before {@code second} ever was. */
  51    public synchronized boolean calledBefore(String first, String second) {
  52        int a = indexOf(first);
  53        int b = indexOf(second);
  54        return a >= 0 && (b < 0 || a < b);
  55    }
  56
  57    private int indexOf(String tool) {
  58        List<String> path = path();
  59        return path.indexOf(tool);
  60    }
  61
  62    public synchronized int size() {
  63        return steps.size();
  64    }
  65
  66    public synchronized void clear() {
  67        steps.clear();
  68    }
  69}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;
   2
   3import java.util.List;
   4import java.util.Map;
   5import java.util.Set;
   6import java.util.TreeSet;
   7
   8import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ErrorCode;
   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Ontology;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Principal;
  11
  12/**
  13 * The part of the system prompt that describes the toolset, generated from the ontology.
  14 *
  15 * <p>Generated, not written. That is the point of this class and it is worth being blunt about
  16 * why. A hand-written system prompt listing which tool to call for what is a second copy of the
  17 * catalog, maintained by hand, consulted by the model on every turn, and wrong within a month. The
  18 * first tool renamed, the first tool added, the first risk tier raised, and the prompt is telling
  19 * the model something that is no longer true — and unlike a stale comment, a stale prompt changes
  20 * behavior.
  21 *
  22 * <p>So the briefing is derived. The prerequisite chains come from the ontology's producer graph.
  23 * The list of what cannot be invented comes from the identifier types marked opaque. The error
  24 * handling rules come from the taxonomy's own {@code retryable} and {@code callerCanFix} flags.
  25 * Nothing here is typed twice, which means nothing here can disagree with the catalog.
  26 *
  27 * <p>What it deliberately does <em>not</em> contain is per-tool advice. "Use
  28 * brokerage_balances_get when the customer asks about money" belongs in that tool's description,
  29 * where it is reviewed with the tool, versioned with the tool, and loaded only when the tool is
  30 * published. A system prompt that duplicates descriptions is paying twice for the same tokens.
  31 */
  32public final class ToolsetBriefing {
  33
  34    private ToolsetBriefing() {
  35    }
  36
  37    /** The toolset section of the system prompt, for one principal's visible catalog. */
  38    public static String forPrincipal(ToolRegistry registry, Principal principal) {
  39        Ontology ontology = registry.ontology();
  40        List<ToolRegistry.Entry> visible = registry.visibleTo(principal);
  41        Set<String> names = new TreeSet<>(visible.stream().map(ToolRegistry.Entry::name).toList());
  42
  43        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
  44        out.append("## The tools you have\n\n");
  45        out.append("You have ").append(visible.size())
  46                .append(" brokerage tools. Each one's description is the contract: read it, and "
  47                        + "do not do anything it says not to. Where a description and this "
  48                        + "briefing disagree, the description wins.\n\n");
  49
  50        Map<String, List<String>> producers = ontology.producers();
  51        StringBuilder opaque = new StringBuilder();
  52        ontology.identifierTypes().forEach((type, identifier) -> {
  53            List<String> from = producers.getOrDefault(type, List.of()).stream()
  54                    .filter(names::contains).toList();
  55            if (identifier.opaque() && !from.isEmpty()) {
  56                opaque.append("- ").append(article(type)).append(' ').append(type)
  57                        .append(" looks like ")
  58                        .append(identifier.example())
  59                        .append(" and can only come from ").append(humanList(from))
  60                        .append(". Never construct one, never edit one, never reuse one from "
  61                                + "earlier in the conversation if anything has changed.\n");
  62            }
  63        });
  64        section(out, "Identifiers you cannot invent", opaque);
  65
  66        StringBuilder first = new StringBuilder();
  67        for (ToolRegistry.Entry entry : visible) {
  68            Set<String> prerequisites = ontology.prerequisitesOf(entry.name()).stream()
  69                    .filter(names::contains)
  70                    .collect(java.util.stream.Collectors.toCollection(TreeSet::new));
  71            if (!prerequisites.isEmpty()) {
  72                first.append("- ").append(entry.name()).append(" needs values from ")
  73                        .append(humanList(List.copyOf(prerequisites))).append(".\n");
  74            }
  75        }
  76        section(out, "What has to happen first", first);
  77
  78        out.append("## Approval\n\n");
  79        List<String> needApproval = visible.stream()
  80                .filter(entry -> entry.governance().requiresApproval())
  81                .map(ToolRegistry.Entry::name).toList();
  82        if (needApproval.isEmpty()) {
  83            out.append("None of your tools changes anything. If the customer asks you to trade, "
  84                    + "say you can look but not act, and offer what you can see.\n");
  85        } else {
  86            out.append("These tools change something real and need the customer's explicit "
  87                    + "approval first: ").append(humanList(needApproval)).append(".\n\n")
  88                    .append("The approval is not yours to give and not yours to infer. Ask, in "
  89                            + "plain words, with the amount and the instrument in the question. "
  90                            + "If the tool answers APPROVAL_REQUIRED, stop and wait; when the "
  91                            + "customer agrees, call it again with exactly the same arguments. "
  92                            + "If they say no, say so and stop — do not look for a different "
  93                            + "tool that achieves the same thing.\n");
  94        }
  95
  96        out.append("\n## Reading an error\n\n");
  97        out.append("Every tool returns an envelope. When ok is false, read error.code and follow "
  98                + "error.remediation. The codes behave like this:\n\n");
  99        for (ErrorCode code : ErrorCode.values()) {
 100            out.append("- ").append(code.name()).append(": ").append(code.guidance()).append('\n');
 101        }
 102
 103        out.append("\n## Calling well\n\n");
 104        out.append("""
 105                - Call the batch tools once with everything, not once per item.
 106                - Ask for the smallest window or page that answers the question.
 107                - When a result says it is incomplete, say so rather than presenting it as all.
 108                - When a result carries an asOf, quote it if any time has passed.
 109                - When two instruments could match what the customer said, ask. Do not pick.
 110                - Never report an action as done because you called the tool; report what the
 111                  result says happened.
 112                """);
 113        return out.toString();
 114    }
 115
 116    /** Append a heading and its body, or nothing at all when the body came out empty. */
 117    private static void section(StringBuilder out, String heading, StringBuilder body) {
 118        if (body.isEmpty()) {
 119            return;
 120        }
 121        out.append("## ").append(heading).append("\n\n").append(body).append('\n');
 122    }
 123
 124    private static String article(String word) {
 125        return "AEIOU".indexOf(word.charAt(0)) >= 0 ? "An" : "A";
 126    }
 127
 128    private static String humanList(List<String> items) {
 129        if (items.isEmpty()) {
 130            return "nothing";
 131        }
 132        if (items.size() == 1) {
 133            return items.getFirst();
 134        }
 135        return String.join(", ", items.subList(0, items.size() - 1)) + " or "
 136                + items.getLast();
 137    }
 138}

   1package com.example.brokerage.agent;
   2
   3import java.util.List;
   4
   5import com.example.brokerage.catalog.BrokerageCatalog;
   6import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolPublisher;
   7import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolTrace;
   8
   9import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.AssistantMessage;
  10import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.UserMessage;
  11import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatModel;
  12import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatResponse;
  13import org.springframework.ai.tool.ToolCallback;
  14import org.springframework.ai.anthropic.AnthropicChatOptions;
  15import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.ChatClient;
  16import org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider;
  17import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  18
  19/**
  20 * The agent: Claude, this session's visible tools, and nothing else.
  21 *
  22 * <p>Three decisions in this class are worth the reader's attention.
  23 *
  24 * <p><b>The tools are published per turn, not per application.</b> Each call builds fresh callbacks
  25 * bound to this session's principal and to a fresh {@link ToolTrace}. Two consequences follow: a
  26 * research session and a trading session running at the same moment see different catalogs, and
  27 * every turn comes back with a complete record of what was called.
  28 *
  29 * <p><b>The system prompt is assembled, not stored.</b> The conduct half is written by a human and
  30 * lives in a file beside the descriptors, where compliance can read it. The toolset half is
  31 * generated from the ontology by {@code ToolsetBriefing}. Nothing in the generated half can
  32 * disagree with the catalog, because it is read from the catalog on every turn.
  33 *
  34 * <p><b>Tool execution is left to the framework.</b> There is no hand-rolled call loop here,
  35 * because there is nothing to gain from one: the trace is collected inside each callback, so the
  36 * visibility a manual loop is usually written for is already there. Less machinery, same evidence.
  37 */
  38@Component
  39public class BrokerageAgent {
  40
  41
  42    private final ObjectProvider<ChatModel> chatModel;
  43    private final ToolPublisher publisher;
  44    private final BrokerageCatalog catalog;
  45
  46    public BrokerageAgent(ObjectProvider<ChatModel> chatModel, ToolPublisher publisher,
  47                          BrokerageCatalog catalog) {
  48        this.chatModel = chatModel;
  49        this.publisher = publisher;
  50        this.catalog = catalog;
  51    }
  52
  53    /** One turn: the assistant's reply, and the tools it used to get there. */
  54    public record Turn(String reply, List<ToolTrace.Step> steps, Integer promptTokens,
  55                       Integer completionTokens, String model) {
  56    }
  57
  58    public boolean available() {
  59        return chatModel.getIfAvailable() != null;
  60    }
  61
  62    public Turn ask(Sessions.Session session, String message, String model, int maxTokens) {
  63        ChatModel llm = chatModel.getIfAvailable();
  64        if (llm == null) {
  65            throw new IllegalStateException(
  66                    "No chat model is configured. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and restart.");
  67        }
  68        ToolTrace trace = new ToolTrace();
  69        List<ToolCallback> callbacks = publisher.publish(session.principal(), trace);
  70        String system = catalog.conduct() + "\n" + publisher.briefing(session.principal());
  71
  72        ChatResponse response = ChatClient.create(llm)
  73                .prompt()
  74                .system(system)
  75                .messages(List.copyOf(session.history()))
  76                .user(message)
  77                .toolCallbacks(callbacks)
  78                .options(AnthropicChatOptions.builder().model(model).maxTokens(maxTokens))
  79                .call()
  80                .chatResponse();
  81
  82        String reply = response == null || response.getResult() == null
  83                ? "" : response.getResult().getOutput().getText();
  84        session.history().add(new UserMessage(message));
  85        session.history().add(new AssistantMessage(reply == null ? "" : reply));
  86
  87        Integer prompt = null;
  88        Integer completion = null;
  89        if (response != null && response.getMetadata() != null
  90                && response.getMetadata().getUsage() != null) {
  91            prompt = response.getMetadata().getUsage().getPromptTokens();
  92            completion = response.getMetadata().getUsage().getCompletionTokens();
  93        }
  94        return new Turn(reply == null ? "" : reply, trace.steps(), prompt, completion, model);
  95    }
  96}
