   3import java.util.ArrayList;
   4import java.util.List;
   5import java.util.Map;
   6import java.util.Set;
   7import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
   8
   9import com.example.brokerage.domain.Accounts;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Principal;
  11
  12import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message;
  13import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  14
  15/**
  16 * Who is talking, and what has been said.
  17 *
  18 * <p>The entitlement set lives here, on the session, rather than being passed in with each request,
  19 * and that is the security property the whole runtime rests on. The console can ask to start a
  20 * session with a named role; it cannot ask for a scope that role does not carry, and nothing the
  21 * model emits reaches this class at all.
  22 *
  23 * <p>The three roles exist to make a point the book returns to repeatedly: the same catalog serves
  24 * all three, and each sees a different number of tools. Nothing is reconfigured and no tool is
  25 * rewritten; only the entitlements differ.
  26 */
  27@Component
  28public class Sessions {
  29
  30    /** A role, as a named set of scopes. Real systems get these from a token; this one does not. */
  31    public enum Role {
  32        /** Market data and reference only. Cannot see a single customer figure. */
  33        RESEARCH(Set.of("brokerage:reference:read", "brokerage:market-data:read")),
  34
  35        /** Everything readable about this customer. Cannot trade. */
  36        SERVICE(Set.of("brokerage:reference:read", "brokerage:market-data:read",
  37                "brokerage:accounts:read", "brokerage:balances:read",
  38                "brokerage:positions:read", "brokerage:orders:read")),
  39
  40        /** The full catalog, including the four tools that change something. */
  41        TRADING(Set.of("brokerage:reference:read", "brokerage:market-data:read",
  42                "brokerage:accounts:read", "brokerage:balances:read",
  43                "brokerage:positions:read", "brokerage:orders:read",
  44                "brokerage:orders:write"));
  45
  46        private final Set<String> entitlements;
  47
  48        Role(Set<String> entitlements) {
  49            this.entitlements = entitlements;
  50        }
  51
  52        public Set<String> entitlements() {
  53            return entitlements;
  54        }
  55    }
  56
  57    public record Session(String sessionId, Principal principal, Role role,
  58                          List<Message> history) {
  59    }
  60
  61    private final Map<String, Session> sessions = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
  62
  63    public Session open(String sessionId, Role role) {
  64        Principal principal = new Principal("user:demo", Accounts.DEMO_CUSTOMER,
  65                role.entitlements(), sessionId);
  66        Session session = new Session(sessionId, principal, role,
  67                java.util.Collections.synchronizedList(new ArrayList<>()));
  68        sessions.put(sessionId, session);
  69        return session;
  70    }
  71
  72    public Session require(String sessionId, Role fallbackRole) {
  73        Session session = sessions.get(sessionId);
  74        return session != null ? session : open(sessionId, fallbackRole);
  75    }
  76
  77    public void close(String sessionId) {
  78        sessions.remove(sessionId);
  79    }
  80
  81    public List<Session> all() {
  82        return List.copyOf(sessions.values());
  83    }
  84}

  12import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolDescriptor;

  14import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolRegistry;
  15import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolsetBriefing;

  17import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
  18import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
  19import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
  20import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;

  22import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;

  24
  25/**
  26 * The registry, over HTTP.
  27 *
  28 * <p>This controller is why the console exists and, more importantly, why it is worth building one
  29 * early. Everything here answers a question somebody will ask repeatedly during development and
  30 * forever afterwards in review: what exactly is the model shown, who can see which tool, what does
  31 * the generated briefing say today, and what does the catalog's own conformance report look like.
  32 * All of it is available without a language model and without a conversation.
  33 */
  34@RestController
  35@RequestMapping("/api/catalog")
  36public class CatalogController {
  37
  38    /** A tool as the console lists it: the governance a human needs, not the schema. */
  39    public record ToolCard(String name, String title, String catalogId, int riskTier,
  40                           String conformanceLevel, String lifecycle, boolean readOnly,
  41                           boolean destructive, boolean idempotent, boolean openWorld,
  42                           String approvalMode, List<String> entitlements, String owner,
  43                           String operation, String entity, List<String> consumes,
  44                           List<String> produces, String costClass, Integer p95LatencyMs,
  45                           Integer perMinute, String killSwitch, boolean enabled,
  46                           Double selectionAccuracy, int descriptionCharacters,
  47                           int inputProperties) {
  48    }
  49
  50    private final ToolRegistry registry;
  51    private final KillSwitches killSwitches;
  52    private final Sessions sessions;
  53
  54    public CatalogController(ToolRegistry registry, KillSwitches killSwitches, Sessions sessions) {
  55        this.registry = registry;
  56        this.killSwitches = killSwitches;
  57        this.sessions = sessions;
  58    }
  59
  60    @GetMapping
  61    public List<ToolCard> tools(@RequestParam(required = false) Sessions.Role role) {
  62        List<ToolRegistry.Entry> entries = role == null
  63                ? registry.all()
  64                : registry.visibleTo(principalFor(role));
  65        return entries.stream().map(this::card).toList();
  66    }
  67
  68    @GetMapping("/{name}")
  69    public ResponseEntity<ToolDescriptor> descriptor(@PathVariable String name) {
  70        return registry.find(name)
  71                .map(entry -> ResponseEntity.ok(entry.descriptor()))
  72                .orElseGet(() -> ResponseEntity.notFound().build());
  73    }
  74
  75    @GetMapping("/ontology")
  76    public Ontology ontology() {
  77        return registry.ontology();
  78    }
  79
  80    /**
  81     * The producer graph: which tool hands out each identifier, and what each tool needs first.
  82     * The console draws this; the briefing is generated from the same two maps.
  83     */
  84    @GetMapping("/graph")
  85    public Map<String, Object> graph() {
  86        Map<String, Object> graph = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  87        graph.put("producers", registry.ontology().producers());
  88        Map<String, Object> prerequisites = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  89        registry.all().forEach(entry ->
  90                prerequisites.put(entry.name(), registry.ontology().prerequisitesOf(entry.name())));
  91        graph.put("prerequisites", prerequisites);
  92        graph.put("unreachable", registry.ontology().unreachableIdentifiers());
  93        return graph;
  94    }
  95
  96    /** The conformance report, so a reviewer can see what the gate saw. */
  97    @GetMapping("/conformance")
  98    public List<Finding> conformance() {
  99        return registry.findings();
 100    }
 101
 102    /** The toolset half of the system prompt, exactly as the model will receive it. */
 103    @GetMapping("/briefing")
 104    public Map<String, Object> briefing(@RequestParam(defaultValue = "TRADING") Sessions.Role role) {
 105        Principal principal = principalFor(role);
 106        String text = ToolsetBriefing.forPrincipal(registry, principal);
 107        return Map.of("role", role, "visible", registry.visibleTo(principal).size(),
 108                "hidden", registry.hiddenFrom(principal), "characters", text.length(),
 109                "briefing", text);
 110    }
 111
 112    @PostMapping("/switches/{name}")
 113    public Map<String, Object> toggle(@PathVariable String name,
 114                                      @RequestParam boolean off) {
 115        if (off) {
 116            killSwitches.trip(name);
 117        } else {
 118            killSwitches.reset(name);
 119        }
 120        return Map.of("switch", name, "off", killSwitches.isOff(name),
 121                "tripped", killSwitches.tripped());
 122    }
 123
 124    private Principal principalFor(Sessions.Role role) {
 125        return sessions.open("preview-" + role, role).principal();
 126    }
 127
 128    private ToolCard card(ToolRegistry.Entry entry) {
 129        ToolDescriptor d = entry.descriptor();
 130        Governance g = entry.governance();
 131        Ontology.Capability capability = entry.capability();
 132        return new ToolCard(d.name(), d.title(), d.catalogId(), g.riskTier(),
 133                g.conformanceLevel().name(), g.lifecycle().name(),
 134                d.annotations().readOnlyHint(), d.annotations().destructiveHint(),
 135                d.annotations().idempotentHint(), d.annotations().openWorldHint(),
 136                g.approval() == null ? "none" : g.approval().mode().name(),
 137                g.entitlements(), g.owner().team(), capability.operation(), capability.entity(),
 138                capability.consumes(), capability.produces(),
 139                g.cost() == null ? null : g.cost().costClass(),
 140                g.cost() == null ? null : g.cost().p95LatencyMs(),
 141                g.rateLimit() == null ? null : g.rateLimit().perPrincipalPerMinute(),
 142                g.availability() == null ? null : g.availability().killSwitch(),
 143                g.availability() == null || !killSwitches.isOff(g.availability().killSwitch()),
 144                g.evaluation() == null ? null : g.evaluation().selectionAccuracy(),
 145                d.description().length(),
 146                d.inputSchema().path("properties").size());
 147    }
 148}

  10import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;

  19
  20/**
  21 * The conversation endpoint.
  22 *
  23 * <p>The response carries the trace alongside the reply, and the console shows both side by side.
  24 * That layout is a deliberate teaching decision: the most common way to misjudge an agent is to
  25 * read only its prose. A reply that says "you have 182,430 dollars of buying power" looks equally
  26 * trustworthy whether the model read it from a tool or produced it from the shape of the
  27 * conversation, and the trace is the only thing that tells them apart.
  28 */
  29@RestController
  30@RequestMapping("/api/chat")
  31public class ChatController {
  32
  33    public record ChatRequest(String sessionId, String message, Sessions.Role role) {
  34    }
  35
  36    public record ChatResponseBody(String sessionId, String reply, List<ToolTrace.Step> trace,
  37                                   Integer promptTokens, Integer completionTokens, String model) {
  38    }
  39
  40    private final BrokerageAgent agent;
  41    private final Sessions sessions;
  42    private final String model;
  43    private final int maxTokens;
  44
  45    public ChatController(BrokerageAgent agent, Sessions sessions,
  46                          @Value("${brokerage.agent.model:claude-opus-5}") String model,
  47                          @Value("${brokerage.agent.max-tokens:16000}") int maxTokens) {
  48        this.agent = agent;
  49        this.sessions = sessions;
  50        this.model = model;
  51        this.maxTokens = maxTokens;
  52    }
  53
  54    @GetMapping("/status")
  55    public Map<String, Object> status() {
  56        return Map.of("modelAvailable", agent.available(), "model", model,
  57                "roles", List.of(Sessions.Role.values()));
  58    }
  59
  60    @PostMapping
  61    public ResponseEntity<?> chat(@RequestBody ChatRequest request) {
  62        if (!agent.available()) {
  63            return ResponseEntity.status(503).body(Map.of("error",
  64                    "No chat model is configured. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and restart the service. "
  65                            + "Everything else in the console works without it."));
  66        }
  67        Sessions.Role role = request.role() == null ? Sessions.Role.SERVICE : request.role();
  68        Sessions.Session session = sessions.require(request.sessionId(), role);
  69        BrokerageAgent.Turn turn = agent.ask(session, request.message(), model, maxTokens);
  70        return ResponseEntity.ok(new ChatResponseBody(session.sessionId(), turn.reply(),
  71                turn.steps(), turn.promptTokens(), turn.completionTokens(), turn.model()));
  72    }
  73
  74    @DeleteMapping("/{sessionId}")
  75    public Map<String, Object> reset(@PathVariable String sessionId) {
  76        sessions.close(sessionId);
  77        return Map.of("sessionId", sessionId, "closed", true);
  78    }
  79}

agent-service/src/main/java/com/example/brokerage/agent/web/ConsoleRouting.java28 lines

   1package com.example.brokerage.agent.web;
   2
   3import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
   4import org.springframework.web.servlet.config.annotation.ViewControllerRegistry;
   5import org.springframework.web.servlet.config.annotation.WebMvcConfigurer;
   6
   7/**
   8 * Deep links into the console.
   9 *
  10 * <p>The console does its own routing, so {@code /ontology} is a path the browser understands and
  11 * the server has never heard of. Without this, opening the console at a page and refreshing gives
  12 * a 404 — which is the single most common complaint about a single-page application served from a
  13 * Spring Boot jar.
  14 *
  15 * <p>Only the four known paths are forwarded, rather than a catch-all. A catch-all would also
  16 * swallow a mistyped {@code /api} call and answer it with HTML, and debugging "why is my JSON an
  17 * HTML document" is a worse afternoon than adding a line here when a page is added.
  18 */
  19@Configuration
  20public class ConsoleRouting implements WebMvcConfigurer {
  21
  22    @Override
  23    public void addViewControllers(ViewControllerRegistry registry) {
  24        for (String page : new String[] {"catalog", "ontology", "agent", "governance"}) {
  25            registry.addViewController("/" + page).setViewName("forward:/index.html");
  26        }
  27    }
  28}

  12import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
  13import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
  14import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
  15import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
  16import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
  17import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
  18import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
  19import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
  20
  21/**
  22 * Calling a tool directly, without a model, and approving what needs approving.
  23 *
  24 * <p>The direct-invocation endpoint is the most useful debugging tool in the project. When an
  25 * agent gives a strange answer, the question is always whether the tool was wrong or the model
  26 * read it wrong, and this is how you find out in ten seconds: send the arguments the trace
  27 * recorded and look at the envelope. It is also how the console's catalog page lets a reviewer
  28 * exercise a tool while reading its descriptor.
  29 *
  30 * <p>Note that it goes through exactly the same pipeline as the model's calls. An endpoint that
  31 * bypassed validation or approval would be a second, unreviewed way into the brokerage, which is
  32 * the sort of convenience that turns up in an audit finding.
  33 */
  34@RestController
  35@RequestMapping("/api")
  36public class InvokeController {
  37
  38    public record InvokeRequest(String tool, JsonNode arguments, Sessions.Role role,
  39                                String sessionId) {
  40    }
  41
  42    public record InvokeResponse(String tool, boolean ok, long latencyMs, String approvalReference,
  43                                 JsonNode result) {
  44    }
  45
  46    private final InvocationPipeline pipeline;
  47    private final ApprovalGate approvals;
  48    private final AuditLog audit;
  49    private final Sessions sessions;
  50    private final java.util.function.Supplier<java.time.Instant> clock;
  51
  52    public InvokeController(InvocationPipeline pipeline, ApprovalGate approvals, AuditLog audit,
  53                            Sessions sessions,
  54                            java.util.function.Supplier<java.time.Instant> clock) {
  55        this.pipeline = pipeline;
  56        this.approvals = approvals;
  57        this.audit = audit;
  58        this.sessions = sessions;
  59        this.clock = clock;
  60    }
  61
  62    @PostMapping("/invoke")
  63    public InvokeResponse invoke(@RequestBody InvokeRequest request) {
  64        Sessions.Role role = request.role() == null ? Sessions.Role.TRADING : request.role();
  65        String sessionId = request.sessionId() == null ? "console" : request.sessionId();
  66        Sessions.Session session = sessions.require(sessionId, role);
  67        InvocationPipeline.Outcome outcome = pipeline.invoke(request.tool(),
  68                request.arguments() == null ? "{}" : DescriptorCodec.json(request.arguments()),
  69                session.principal());
  70        return new InvokeResponse(outcome.tool(), outcome.ok(), outcome.latencyMs(),
  71                outcome.approvalReference(), DescriptorCodec.tree(outcome.json()));
  72    }
  73
  74    @GetMapping("/approvals")
  75    public List<ApprovalGate.Pending> awaiting(@RequestParam(required = false) String sessionId) {
  76        return approvals.awaiting(sessionId);
  77    }
  78
  79    @PostMapping("/approvals/{reference}/grant")
  80    public Map<String, Object> grant(@PathVariable String reference,
  81                                     @RequestParam(defaultValue = "customer") String by) {
  82        approvals.grant(reference, by, clock.get());
  83        return Map.of("reference", reference, "granted", true, "by", by);
  84    }
  85
  86    @PostMapping("/approvals/{reference}/deny")
  87    public Map<String, Object> deny(@PathVariable String reference) {
  88        approvals.deny(reference);
  89        return Map.of("reference", reference, "granted", false);
  90    }
  91
  92    @GetMapping("/audit")
  93    public List<AuditLog.Record> auditTrail(@RequestParam(defaultValue = "50") int limit) {
  94        return audit.recent(limit);
  95    }
  96}

   1package com.example.brokerage.harness;
   2
   3import java.io.IOException;
   4import java.nio.file.Files;
   5import java.nio.file.Path;
   6import java.util.List;
   7
   8import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
   9
  10import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonInclude;
  11
  12/**
  13 * One recorded conversation: the choices Claude made, in order, and what it finally said.
  14 *
  15 * <p>A cassette is the answer to a problem every team building agents runs into about three weeks
  16 * in. Evaluating tool selection means asking a frontier model what it would do, which means a
  17 * network call, a bill, a minute of latency and a result that is not quite the same twice. Put
  18 * that in CI and the suite is slow, expensive and flaky — so it gets marked {@code @Disabled} and
  19 * the tools drift unchecked.
  20 *
  21 * <p>What the cassette holds is only the model's part: which tool it chose, with what arguments,
  22 * in what order, and the prose it ended on. The tools themselves are <em>not</em> recorded. On
  23 * replay the real pipeline runs, the real handlers run, the real schemas validate and the real
  24 * approval gate fires. So a replayed scenario still fails when somebody breaks a handler, narrows
  25 * a pattern, renames an output field or changes a risk tier — which is most of what changes.
  26 *
  27 * <p>What replay cannot catch is a change to a <em>description</em>, because the model's reading of
  28 * it is what was recorded. That is why the suite has two modes and why the live mode is wired to
  29 * descriptor changes in CI: edit a description and the cassettes for that tool are stale by
  30 * definition.
  31 *
  32 * <p>A recorded confirmation token is a dead token — single-use, long expired, and bound to a
  33 * session that no longer exists. So the recorder rewrites any token argument to the placeholder
  34 * {@value #TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER}, and on replay the harness substitutes the live token issued by the
  35 * preview that ran a moment earlier. That substitution is the one place replay is not byte for
  36 * byte, and it is the place it has to be.
  37 */
  38@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  39public record Cassette(String scenarioId, Source source, String model, String recordedAt,
  40                       String note, List<Turn> turns, String reply, Integer promptTokens,
  41                       Integer completionTokens) {
  42
  43    /**
  44     * Where this cassette came from. The distinction is published rather than implied, because a
  45     * suite that cannot tell the two apart will quietly claim evidence it does not have.
  46     */
  47    public enum Source {
  48        /** Captured from a real call to the model. Evidence of what it actually chose. */
  49        RECORDED,
  50        /**
  51         * Written by hand as the trajectory the catalog's authors intend. It exercises the whole
  52         * runtime — schemas, entitlements, the approval gate, the handlers — and it is not evidence
  53         * about the model. Run the suite with {@code --record} and an API key to replace it.
  54         */
  55        AUTHORED
  56    }
  57
  58    public Cassette {
  59        turns = turns == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(turns);
  60        source = source == null ? Source.AUTHORED : source;
  61    }
  62
  63    /** One assistant turn: the tools it asked for, or the text it ended with. */
  64    public record Turn(List<Call> calls, String text) {
  65
  66        public Turn {
  67            calls = calls == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(calls);
  68        }
  69    }
  70
  71    /** One tool call as the model emitted it. The arguments are kept verbatim, warts and all. */
  72    public record Call(String tool, String arguments) {
  73    }
  74
  75    public static Cassette read(Path file) throws IOException {
  76        return DescriptorCodec.mapper().readValue(Files.readString(file), Cassette.class);
  77    }
  78
  79    public void write(Path file) throws IOException {
  80        Files.createDirectories(file.getParent());
  81        Files.writeString(file, DescriptorCodec.mapper().writerWithDefaultPrettyPrinter()
  82                .writeValueAsString(this) + "\n");
  83    }
  84
  85    /** Stands in for a confirmation token, which cannot meaningfully be recorded. */
  86    public static final String TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER = "{{confirmationToken}}";
  87
  88    public static Path pathFor(Path directory, String scenarioId) {
  89        return directory.resolve(scenarioId + ".json");
  90    }
  91}

   1package com.example.brokerage.harness;
   2
   3import java.util.ArrayList;
   4import java.util.List;
   5import java.util.Map;
   6
   7import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
   8import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolTrace;
   9
  10import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
  11
  12/**
  13 * Checking one run against what the scenario expected.
  14 *
  15 * <p>Every assertion here is about the {@link ToolTrace} or about the reply text, and never about
  16 * the reply's wording. That constraint is deliberate and it is the thing that makes an agent suite
  17 * maintainable. Assert that a reply "mentions the buying power" and the test fails the day the
  18 * model phrases it differently, which is a Tuesday. Assert that the agent called
  19 * {@code brokerage_balances_get} with this account and did not call {@code brokerage_order_place},
  20 * and the test keeps meaning the same thing across model versions.
  21 *
  22 * <p>The one place prose is examined is {@code expectRefusal}, and even there it is a coarse check
  23 * for the shape of a refusal rather than a phrase. A better refusal check, once a team has the
  24 * appetite for it, is a second model asked a yes-or-no question about the reply; the structure
  25 * here leaves room for that without requiring it.
  26 */
  27public final class Expectations {
  28
  29    /** One failed expectation, phrased so that a developer knows what to do about it. */
  30    public record Failure(String kind, String detail) {
  31
  32        @Override
  33        public String toString() {
  34            return kind + ": " + detail;
  35        }
  36    }
  37
  38    private static final List<String> REFUSAL_MARKERS = List.of(
  39            "cannot", "can't", "not able", "unable", "not something i", "i am not",
  40            "i'm not", "not permitted", "do not", "don't provide", "not allowed",
  41            "not advice", "cannot advise", "restricted", "would need");
  42
  43    private Expectations() {
  44    }
  45
  46    public static List<Failure> check(Scenario scenario, List<ToolTrace.Step> steps, String reply) {
  47        List<Failure> failures = new ArrayList<>();
  48        List<String> path = steps.stream().map(ToolTrace.Step::tool).toList();
  49
  50        for (String expected : scenario.expectTools()) {
  51            if (!path.contains(expected)) {
  52                failures.add(new Failure("tool-not-called",
  53                        expected + " was expected but the agent called " + describe(path)));
  54            }
  55        }
  56        for (String forbidden : scenario.forbidTools()) {
  57            if (path.contains(forbidden)) {
  58                failures.add(new Failure("forbidden-tool",
  59                        forbidden + " must not be called for this utterance, but it was"));
  60            }
  61        }
  62        if (!scenario.expectOrder().isEmpty()) {
  63            int cursor = -1;
  64            for (String tool : scenario.expectOrder()) {
  65                int at = indexFrom(path, tool, cursor + 1);
  66                if (at < 0) {
  67                    failures.add(new Failure("out-of-order",
  68                            "expected " + String.join(" then ", scenario.expectOrder())
  69                                    + " but the agent called " + describe(path)));
  70                    break;
  71                }
  72                cursor = at;
  73            }
  74        }
  75        scenario.expectArguments().forEach((tool, expected) ->
  76                failures.addAll(arguments(steps, tool, expected)));
  77
  78        if (Boolean.TRUE.equals(scenario.expectRefusal()) && !looksLikeRefusal(reply)) {
  79            failures.add(new Failure("not-refused",
  80                    "the agent was expected to decline, but the reply reads as compliance: \""
  81                            + snippet(reply) + "\""));
  82        }
  83        if (scenario.maxToolCalls() != null && steps.size() > scenario.maxToolCalls()) {
  84            failures.add(new Failure("too-many-calls",
  85                    steps.size() + " tool calls where at most " + scenario.maxToolCalls()
  86                            + " was expected: " + describe(path)));
  87        }
  88        return failures;
  89    }
  90
  91    /** Argument checks are per named tool, and only the named fields are examined. */
  92    private static List<Failure> arguments(List<ToolTrace.Step> steps, String tool,
  93                                           Map<String, Object> expected) {
  94        List<Failure> failures = new ArrayList<>();
  95        List<ToolTrace.Step> calls = steps.stream()
  96                .filter(step -> step.tool().equals(tool)).toList();
  97        if (calls.isEmpty()) {
  98            failures.add(new Failure("arguments-unchecked",
  99                    tool + " was never called, so its arguments could not be checked"));
 100            return failures;
 101        }
 102        boolean anyMatched = false;
 103        for (ToolTrace.Step call : calls) {
 104            JsonNode actual = parse(call.arguments());
 105            if (expected.entrySet().stream().allMatch(entry ->
 106                    matches(actual.path(entry.getKey()), entry.getValue()))) {
 107                anyMatched = true;
 108                break;
 109            }
 110        }
 111        if (!anyMatched) {
 112            failures.add(new Failure("wrong-arguments",
 113                    tool + " was expected with " + expected + " but was called with "
 114                            + calls.stream().map(ToolTrace.Step::arguments).toList()));
 115        }
 116        return failures;
 117    }
 118
 119    private static boolean matches(JsonNode actual, Object expected) {
 120        if (expected == null) {
 121            return actual.isMissingNode() || actual.isNull();
 122        }
 123        if (expected instanceof Number number) {
 124            return actual.isNumber() && actual.asDouble() == number.doubleValue();
 125        }
 126        if (expected instanceof Boolean flag) {
 127            return actual.isBoolean() && actual.asBoolean() == flag;
 128        }
 129        if (expected instanceof List<?> options) {
 130            return options.stream().anyMatch(option -> matches(actual, option));
 131        }
 132        if (actual.isArray() || actual.isObject()) {
 133            // An array or object argument is compared as canonical JSON, so a scenario can pin
 134            // `symbols` to ["AAPL","MSFT","NVDA"] and catch an agent that called it three times.
 135            return DescriptorCodec.json(actual).equals(String.valueOf(expected));
 136        }
 137        return actual.asString("").equals(String.valueOf(expected));
 138    }
 139
 140    private static JsonNode parse(String json) {
 141        try {
 142            return DescriptorCodec.tree(json == null || json.isBlank() ? "{}" : json);
 143        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
 144            return DescriptorCodec.mapper().createObjectNode();
 145        }
 146    }
 147
 148    static boolean looksLikeRefusal(String reply) {
 149        String lower = reply == null ? "" : reply.toLowerCase();
 150        return REFUSAL_MARKERS.stream().anyMatch(lower::contains);
 151    }
 152
 153    private static int indexFrom(List<String> path, String tool, int from) {
 154        for (int i = Math.max(0, from); i < path.size(); i++) {
 155            if (path.get(i).equals(tool)) {
 156                return i;
 157            }
 158        }
 159        return -1;
 160    }
 161
 162    private static String describe(List<String> path) {
 163        return path.isEmpty() ? "no tools at all" : String.join(" then ", path);
 164    }
 165
 166    private static String snippet(String reply) {
 167        if (reply == null) {
 168            return "";
 169        }
 170        String flat = reply.replace('\n', ' ').trim();
 171        return flat.length() <= 120 ? flat : flat.substring(0, 117) + "...";
 172    }
 173}

  15import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.OrderPreviewHandler;
  16import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.OrderReplaceHandler;
  17import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.OrdersListHandler;
  18import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.PositionsListHandler;
  19import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.PriceHistoryGetHandler;
  20import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.QuotesGetHandler;
  21import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.TaxLotsListHandler;
  22import com.example.brokerage.catalog.handlers.Tickets;
  23import com.example.brokerage.domain.Accounts;
  24import com.example.brokerage.domain.Brokerage;
  25import com.example.brokerage.domain.ConfirmationTokens;
  26import com.example.brokerage.domain.Instruments;
  27import com.example.brokerage.domain.MarketClock;
  28import com.example.brokerage.domain.MarketData;
  29import com.example.brokerage.domain.Orders;
  30import com.example.brokerage.domain.RiskEngine;
  31import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolHandler;
  32import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ApprovalGate;
  33import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.AuditLog;
  34import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.InvocationPipeline;
  35import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.KillSwitches;
  36import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.RateLimiter;
  37import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolPublisher;
  38import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolRegistry;
  39
  40/**
  41 * The whole system, built by hand in one method.
  42 *
  43 * <p>No container, no profiles, no component scan. That is a deliberate property of a test harness
  44 * rather than a shortcut: a suite that boots an application context tests the application context
  45 * too, and when it fails you are debugging dependency injection instead of a descriptor. Twenty
  46 * lines of constructor calls are also the clearest statement of what the system is made of that
  47 * exists anywhere in this project.
  48 *
  49 * <p>Each harness run gets a fresh instance, so one scenario cannot leave an order in the book for
  50 * the next one to trip over. Evaluation suites that share state are the reason an agent suite
  51 * passes on its own and fails in the full run.
  52 */
  53public class HarnessContext {
  54
  55    private final BrokerageCatalog catalog;
  56    private final Brokerage brokerage;
  57    private final ToolRegistry registry;
  58    private final ApprovalGate approvals;
  59    private final AuditLog audit;
  60    private final ToolPublisher publisher;
  61
  62    public HarnessContext() {
  63        this.catalog = new BrokerageCatalog();
  64        MarketClock clock = new MarketClock();
  65        Instruments instruments = new Instruments();
  66        MarketData marketData = new MarketData(instruments, clock);
  67        Accounts accounts = new Accounts(instruments, marketData, clock);
  68        Orders orders = new Orders(clock, marketData);
  69        RiskEngine risk = new RiskEngine(accounts, instruments, marketData, clock, orders);
  70        ConfirmationTokens confirmations = new ConfirmationTokens(clock);
  71        this.brokerage = new Brokerage(accounts, instruments, marketData, orders, risk,
  72                confirmations, clock);
  73
  74        AccountGuard guard = new AccountGuard(brokerage);
  75        Tickets tickets = new Tickets(brokerage);
  76        List<ToolHandler> handlers = List.of(
  77                new AccountsListHandler(brokerage),
  78                new InstrumentsSearchHandler(brokerage),
  79                new QuotesGetHandler(brokerage),
  80                new PriceHistoryGetHandler(brokerage),
  81                new BalancesGetHandler(brokerage, guard),
  82                new PositionsListHandler(brokerage, guard),
  83                new TaxLotsListHandler(brokerage, guard),
  84                new OrdersListHandler(brokerage, guard),
  85                new OrderGetHandler(brokerage, guard),
  86                new ExecutionsListHandler(brokerage, guard),
  87                new OrderPreviewHandler(brokerage, guard, tickets),
  88                new OrderPlaceHandler(brokerage, guard, tickets),
  89                new OrderReplaceHandler(brokerage, guard),
  90                new OrderCancelHandler(brokerage, guard));
  91
  92        this.registry = new ToolRegistry(catalog.ontology(), catalog.descriptors(), handlers);
  93        this.approvals = new ApprovalGate();
  94        this.audit = new AuditLog();
  95        InvocationPipeline pipeline = new InvocationPipeline(registry, approvals,
  96                new RateLimiter(), new KillSwitches(), audit,
  97                new BrokerageApprovalContext(brokerage), clock::now);
  98        this.publisher = new ToolPublisher(registry, pipeline);
  99    }
 100
 101    public BrokerageCatalog catalog() {
 102        return catalog;
 103    }
 104
 105    public Brokerage brokerage() {
 106        return brokerage;
 107    }
 108
 109    public ToolRegistry registry() {
 110        return registry;
 111    }
 112
 113    public ToolPublisher publisher() {
 114        return publisher;
 115    }
 116
 117    public AuditLog audit() {
 118        return audit;
 119    }
 120
 121    /**
 122     * Stand in for the human on every approval.
 123     *
 124     * <p>Approving automatically in a harness is a defensible thing to do and an indefensible
 125     * thing to do silently, so it is a named method rather than a default. A trading scenario that
 126     * never reaches the place tool is not testing the place tool; a suite that approves without
 127     * saying so is not testing the approval gate. The refusal suite leaves this off, which is how
 128     * the gate itself gets covered.
 129     */
 130    public ApprovalGate autoApprovingGate() {
 131        return approvals;
 132    }
 133
 134    public void approveEverythingPending(String grantedBy) {
 135        approvals.awaiting(null).forEach(pending ->
 136                approvals.grant(pending.reference(), grantedBy, brokerage.clock().now()));
 137    }
 138}

   1package com.example.brokerage.harness;
   2
   3import java.io.IOException;
   4import java.nio.file.Files;
   5import java.nio.file.Path;
   6import java.util.ArrayList;
   7import java.util.List;
   8
   9import org.springframework.ai.anthropic.AnthropicChatModel;
  10import org.springframework.ai.anthropic.AnthropicChatOptions;
  11import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatModel;
  12
  13/**
  14 * The harness as a command.
  15 *
  16 * <pre>
  17 *   ./harness.sh                      every suite, offline, from the cassettes
  18 *   ./harness.sh --live               every suite against Claude
  19 *   ./harness.sh --record             against Claude, writing new cassettes
  20 *   ./harness.sh --suite trading      one suite
  21 * </pre>
  22 *
  23 * <p>Offline is the default, and that choice is the difference between a suite that runs on every
  24 * commit and a suite that runs when somebody remembers. A conformance gate nobody runs is a style
  25 * guide.
  26 */
  27public final class HarnessMain {
  28
  29    private static final Path SUITES = Path.of("test-harness/src/main/resources/evals");
  30    private static final Path CASSETTES = Path.of("test-harness/src/main/resources/cassettes");
  31    private static final Path REPORTS = Path.of("test-harness/target/reports");
  32
  33    private HarnessMain() {
  34    }
  35
  36    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
  37        List<String> flags = List.of(args);
  38        HarnessRunner.Mode mode = flags.contains("--record") ? HarnessRunner.Mode.RECORD
  39                : flags.contains("--live") ? HarnessRunner.Mode.LIVE : HarnessRunner.Mode.REPLAY;
  40        String only = value(flags, "--suite");
  41        String model = value(flags, "--model") == null ? "claude-opus-5" : value(flags, "--model");
  42
  43        ChatModel chatModel = mode == HarnessRunner.Mode.REPLAY ? null : anthropic(model);
  44        boolean clean = true;
  45        for (Path file : suiteFiles(only)) {
  46            Scenario.Suite suite = Scenario.read(file);
  47            List<HarnessRunner.Result> results = new ArrayList<>();
  48            for (Scenario scenario : suite.scenarios()) {
  49                HarnessContext context = new HarnessContext();   // a fresh world per scenario
  50                HarnessRunner runner = new HarnessRunner(context.publisher(),
  51                        context.autoApprovingGate(), chatModel, CASSETTES, model, 16000,
  52                        context.catalog().conduct());
  53                results.add(runner.run(scenario, mode));
  54            }
  55            Report report = Report.of(suite.name(), mode, results);
  56            System.out.println(report.text());
  57            report.write(REPORTS.resolve(suite.name() + ".json"));
  58            clean &= report.clean();
  59        }
  60        if (!clean) {
  61            System.exit(1);
  62        }
  63    }
  64
  65    private static List<Path> suiteFiles(String only) throws IOException {
  66        try (var files = Files.list(SUITES)) {
  67            return files.filter(path -> path.toString().endsWith(".json"))
  68                    .filter(path -> only == null || path.getFileName().toString().contains(only))
  69                    .sorted()
  70                    .toList();
  71        }
  72    }
  73
  74    private static ChatModel anthropic(String model) {
  75        String key = System.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY");
  76        if (key == null || key.isBlank()) {
  77            throw new IllegalStateException(
  78                    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set. Run without --live to replay the cassettes.");
  79        }
  80        return AnthropicChatModel.builder()
  81                .options(AnthropicChatOptions.builder()
  82                        .apiKey(key)
  83                        .model(model)
  84                        .maxTokens(16000)
  85                        .build())
  86                .build();
  87    }
  88
  89    private static String value(List<String> flags, String name) {
  90        int at = flags.indexOf(name);
  91        return at >= 0 && at + 1 < flags.size() ? flags.get(at + 1) : null;
  92    }
  93}

   1package com.example.brokerage.harness;
   2
   3import java.io.IOException;
   4import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
   5import java.nio.file.Path;
   6import java.time.Instant;
   7import java.util.ArrayList;
   8import java.util.List;
   9import java.util.Set;
  10
  11import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Principal;
  12import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ApprovalGate;
  13import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolCallbackHolder;
  14import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolPublisher;
  15import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolTrace;
  16
  17import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.ChatClient;
  18import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.AssistantMessage;
  19import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message;
  20import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.UserMessage;
  21import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatModel;
  22import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatResponse;
  23import org.springframework.ai.tool.ToolCallback;
  24import org.springframework.ai.anthropic.AnthropicChatOptions;
  25
  26/**
  27 * Runs one scenario, either against Claude or against a recorded cassette.
  28 *
  29 * <p>The two modes are not two test suites. They run the same scenario, against the same registry,
  30 * through the same pipeline, and check the same expectations. The only difference is where the
  31 * model's choices come from: the network, or a file recorded from the network. That is what makes
  32 * the offline suite worth trusting — it is not a mock of the system, it is the system with a
  33 * recording of the model's half of the conversation.
  34 */
  35public class HarnessRunner {
  36
  37    public enum Mode {
  38        /** Call Claude. Costs money, takes a minute, catches description regressions. */
  39        LIVE,
  40        /** Call Claude and write the cassette. */
  41        RECORD,
  42        /** Replay the cassette. Free, fast, deterministic, and runs the real tools. */
  43        REPLAY
  44    }
  45
  46    /** One scenario's outcome: the trace it produced, and what failed. */
  47    public record Result(Scenario scenario, Mode mode, List<ToolTrace.Step> steps, String reply,
  48                         List<Expectations.Failure> failures, long millis, Integer promptTokens,
  49                         Integer completionTokens) {
  50
  51        public boolean passed() {
  52            return failures.isEmpty();
  53        }
  54    }
  55
  56    private final ToolPublisher publisher;
  57    private final ApprovalGate approvals;
  58    private final ChatModel chatModel;
  59    private final Path cassettes;
  60    private final String model;
  61    private final int maxTokens;
  62    private final String conduct;
  63
  64    public HarnessRunner(ToolPublisher publisher, ApprovalGate approvals, ChatModel chatModel,
  65                         Path cassettes, String model, int maxTokens, String conduct) {
  66        this.publisher = publisher;
  67        this.approvals = approvals;
  68        this.chatModel = chatModel;
  69        this.cassettes = cassettes;
  70        this.model = model;
  71        this.maxTokens = maxTokens;
  72        this.conduct = conduct;
  73    }
  74
  75    public Result run(Scenario scenario, Mode mode) {
  76        long started = System.currentTimeMillis();
  77        Principal principal = principalFor(scenario);
  78        approvals.standInForTheHuman(scenario.approvesAutomatically() ? "harness" : null);
  79        ToolTrace trace = new ToolTrace();
  80        List<ToolCallback> callbacks = publisher.publish(principal, trace);
  81        try {
  82            return mode == Mode.REPLAY
  83                    ? replay(scenario, callbacks, trace, started)
  84                    : live(scenario, principal, callbacks, trace, mode, started);
  85        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
  86            return new Result(scenario, mode, trace.steps(), "",
  87                    List.of(new Expectations.Failure("harness-error", e.toString())),
  88                    System.currentTimeMillis() - started, null, null);
  89        }
  90    }
  91
  92    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ live
  93
  94    private Result live(Scenario scenario, Principal principal, List<ToolCallback> callbacks,
  95                        ToolTrace trace, Mode mode, long started) {
  96        if (chatModel == null) {
  97            throw new IllegalStateException(
  98                    "No chat model. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or run the suite in REPLAY mode.");
  99        }
 100        List<Message> history = new ArrayList<>();
 101        for (int i = 0; i < scenario.priorTurns().size(); i++) {
 102            history.add(i % 2 == 0 ? new UserMessage(scenario.priorTurns().get(i))
 103                    : new AssistantMessage(scenario.priorTurns().get(i)));
 104        }
 105        String system = conduct + "\n" + publisher.briefing(principal);
 106        ChatResponse response = ChatClient.create(chatModel)
 107                .prompt()
 108                .system(system)
 109                .messages(history)
 110                .user(scenario.utterance())
 111                .toolCallbacks(callbacks)
 112                .options(AnthropicChatOptions.builder().model(model).maxTokens(maxTokens))
 113                .call()
 114                .chatResponse();
 115        String reply = response == null || response.getResult() == null ? ""
 116                : String.valueOf(response.getResult().getOutput().getText());
 117        Integer prompt = null;
 118        Integer completion = null;
 119        if (response != null && response.getMetadata() != null
 120                && response.getMetadata().getUsage() != null) {
 121            prompt = response.getMetadata().getUsage().getPromptTokens();
 122            completion = response.getMetadata().getUsage().getCompletionTokens();
 123        }
 124        if (mode == Mode.RECORD) {
 125            record(scenario, trace, reply, prompt, completion);
 126        }
 127        return new Result(scenario, mode, trace.steps(), reply,
 128                Expectations.check(scenario, trace.steps(), reply),
 129                System.currentTimeMillis() - started, prompt, completion);
 130    }
 131
 132    private void record(Scenario scenario, ToolTrace trace, String reply, Integer prompt,
 133                        Integer completion) {
 134        List<Cassette.Call> calls = trace.steps().stream()
 135                .map(step -> new Cassette.Call(step.tool(), maskTokens(step.arguments())))
 136                .toList();
 137        Cassette cassette = new Cassette(scenario.id(), Cassette.Source.RECORDED, model,
 138                Instant.now().toString(), null, List.of(new Cassette.Turn(calls, reply)), reply,
 139                prompt, completion);
 140        try {
 141            cassette.write(Cassette.pathFor(cassettes, scenario.id()));
 142        } catch (IOException e) {
 143            throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
 144        }
 145    }
 146
 147    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ replay
 148
 149    /**
 150     * Replay the recorded choices through the real tools.
 151     *
 152     * <p>Each recorded call goes through the callback, which means the pipeline validates the
 153     * arguments, checks entitlements, applies the rate limit, consults the approval gate and runs
 154     * the handler, exactly as it would for a live model. The trace this produces is a real trace;
 155     * only the decisions behind it are historical.
 156     */
 157    private Result replay(Scenario scenario, List<ToolCallback> callbacks, ToolTrace trace,
 158                          long started) {
 159        Cassette cassette;
 160        try {
 161            cassette = Cassette.read(Cassette.pathFor(cassettes, scenario.id()));
 162        } catch (IOException e) {
 163            return new Result(scenario, Mode.REPLAY, List.of(), "",
 164                    List.of(new Expectations.Failure("no-cassette",
 165                            "no recording for " + scenario.id()
 166                                    + ". Run the suite with --record once, with an API key.")),
 167                    System.currentTimeMillis() - started, null, null);
 168        }
 169        ToolCallbackHolder holder = new ToolCallbackHolder(callbacks);
 170        String liveToken = null;
 171        for (Cassette.Turn turn : cassette.turns()) {
 172            for (Cassette.Call call : turn.calls()) {
 173                String arguments = liveToken == null ? call.arguments()
 174                        : call.arguments().replace(Cassette.TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER, liveToken);
 175                String envelope = holder.call(call.tool(), arguments);
 176                String issued = tokenIn(envelope);
 177                if (issued != null) {
 178                    liveToken = issued;
 179                }
 180            }
 181        }
 182        String reply = cassette.reply() == null ? "" : cassette.reply();
 183        return new Result(scenario, Mode.REPLAY, trace.steps(), reply,
 184                Expectations.check(scenario, trace.steps(), reply),
 185                System.currentTimeMillis() - started, cassette.promptTokens(),
 186                cassette.completionTokens());
 187    }
 188
 189    /** Rewrite a recorded token to the placeholder, so the recording stays replayable. */
 190    static String maskTokens(String arguments) {
 191        return arguments == null ? null
 192                : arguments.replaceAll("cnf_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{24}",
 193                        java.util.regex.Matcher.quoteReplacement(Cassette.TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER));
 194    }
 195
 196    /** The confirmation token a preview just issued, if this envelope carries one. */
 197    private static String tokenIn(String envelope) {
 198        java.util.regex.Matcher matcher = java.util.regex.Pattern
 199                .compile("\"confirmationToken\"\\s*:\\s*\"(cnf_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{24})\"")
 200                .matcher(envelope == null ? "" : envelope);
 201        return matcher.find() ? matcher.group(1) : null;
 202    }
 203
 204    private Principal principalFor(Scenario scenario) {
 205        Set<String> entitlements = switch (scenario.roleOrDefault()) {
 206            case RESEARCH -> Set.of("brokerage:reference:read", "brokerage:market-data:read");
 207            case SERVICE -> Set.of("brokerage:reference:read", "brokerage:market-data:read",
 208                    "brokerage:accounts:read", "brokerage:balances:read",
 209                    "brokerage:positions:read", "brokerage:orders:read");
 210            case TRADING -> Set.of("brokerage:reference:read", "brokerage:market-data:read",
 211                    "brokerage:accounts:read", "brokerage:balances:read",
 212                    "brokerage:positions:read", "brokerage:orders:read",
 213                    "brokerage:orders:write");
 214        };
 215        return new Principal("harness:" + scenario.id(),
 216                com.example.brokerage.domain.Accounts.DEMO_CUSTOMER, entitlements,
 217                "eval-" + scenario.id());
 218    }
 219}

   1package com.example.brokerage.harness;
   2
   3import java.io.IOException;
   4import java.nio.file.Files;
   5import java.nio.file.Path;
   6import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
   7import java.util.List;
   8import java.util.Map;
   9
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
  11import com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime.ToolTrace;
  12
  13/**
  14 * The scores, and the per-scenario detail behind them.
  15 *
  16 * <p>Four numbers, because they fail independently and a single pass rate hides which one moved.
  17 *
  18 * <ul>
  19 *   <li><b>Selection accuracy</b> — of the scenarios that expected a tool, how many got it. This
  20 *       is the one everybody measures and it is the least interesting on its own.</li>
  21 *   <li><b>Refusal accuracy</b> — of the scenarios where declining was correct, how many declined.
  22 *       An agent can score 100 percent on selection and still be unshippable because it answers
  23 *       questions it has no business answering.</li>
  24 *   <li><b>Argument accuracy</b> — of the scenarios that pinned arguments, how many matched. The
  25 *       right tool with the wrong account is not a near miss.</li>
  26 *   <li><b>Over-calling</b> — average tool calls per scenario against the budget. This is the
  27 *       number that shows up on the invoice.</li>
  28 * </ul>
  29 *
  30 * <p>Each score is published back into the governance block of the descriptors it covers, which is
  31 * what makes the {@code evaluation} field in a descriptor an assertion somebody can check rather
  32 * than a number somebody typed.
  33 */
  34public record Report(String suite, HarnessRunner.Mode mode, int scenarios, int passed, int failed,
  35                     double selectionAccuracy, double refusalAccuracy, double argumentAccuracy,
  36                     double averageToolCalls, long totalMillis, Integer totalPromptTokens,
  37                     Integer totalCompletionTokens, List<Entry> entries) {
  38
  39    public record Entry(String id, String utterance, boolean passed, List<String> path,
  40                        List<String> failures, long millis, String reply) {
  41    }
  42
  43    public static Report of(String suite, HarnessRunner.Mode mode,
  44                            List<HarnessRunner.Result> results) {
  45        int passed = (int) results.stream().filter(HarnessRunner.Result::passed).count();
  46        long millis = results.stream().mapToLong(HarnessRunner.Result::millis).sum();
  47        return new Report(suite, mode, results.size(), passed, results.size() - passed,
  48                rate(results, scenario -> !scenario.expectTools().isEmpty(), "tool-not-called"),
  49                rate(results, scenario -> Boolean.TRUE.equals(scenario.expectRefusal()),
  50                        "not-refused"),
  51                rate(results, scenario -> !scenario.expectArguments().isEmpty(),
  52                        "wrong-arguments"),
  53                results.isEmpty() ? 0
  54                        : results.stream().mapToInt(result -> result.steps().size()).average()
  55                                .orElse(0),
  56                millis,
  57                sum(results, HarnessRunner.Result::promptTokens),
  58                sum(results, HarnessRunner.Result::completionTokens),
  59                results.stream().map(Report::entry).toList());
  60    }
  61
  62    /** The share of in-scope scenarios with no failure of the given kind. */
  63    private static double rate(List<HarnessRunner.Result> results,
  64                               java.util.function.Predicate<Scenario> inScope, String kind) {
  65        List<HarnessRunner.Result> scoped = results.stream()
  66                .filter(result -> inScope.test(result.scenario())).toList();
  67        if (scoped.isEmpty()) {
  68            return Double.NaN;
  69        }
  70        long clean = scoped.stream().filter(result -> result.failures().stream()
  71                .noneMatch(failure -> failure.kind().equals(kind))).count();
  72        return Math.round(1000.0 * clean / scoped.size()) / 1000.0;
  73    }
  74
  75    private static Integer sum(List<HarnessRunner.Result> results,
  76                               java.util.function.Function<HarnessRunner.Result, Integer> field) {
  77        int total = 0;
  78        boolean any = false;
  79        for (HarnessRunner.Result result : results) {
  80            Integer value = field.apply(result);
  81            if (value != null) {
  82                total += value;
  83                any = true;
  84            }
  85        }
  86        return any ? total : null;
  87    }
  88
  89    private static Entry entry(HarnessRunner.Result result) {
  90        return new Entry(result.scenario().id(), result.scenario().utterance(), result.passed(),
  91                result.steps().stream().map(ToolTrace.Step::tool).toList(),
  92                result.failures().stream().map(Expectations.Failure::toString).toList(),
  93                result.millis(), result.reply());
  94    }
  95
  96    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ rendering
  97
  98    /** The console form: one line per scenario, then the scores. */
  99    public String text() {
 100        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
 101        out.append("  ").append(suite).append("  (").append(mode).append(")\n\n");
 102        for (Entry entry : entries) {
 103            out.append(entry.passed() ? "  pass  " : "  FAIL  ")
 104                    .append(String.format("%-36s", entry.id()))
 105                    .append(entry.path().isEmpty() ? "(no tools)"
 106                            : String.join(" > ", entry.path()))
 107                    .append('\n');
 108            for (String failure : entry.failures()) {
 109                out.append("        ").append(failure).append('\n');
 110            }
 111        }
 112        out.append('\n');
 113        out.append("  ").append(passed).append('/').append(scenarios).append(" passed\n");
 114        out.append(score("  selection accuracy", selectionAccuracy));
 115        out.append(score("  refusal accuracy  ", refusalAccuracy));
 116        out.append(score("  argument accuracy ", argumentAccuracy));
 117        out.append(String.format("  tool calls per scenario  %.2f%n", averageToolCalls));
 118        if (totalPromptTokens != null) {
 119            out.append(String.format("  tokens  %d in, %d out%n", totalPromptTokens,
 120                    totalCompletionTokens == null ? 0 : totalCompletionTokens));
 121        }
 122        out.append(String.format("  elapsed  %.1fs%n", totalMillis / 1000.0));
 123        return out.toString();
 124    }
 125
 126    private static String score(String label, double value) {
 127        return Double.isNaN(value) ? label + "  (no scenarios)\n"
 128                : String.format("%s  %.1f%%%n", label, value * 100);
 129    }
 130
 131    public Map<String, Object> summary() {
 132        Map<String, Object> summary = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 133        summary.put("suite", suite);
 134        summary.put("mode", mode);
 135        summary.put("scenarios", scenarios);
 136        summary.put("passed", passed);
 137        summary.put("selectionAccuracy", selectionAccuracy);
 138        summary.put("refusalAccuracy", refusalAccuracy);
 139        summary.put("argumentAccuracy", argumentAccuracy);
 140        summary.put("averageToolCalls", averageToolCalls);
 141        return summary;
 142    }
 143
 144    public void write(Path file) throws IOException {
 145        Files.createDirectories(file.getParent());
 146        Files.writeString(file, DescriptorCodec.mapper().writerWithDefaultPrettyPrinter()
 147                .writeValueAsString(this) + "\n");
 148    }
 149
 150    public boolean clean() {
 151        return failed == 0;
 152    }
 153}

   1package com.example.brokerage.harness;
   2
   3import java.io.IOException;
   4import java.nio.file.Files;
   5import java.nio.file.Path;
   6import java.util.List;
   7import java.util.Map;
   8
   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
  10
  11import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonInclude;
  12
  13/**
  14 * One thing a customer might say, and what the agent is expected to do about it.
  15 *
  16 * <p>Scenarios are data, in files, for the same reason descriptors are. A selection suite written
  17 * as JUnit methods is a suite only a Java developer can extend, and the people who know what a
  18 * customer will actually say are not Java developers. A scenario file can be written by the
  19 * product owner who took the support call.
  20 *
  21 * <p>The five expectation fields answer five different questions, and most scenarios set two or
  22 * three of them:
  23 *
  24 * <ul>
  25 *   <li>{@code expectTools} — did it reach for the right tool? The headline number.</li>
  26 *   <li>{@code forbidTools} — did it reach for something it should not have? Usually the more
  27 *       interesting half, and the half nobody writes.</li>
  28 *   <li>{@code expectOrder} — did it do things in the right sequence? Preview before place.</li>
  29 *   <li>{@code expectArguments} — did it get the arguments right, not just the tool?</li>
  30 *   <li>{@code expectRefusal} — did it decline, when declining was the correct answer?</li>
  31 * </ul>
  32 */
  33@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
  34public record Scenario(
  35        String id,
  36        String utterance,
  37        String why,
  38        Role role,
  39        List<String> expectTools,
  40        List<String> forbidTools,
  41        List<String> expectOrder,
  42        Map<String, Map<String, Object>> expectArguments,
  43        Boolean expectRefusal,
  44        Boolean autoApprove,
  45        Integer maxToolCalls,
  46        List<String> priorTurns,
  47        List<String> tags) {
  48
  49    /** Which entitlements the session under test holds. Mirrors the service's roles. */
  50    public enum Role { RESEARCH, SERVICE, TRADING }
  51
  52    public Scenario {
  53        expectTools = expectTools == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(expectTools);
  54        forbidTools = forbidTools == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(forbidTools);
  55        expectOrder = expectOrder == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(expectOrder);
  56        expectArguments = expectArguments == null ? Map.of() : Map.copyOf(expectArguments);
  57        priorTurns = priorTurns == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(priorTurns);
  58        tags = tags == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(tags);
  59    }
  60
  61    public Role roleOrDefault() {
  62        return role == null ? Role.TRADING : role;
  63    }
  64
  65    /**
  66     * Whether the harness should answer yes to approvals during this scenario. Off by default,
  67     * because the default question an evaluation suite should be asking about a trading tool is
  68     * whether the agent stops and asks.
  69     */
  70    public boolean approvesAutomatically() {
  71        return Boolean.TRUE.equals(autoApprove);
  72    }
  73
  74    public record Suite(String name, String description, List<Scenario> scenarios) {
  75    }
  76
  77    public static Suite read(Path file) throws IOException {
  78        return DescriptorCodec.mapper().readValue(Files.readString(file), Suite.class);
  79    }
  80
  81    public static Suite read(String json) {
  82        return DescriptorCodec.mapper().readValue(json, Suite.class);
  83    }
  84}

   1package com.example.brokerage.bridge;
   2
   3import java.io.BufferedReader;
   4import java.io.IOException;
   5import java.io.InputStreamReader;
   6import java.io.PrintStream;
   7import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
   8
   9import com.example.brokerage.domain.Accounts;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
  11import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Principal;
  12
  13import org.springframework.boot.ApplicationArguments;
  14import org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner;
  15import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
  16
  17/**
  18 * The transport: line-delimited JSON on standard input and output.
  19 *
  20 * <p>One JSON object per line in, one per line out, correlated by {@code id}:
  21 *
  22 * <pre>
  23 *   {"id":1,"method":"list_tools"}
  24 *   {"id":2,"method":"call_tool","params":{"name":"brokerage_accounts_list","arguments":{}}}
  25 *   {"id":3,"method":"approve","params":{"reference":"apr_..."}}
  26 * </pre>
  27 *
  28 * <p>This file is the entire adapter. Point the connector at a desktop client that expects
  29 * something else on the wire and this is what changes — not a descriptor, not a handler, not
  30 * the ontology, not the linter, not a test. The contract is the asset; the transport is a detail,
  31 * and keeping them in separate files is how that claim stays true rather than aspirational.
  32 *
  33 * <p>Nothing is written to standard output except protocol, ever, because standard output
  34 * <em>is</em> the channel. Logging goes to standard error, which is also where a desktop client
  35 * will show you a stack trace. It is the single most common way a connector fails on first run.
  36 */
  37@Component
  38public class BridgeLoop implements ApplicationRunner {
  39
  40    private final BridgeProtocol protocol;
  41
  42    public BridgeLoop(BridgeProtocol protocol) {
  43        this.protocol = protocol;
  44    }
  45
  46    @Override
  47    public void run(ApplicationArguments args) throws Exception {
  48        boolean trading = args.containsOption("trading");
  49        Principal principal = new Principal("desktop:local", Accounts.DEMO_CUSTOMER,
  50                BridgeProtocol.entitlements(trading), "desktop-" + System.currentTimeMillis());
  51
  52        if (args.containsOption("manifest")) {
  53            System.out.println(DescriptorCodec.mapper().writerWithDefaultPrettyPrinter()
  54                    .writeValueAsString(protocol.manifest(principal)));
  55            return;
  56        }
  57        if (args.containsOption("briefing")) {
  58            System.out.println(protocol.briefing(principal));
  59            return;
  60        }
  61        serve(principal);
  62    }
  63
  64    private void serve(Principal principal) throws IOException {
  65        PrintStream out = new PrintStream(System.out, true, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
  66        try (BufferedReader in = new BufferedReader(
  67                new InputStreamReader(System.in, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
  68            String line;
  69            while ((line = in.readLine()) != null) {
  70                if (line.isBlank()) {
  71                    continue;
  72                }
  73                out.println(DescriptorCodec.json(protocol.handle(line, principal)));
  74            }
  75        }
  76    }
  77}

  22/**
  23 * What the connector says, as distinct from how it says it.
  24 *
  25 * <p>Five methods, no input and no output. Everything about pipes, line endings and which stream
  26 * is the channel lives next door in {@link BridgeLoop}, and the split is the point: this book
  27 * claims that publishing the catalog to a different desktop client changes one file, and the claim
  28 * is only true if the protocol and the transport are two files to begin with.
  29 *
  30 * <p>It is also what makes the connector testable. A class that reads standard input cannot be
  31 * driven by a unit test without a pipe, and a connector nobody tests is a connector that fails on
  32 * the one Monday somebody tries it.
  33 */
  34@Component
  35public class BridgeProtocol {
  36
  37    /** What a connector published without {@code --trading} may do. Reads, and nothing else. */
  38    static final Set<String> READ_ONLY = Set.of("brokerage:reference:read",
  39            "brokerage:market-data:read", "brokerage:accounts:read", "brokerage:balances:read",
  40            "brokerage:positions:read", "brokerage:orders:read");
  41
  42    private final BrokerageCatalog catalog;
  43    private final ToolRegistry registry;
  44    private final InvocationPipeline pipeline;
  45    private final ApprovalGate approvals;
  46    private final java.util.function.Supplier<java.time.Instant> clock;
  47
  48    public BridgeProtocol(BrokerageCatalog catalog, ToolRegistry registry,
  49                          InvocationPipeline pipeline, ApprovalGate approvals,
  50                          java.util.function.Supplier<java.time.Instant> clock) {
  51        this.catalog = catalog;
  52        this.registry = registry;
  53        this.pipeline = pipeline;
  54        this.approvals = approvals;
  55        this.clock = clock;
  56    }
  57
  58    /**
  59     * The scopes a session gets. Fixed when the connector starts, from a command-line flag, and
  60     * never from anything that arrives on the wire — a desktop client feels like a trusted
  61     * peer and is not, because whatever is on the other end of the pipe is relaying a language
  62     * model's output.
  63     */
  64    public static Set<String> entitlements(boolean trading) {
  65        if (!trading) {
  66            return READ_ONLY;
  67        }
  68        Set<String> all = new LinkedHashSet<>(READ_ONLY);
  69        all.add("brokerage:orders:write");
  70        return all;
  71    }
  72
  73    /**
  74     * The catalog in the shape a frontier model's API takes it: a name, a description and an input
  75     * schema, per tool. Nothing is translated and nothing is renamed — which is the point of
  76     * having written the descriptors as data in the first place.
  77     *
  78     * <p>Note what is absent. The output schema, the annotations, the icons and the whole
  79     * governance block stay behind, because the model never sees them and publishing them would
  80     * cost tokens on every turn to no purpose.
  81     */
  82    public List<Map<String, Object>> manifest(Principal principal) {
  83        List<Map<String, Object>> tools = new ArrayList<>();
  84        for (ToolRegistry.Entry entry : registry.visibleTo(principal)) {
  85            ToolDescriptor descriptor = entry.descriptor();
  86            Map<String, Object> tool = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  87            tool.put("name", descriptor.name());
  88            tool.put("description", descriptor.description());
  89            tool.put("input_schema", descriptor.inputSchema());
  90            tools.add(tool);
  91        }
  92        return tools;
  93    }
  94
  95    /** The toolset half of the system prompt, for a client that wants to show or forward it. */
  96    public String briefing(Principal principal) {
  97        return ToolsetBriefing.forPrincipal(registry, principal);
  98    }
  99
 100    /**
 101     * One request, one response.
 102     *
 103     * <p>{@code approve} and {@code deny} are here because a desktop assistant is the one runtime
 104     * where the approval loop can actually close: there is a person sitting in front of it. Without
 105     * them the trading tools would be publishable but not usable, which is worse than not
 106     * publishing them — an agent that can see a tool it can never successfully call will keep
 107     * trying.
 108     */
 109    public Map<String, Object> handle(String line, Principal principal) {
 110        Map<String, Object> response = new LinkedHashMap<>();
 111        JsonNode request;
 112        try {
 113            request = DescriptorCodec.tree(line);
 114        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
 115            response.put("error", Map.of("code", "BAD_REQUEST", "message", "not JSON"));
 116            return response;
 117        }
 118        response.put("id", request.path("id").asInt(0));
 119        String method = request.path("method").asString("");
 120        JsonNode params = request.path("params");
 121        switch (method) {
 122            case "list_tools" -> response.put("result", Map.of(
 123                    "tools", manifest(principal),
 124                    "briefing", briefing(principal),
 125                    "conduct", catalog.conduct()));
 126            case "call_tool" -> {
 127                InvocationPipeline.Outcome outcome = pipeline.invoke(
 128                        params.path("name").asString(""),
 129                        DescriptorCodec.json(params.path("arguments")), principal);
 130                response.put("result", DescriptorCodec.tree(outcome.json()));
 131            }
 132            case "pending_approvals" -> response.put("result",
 133                    Map.of("pending", approvals.awaiting(principal.sessionId())));
 134            case "approve" -> {
 135                approvals.grant(params.path("reference").asString(""), "desktop-user", clock.get());
 136                response.put("result", Map.of("granted", true));
 137            }
 138            case "deny" -> {
 139                approvals.deny(params.path("reference").asString(""));
 140                response.put("result", Map.of("granted", false));
 141            }
 142            default -> response.put("error", Map.of("code", "UNKNOWN_METHOD",
 143                    "message", "no method " + method,
 144                    "methods", List.of("list_tools", "call_tool", "pending_approvals", "approve",
 145                            "deny")));
 146        }
 147        return response;
 148    }
 149}

   1package com.example.brokerage.bridge;
   2
   3import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
   4import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
   5import org.springframework.context.annotation.ComponentScan;
   6
   7/**
   8 * A local connector that presents the brokerage catalog to a desktop assistant such as Claude
   9 * Desktop.
  10 *
  11 * <p><b>What this is and is not.</b> This book specifies a tool <em>contract</em>, not a wire
  12 * protocol, and that distinction is the reason this module is as short as it is. The descriptor is
  13 * the asset. Whatever a particular desktop client expects on the wire is an adapter concern, and
  14 * the adapter here is {@link BridgeLoop}: a few dozen lines that read requests, look up a name,
  15 * and hand back an envelope. Point it at a different client and {@link BridgeLoop} is the only
  16 * file that changes — not a descriptor, not a handler, not the ontology, not the linter.
  17 *
  18 * <p>So the useful way to read this module is as a worked example of how little work publishing
  19 * to a new runtime should be, and as a demonstration of the two things that are not negotiable
  20 * wherever you publish: the schema is validated before a handler runs, and a tier 2 or 3 tool
  21 * stops at the approval gate.
  22 *
  23 * <pre>
  24 *   ./mvnw -q -pl desktop-bridge -am install -DskipTests
  25 *   java -jar desktop-bridge/target/desktop-bridge-1.0.0.jar --manifest     # the tools array
  26 *   java -jar desktop-bridge/target/desktop-bridge-1.0.0.jar                # serve on stdio
  27 * </pre>
  28 *
  29 * <p>Nothing is logged to standard output, ever, because standard output is the channel. Logging
  30 * goes to standard error, which is also where a desktop client will show you a stack trace.
  31 */
  32@SpringBootApplication
  33@ComponentScan(basePackages = "com.example.brokerage")
  34public class DesktopBridgeApplication {
  35
  36    public static void main(String[] args) {
  37        SpringApplication application = new SpringApplication(DesktopBridgeApplication.class);
  38        application.setLogStartupInfo(false);
  39        application.run(args);
  40    }
  41}
