 179/**
 180 * Everything the console knows about the service.
 181 *
 182 * <p>The role lives here as a signal rather than in each page, because it is the one piece of
 183 * state every page cares about: the whole console is a demonstration that the same catalog looks
 184 * different to different sessions, and a role that reset when you changed tabs would hide that.
 185 */
 186@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
 187export class Api {
 188  readonly role = signal<Role>('TRADING');
 189  readonly sessionId = signal<string>('console-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 9));
 190
 191  constructor(private readonly http: HttpClient) {}
 192
 193  catalog(role: Role): Observable<ToolCard[]> {
 194    return this.http.get<ToolCard[]>('/api/catalog', { params: { role } });
 195  }
 196
 197  descriptor(name: string): Observable<Record<string, unknown>> {
 198    return this.http.get<Record<string, unknown>>(`/api/catalog/${name}`);
 199  }
 200
 201  ontology(): Observable<Ontology> {
 202    return this.http.get<Ontology>('/api/catalog/ontology');
 203  }
 204
 205  graph(): Observable<Graph> {
 206    return this.http.get<Graph>('/api/catalog/graph');
 207  }
 208
 209  conformance(): Observable<Finding[]> {
 210    return this.http.get<Finding[]>('/api/catalog/conformance');
 211  }
 212
 213  briefing(role: Role): Observable<Briefing> {
 214    return this.http.get<Briefing>('/api/catalog/briefing', { params: { role } });
 215  }
 216
 217  invoke(tool: string, args: unknown): Observable<InvokeResult> {
 218    return this.http.post<InvokeResult>('/api/invoke', {
 219      tool,
 220      arguments: args,
 221      role: this.role(),
 222      sessionId: this.sessionId(),
 223    });
 224  }
 225
 226  chat(message: string): Observable<ChatReply> {
 227    return this.http.post<ChatReply>('/api/chat', {
 228      sessionId: this.sessionId(),
 229      message,
 230      role: this.role(),
 231    });
 232  }
 233
 234  chatStatus(): Observable<{ modelAvailable: boolean; model: string }> {
 235    return this.http.get<{ modelAvailable: boolean; model: string }>('/api/chat/status');
 236  }
 237
 238  resetChat(): Observable<unknown> {
 239    return this.http.delete(`/api/chat/${this.sessionId()}`);
 240  }
 241
 242  approvals(): Observable<Pending[]> {
 243    return this.http.get<Pending[]>('/api/approvals');
 244  }
 245
 246  grant(reference: string): Observable<unknown> {
 247    return this.http.post(`/api/approvals/${reference}/grant`, {});
 248  }
 249
 250  deny(reference: string): Observable<unknown> {
 251    return this.http.post(`/api/approvals/${reference}/deny`, {});
 252  }
 253
 254  audit(limit = 50): Observable<AuditRecord[]> {
 255    return this.http.get<AuditRecord[]>('/api/audit', { params: { limit } });
 256  }
 257
 258  toggleSwitch(name: string, off: boolean): Observable<unknown> {
 259    return this.http.post(`/api/catalog/switches/${name}`, null, {
 260      params: { off },
 261    });
 262  }
 263}

   1import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

   3/**
   4 * Four pages, each answering a question that is otherwise hard to answer about a tool catalog.
   5 * Lazily loaded, so the page a reviewer opens is the only one that is fetched.
   6 */
   7export const routes: Routes = [
   8  { path: '', redirectTo: 'catalog', pathMatch: 'full' },
   9  {
  10    path: 'catalog',
  11    title: 'Catalog',
  12    loadComponent: () => import('./pages/catalog').then((m) => m.CatalogPage),
  13  },
  14  {
  15    path: 'ontology',
  16    title: 'Ontology',
  17    loadComponent: () => import('./pages/ontology').then((m) => m.OntologyPage),
  18  },
  19  {
  20    path: 'agent',
  21    title: 'Agent',
  22    loadComponent: () => import('./pages/agent').then((m) => m.AgentPage),
  23  },
  24  {
  25    path: 'governance',
  26    title: 'Governance',
  27    loadComponent: () => import('./pages/governance').then((m) => m.GovernancePage),
  28  },
  29  { path: '**', redirectTo: 'catalog' },

   1import { Component, inject } from '@angular/core';
   2import { RouterLink, RouterLinkActive, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';
   3import { Api, Role } from './api';
   4
   5/**
   6 * The shell: a title, four tabs, and the role selector.
   7 *
   8 * <p>The role selector is in the shell rather than on one page because it is the console's main
   9 * point. The same fourteen descriptors, the same handlers and the same pipeline look like three
  10 * different products depending on one set of entitlements, and nothing is reconfigured to make
  11 * that happen.
  12 */
  13@Component({
  14  selector: 'app-root',
  15  imports: [RouterOutlet, RouterLink, RouterLinkActive],
  16  template: `
  17    <header>
  18      <div class="brand">
  19        <strong>Brokerage Tools</strong>
  20        <span class="faint small">tool registry &amp; agent console</span>
  21      </div>
  22      <nav>
  23        <a routerLink="/catalog" routerLinkActive="on">Catalog</a>
  24        <a routerLink="/ontology" routerLinkActive="on">Ontology</a>
  25        <a routerLink="/agent" routerLinkActive="on">Agent</a>
  26        <a routerLink="/governance" routerLinkActive="on">Governance</a>
  27      </nav>
  28      <label class="role">
  29        <span class="faint small">session</span>
  30        <select [value]="api.role()" (change)="setRole($event)">
  31          <option value="RESEARCH">RESEARCH &mdash; market data only</option>
  32          <option value="SERVICE">SERVICE &mdash; reads, no trading</option>
  33          <option value="TRADING">TRADING &mdash; the full catalog</option>
  34        </select>
  35      </label>
  36    </header>
  37    <main>
  38      <router-outlet />
  39    </main>
  40  `,
  41  styles: `
  42    header {
  43      display: flex;
  44      align-items: center;
  45      gap: 1.5rem;
  46      flex-wrap: wrap;
  47      padding: 0.7rem 1.25rem;
  48      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  49      background: var(--surface);
  50      position: sticky;
  51      top: 0;
  52      z-index: 10;
  53    }
  54    .brand { display: flex; flex-direction: column; line-height: 1.2; }
  55    nav { display: flex; gap: 0.25rem; margin-right: auto; }
  56    nav a {
  57      padding: 0.3rem 0.65rem;
  58      border-radius: var(--radius);
  59      text-decoration: none;
  60      color: var(--muted);
  61      font-size: 0.9rem;
  62    }
  63    nav a:hover { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--text); }
  64    nav a.on { background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent); font-weight: 600; }
  65    .role { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; }
  66    main { padding: 1.5rem 1.25rem 4rem; max-width: 1180px; margin: 0 auto; }
  67    @media (max-width: 720px) {
  68      header { gap: 0.7rem; }
  69      nav { width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; }
  70      main { padding: 1rem 1rem 3rem; }
  71    }
  72  `,
  73})
  74export class App {
  75  protected readonly api = inject(Api);
  76
  77  protected setRole(event: Event): void {
  78    this.api.role.set((event.target as HTMLSelectElement).value as Role);
  79  }
  80}

   1import { Component, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
   2import { Api, Pending, TraceStep } from '../api';
   3
   4interface Turn {
   5  who: 'customer' | 'assistant' | 'system';
   6  text: string;
   7  trace?: TraceStep[];
   8  promptTokens?: number | null;
   9  completionTokens?: number | null;
  10}
  11
  12/**
  13 * The agent page: the conversation on the left, the trace on the right.
  14 *
  15 * <p>That layout is the teaching point of the whole console. The most common way to misjudge an
  16 * agent is to read only its prose: a reply that says "your buying power is 579,099.35" looks
  17 * exactly as trustworthy whether the model read it from a tool or produced it from the shape of
  18 * the conversation. The trace is the only thing that tells them apart, so it is not behind a
  19 * toggle.
  20 *
  21 * <p>The approvals panel is live. When the agent reaches a tier 2 or 3 tool it gets
  22 * {@code APPROVAL_REQUIRED} and stops; the pending request appears here with the priced summary
  23 * the customer is meant to read; and the next turn can go through once it is granted. That is the
  24 * real loop, not a simulation of it.
  25 */
  26@Component({
  27  selector: 'app-agent',
  28  template: `
  29    <h1>Agent</h1>
  30    @if (!available()) {
  31      <p class="pill warn">
  32        No chat model is configured. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and restart the service. Everything else
  33        in the console works without it.
  34      </p>
  35    } @else {
  36      <p class="muted">
  37        Talking to {{ model() }} as a {{ api.role() }} session. The reply is on the left; what it
  38        actually called is on the right.
  39      </p>
  40    }
  41
  42    <div class="layout">
  43      <section class="stack">
  44        @for (turn of turns(); track $index) {
  45          <div class="turn" [class]="turn.who">
  46            <div class="faint small">{{ turn.who }}</div>
  47            <div class="text">{{ turn.text }}</div>
  48            @if (turn.promptTokens) {
  49              <div class="faint small">
  50                {{ turn.promptTokens }} tokens in, {{ turn.completionTokens }} out
  51              </div>
  52            }
  53          </div>
  54        } @empty {
  55          <div class="card">
  56            <h3 style="margin-top: 0">Try one of these</h3>
  57            @for (example of examples; track example) {
  58              <button class="small" style="margin: 0 0.3rem 0.3rem 0"
  59                      (click)="send(example)">{{ example }}</button>
  60            }
  61          </div>
  62        }
  63
  64        <div class="row">
  65          <input style="flex: 1" placeholder="Ask about the account, or ask to trade"
  66                 [value]="draft()" (input)="draft.set($any($event.target).value)"
  67                 (keydown.enter)="send(draft())" />
  68          <button class="primary" (click)="send(draft())"
  69                  [disabled]="busy() || !available()">Send</button>
  70          <button (click)="reset()">Reset</button>
  71        </div>
  72      </section>
  73
  74      <section class="stack">
  75        @if (pending().length) {
  76          <div class="card">
  77            <h3 style="margin-top: 0">Waiting for you</h3>
  78            @for (request of pending(); track request.reference) {
  79              <div class="approval">
  80                <div class="row" style="justify-content: space-between">
  81                  <code>{{ request.tool }}</code>
  82                  <span class="tier" [class]="'tier tier-' + request.riskTier">
  83                    T{{ request.riskTier }}</span>
  84                </div>
  85                <pre class="small">{{ request.summary }}</pre>
  86                <div class="row">
  87                  <button class="primary" (click)="approve(request)">Approve</button>
  88                  <button (click)="deny(request)">Decline</button>
  89                  <span class="faint small">expires {{ request.expiresAt }}</span>
  90                </div>
  91              </div>
  92            }
  93          </div>
  94        }
  95
  96        <div class="card">
  97          <h3 style="margin-top: 0">The trace</h3>
  98          @if (lastTrace().length) {
  99            @for (step of lastTrace(); track step.step) {
 100              <div class="step">
 101                <div class="row" style="justify-content: space-between">
 102                  <span><span class="faint">{{ step.step }}.</span> <code>{{ step.tool }}</code></span>
 103                  <span class="pill" [class.ok]="step.ok" [class.bad]="!step.ok">
 104                    {{ step.ok ? 'ok' : step.errorCode }} &middot; {{ step.latencyMs }}ms
 105                  </span>
 106                </div>
 107                <pre class="small">{{ pretty(step.arguments) }}</pre>
 108              </div>
 109            }
 110          } @else {
 111            <p class="faint small">
 112              Nothing yet. A turn with no tool calls is worth noticing in its own right: it means
 113              the answer came from the model rather than from your data.
 114            </p>
 115          }
 116        </div>
 117      </section>
 118    </div>
 119  `,
 120  styles: `
 121    .layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 24rem; gap: 1.5rem; align-items: start; }
 122    .turn { border-left: 3px solid var(--border-strong); padding: 0.15rem 0 0.15rem 0.75rem; }
 123    .turn.customer { border-left-color: var(--accent); }
 124    .turn.assistant { border-left-color: var(--tier-0); }
 125    .turn.system { border-left-color: var(--bad); }

 128    .step:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
 129    .step pre { margin: 0.35rem 0 0; }
 130    .approval { padding: 0.5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }
 131    .approval:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
 132    @media (max-width: 900px) { .layout { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
 133  `,
 134})
 135export class AgentPage {
 136  protected readonly api = inject(Api);
 137  protected readonly turns = signal<Turn[]>([]);
 138  protected readonly draft = signal('');
 139  protected readonly busy = signal(false);
 140  protected readonly pending = signal<Pending[]>([]);
 141  protected readonly lastTrace = signal<TraceStep[]>([]);
 142  protected readonly available = signal(false);
 143  protected readonly model = signal('');
 144
 145  protected readonly examples = [
 146    'What accounts do I have?',
 147    'How much can I spend in the everyday brokerage account?',
 148    'What am I holding, and am I too concentrated in anything?',
 149    'What would 50 Apple shares cost me?',
 150    'Buy 50 Apple at market in the everyday brokerage account',
 151    'Is Nvidia a good buy right now?',
 152    'Cancel my Microsoft order',
 153  ];
 154
 155  constructor() {
 156    this.api.chatStatus().subscribe((status) => {
 157      this.available.set(status.modelAvailable);
 158      this.model.set(status.model);
 159    });
 160    this.refreshApprovals();
 161  }
 162
 163  protected send(message: string): void {
 164    const text = message.trim();
 165    if (!text || this.busy()) {
 166      return;
 167    }
 168    this.draft.set('');
 169    this.turns.update((turns) => [...turns, { who: 'customer', text }]);
 170    this.busy.set(true);
 171    this.api.chat(text).subscribe({
 172      next: (reply) => {
 173        this.turns.update((turns) => [
 174          ...turns,
 175          {
 176            who: 'assistant',
 177            text: reply.reply,
 178            trace: reply.trace,
 179            promptTokens: reply.promptTokens,
 180            completionTokens: reply.completionTokens,
 181          },
 182        ]);
 183        this.lastTrace.set(reply.trace);
 184        this.busy.set(false);
 185        this.refreshApprovals();
 186      },
 187      error: (error) => {
 188        this.turns.update((turns) => [
 189          ...turns,
 190          { who: 'system', text: error?.error?.error ?? String(error?.message ?? error) },
 191        ]);
 192        this.busy.set(false);
 193      },
 194    });
 195  }
 196
 197  protected approve(request: Pending): void {
 198    this.api.grant(request.reference).subscribe(() => {
 199      this.refreshApprovals();
 200      this.turns.update((turns) => [
 201        ...turns,
 202        { who: 'system', text: 'You approved ' + request.tool + '. Ask the agent to go ahead.' },
 203      ]);
 204    });
 205  }
 206
 207  protected deny(request: Pending): void {
 208    this.api.deny(request.reference).subscribe(() => {
 209      this.refreshApprovals();
 210      this.turns.update((turns) => [
 211        ...turns,
 212        { who: 'system', text: 'You declined ' + request.tool + '.' },
 213      ]);
 214    });
 215  }
 216
 217  protected reset(): void {
 218    this.api.resetChat().subscribe(() => {
 219      this.turns.set([]);
 220      this.lastTrace.set([]);
 221      this.refreshApprovals();
 222    });
 223  }
 224
 225  private refreshApprovals(): void {
 226    this.api.approvals().subscribe((pending) => this.pending.set(pending));
 227  }
 228
 229  /** Arguments are shown as the model sent them, re-indented but never corrected. */
 230  protected pretty(json: string): string {
 231    try {
 232      return JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(json || '{}'), null, 1);
 233    } catch {
 234      return json;
 235    }
 236  }
 237}

   5/**
   6 * The catalog page: what the model is being shown, and what happens when you call it yourself.
   7 *
   8 * <p>The two halves are deliberate. On the left, the tools this session can see, with the
   9 * governance a human needs in order to have an opinion about them. On the right, the descriptor
  10 * verbatim — not a rendering of it, the file — and a box to call the tool with arguments you type.
  11 *
  12 * <p>That second half is the most used thing in the whole console. When an agent gives a strange
  13 * answer, the question is always whether the tool was wrong or the model read it wrong, and this
  14 * is how you find out in ten seconds: paste the arguments from the trace and look at the envelope.
  15 */
  16@Component({
  17  selector: 'app-catalog',
  18  imports: [JsonPipe],
  19  template: `
  20    <h1>Catalog</h1>
  21    <p class="muted">
  22      {{ tools().length }} of 14 tools are visible to a {{ api.role() }} session. A tool this
  23      session cannot call is not shown to the model at all &mdash; publishing one would cost tokens
  24      and buy a wrong turn.
  25    </p>
  26
  27    <div class="layout">
  28      <section>
  29        <div class="row" style="margin-bottom: 0.75rem">
  30          <input
  31            placeholder="filter by name, entity or operation"
  32            [value]="filter()"
  33            (input)="filter.set($any($event.target).value)"
  34            style="flex: 1; min-width: 12rem" />
  35          <label class="small muted row" style="gap: 0.3rem">
  36            <input type="checkbox" [checked]="writesOnly()"
  37                   (change)="writesOnly.set($any($event.target).checked)" />
  38            changes state only
  39          </label>
  40        </div>
  41
  42        @for (tool of visible(); track tool.name) {
  43          <button class="tool" [class.on]="selected() === tool.name"
  44                  (click)="select(tool.name)">
  45            <div class="row" style="justify-content: space-between; width: 100%">
  46              <code>{{ tool.name }}</code>
  47              <span class="tier" [class]="'tier tier-' + tool.riskTier">T{{ tool.riskTier }}</span>
  48            </div>
  49            <div class="small muted">{{ tool.title }}</div>
  50            <div class="row small" style="gap: 0.3rem">
  51              <span class="pill">{{ tool.operation }} / {{ tool.entity }}</span>
  52              @if (tool.readOnly) {
  53                <span class="pill ok">read-only</span>
  54              } @else {
  55                <span class="pill bad">{{ tool.approvalMode }}</span>
  56              }
  57              @if (!tool.enabled) { <span class="pill bad">switched off</span> }
  58            </div>
  59          </button>
  60        } @empty {
  61          <p class="faint">Nothing matches.</p>
  62        }
  63      </section>
  64
  65      <section>
  66        @if (card(); as tool) {
  67          <div class="card stack">
  68            <div>
  69              <h2 style="margin-top: 0">{{ tool.title }}</h2>
  70              <code class="muted">{{ tool.catalogId }}</code>
  71            </div>
  72
  73            <table>
  74              <tbody>
  75                <tr><th>risk tier</th><td>
  76                  <span class="tier" [class]="'tier tier-' + tool.riskTier">T{{ tool.riskTier }}</span>
  77                  &nbsp;approval: {{ tool.approvalMode }}
  78                </td></tr>
  79                <tr><th>conformance</th><td>{{ tool.conformanceLevel }} &middot; {{ tool.lifecycle }}</td></tr>
  80                <tr><th>annotations</th><td>
  81                  readOnly {{ tool.readOnly }} &middot; destructive {{ tool.destructive }}
  82                  &middot; idempotent {{ tool.idempotent }} &middot; openWorld {{ tool.openWorld }}
  83                </td></tr>
  84                <tr><th>entitlements</th><td><code>{{ tool.entitlements.join(', ') }}</code></td></tr>
  85                <tr><th>owner</th><td>{{ tool.owner }}</td></tr>
  86                <tr><th>consumes</th><td>{{ tool.consumes.join(', ') || '&mdash;' }}</td></tr>
  87                <tr><th>produces</th><td>{{ tool.produces.join(', ') || '&mdash;' }}</td></tr>
  88                <tr><th>budget</th><td>
  89                  {{ tool.costClass }} &middot; p95 {{ tool.p95LatencyMs }}ms
  90                  &middot; {{ tool.perMinute }}/min
  91                </td></tr>
  92                <tr><th>description</th><td>{{ tool.descriptionCharacters }} characters,
  93                  {{ tool.inputProperties }} parameters</td></tr>
  94                @if (tool.selectionAccuracy !== null) {
  95                  <tr><th>last evaluated</th><td>
  96                    selection accuracy {{ (tool.selectionAccuracy * 100).toFixed(0) }}%
  97                  </td></tr>
  98                }
  99              </tbody>
 100            </table>
 101
 102            <div>
 103              <h3>Call it</h3>
 104              <p class="small muted">
 105                This goes through the same pipeline the model's calls go through: the schema is
 106                validated, entitlements are checked, and a tier 2 or 3 tool still stops at the
 107                approval gate. There is no back door.
 108              </p>
 109              <textarea rows="5" style="width: 100%" [value]="args()"
 110                        (input)="args.set($any($event.target).value)"></textarea>
 111              <div class="row" style="margin-top: 0.5rem">
 112                <button class="primary" (click)="call()" [disabled]="running()">

 115                @if (result(); as outcome) {

 123              }
 124            </div>
 125
 126            <div>
 127              <h3>The descriptor, verbatim</h3>
 128              <p class="small muted">
 129                This is the file, not a rendering of it. The four fields at the top are what the
 130                model sees; everything under <code>_meta</code> never reaches it.
 131              </p>
 132              <pre>{{ descriptor() | json }}</pre>
 133            </div>
 134          </div>
 135        } @else {
 136          <p class="faint">Pick a tool.</p>
 137        }
 138      </section>
 139    </div>
 140  `,
 141  styles: `
 142    .layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 22rem 1fr; gap: 1.5rem; align-items: start; }
 143    .tool {
 144      display: flex;
 145      flex-direction: column;
 146      align-items: flex-start;
 147      gap: 0.25rem;
 148      width: 100%;
 149      text-align: left;
 150      margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
 151      padding: 0.6rem 0.7rem;
 152      border-color: var(--border);
 153    }
 154    .tool.on { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); }
 155    th { width: 9rem; border-bottom-color: var(--border); }
 156    @media (max-width: 900px) { .layout { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
 157  `,
 158})
 159export class CatalogPage {
 160  protected readonly api = inject(Api);
 161  protected readonly tools = signal<ToolCard[]>([]);
 162  protected readonly filter = signal('');
 163  protected readonly writesOnly = signal(false);
 164  protected readonly selected = signal<string | null>(null);
 165  protected readonly descriptor = signal<unknown>(null);
 166  protected readonly args = signal('{}');
 167  protected readonly result = signal<InvokeResult | null>(null);
 168  protected readonly running = signal(false);
 169
 170  protected readonly visible = computed(() => {
 171    const needle = this.filter().toLowerCase();
 172    return this.tools().filter(
 173      (tool) =>
 174        (!this.writesOnly() || !tool.readOnly) &&
 175        (needle === '' ||
 176          tool.name.includes(needle) ||
 177          tool.entity.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
 178          tool.operation.includes(needle)),
 179    );
 180  });
 181
 182  protected readonly card = computed(() =>
 183    this.tools().find((tool) => tool.name === this.selected()) ?? null,
 184  );
 185
 186  constructor() {
 187    // Reloads whenever the role changes, which is the behavior the page is there to show.
 188    effect(() => {
 189      const role = this.api.role();
 190      this.api.catalog(role).subscribe((tools) => {
 191        this.tools.set(tools);
 192        if (!tools.some((tool) => tool.name === this.selected())) {
 193          this.select(tools[0]?.name ?? null);
 194        }
 195      });
 196    });
 197  }
 198
 199  protected select(name: string | null): void {
 200    this.selected.set(name);
 201    this.result.set(null);
 202    this.descriptor.set(null);
 203    if (!name) {
 204      return;
 205    }
 206    this.api.descriptor(name).subscribe((descriptor) => {
 207      this.descriptor.set(descriptor);
 208      this.args.set(JSON.stringify(this.exampleFor(descriptor), null, 2));
 209    });
 210  }
 211
 212  /**
 213   * A starting point for the arguments box, built from the input schema's required fields and
 214   * whatever example the schema offers. It is a convenience, not a validator: whatever is typed
 215   * here goes to the real pipeline and gets the real answer.
 216   */
 217  private exampleFor(descriptor: any): Record<string, unknown> {
 218    const schema = descriptor?.inputSchema ?? {};
 219    const example: Record<string, unknown> = {};
 220    for (const name of schema.required ?? []) {
 221      const property = schema.properties?.[name] ?? {};
 222      example[name] = this.sampleFor(property);
 223    }
 224    return example;
 225  }
 226
 227  private sampleFor(property: any): unknown {
 228    if (property.enum) {
 229      return property.enum[0];
 230    }
 231    if (property.type === 'integer' || property.type === 'number') {
 232      return property.minimum ?? 1;
 233    }
 234    if (property.type === 'array') {
 235      return [this.sampleFor(property.items ?? {})];
 236    }
 237    if (property.type === 'boolean') {
 238      return false;
 239    }
 240    return property.examples?.[0] ?? '';
 241  }
 242
 243  protected call(): void {
 244    const name = this.selected();
 245    if (!name) {
 246      return;
 247    }
 248    let parsed: unknown;
 249    try {
 250      parsed = JSON.parse(this.args() || '{}');
 251    } catch {
 252      this.result.set({
 253        tool: name,
 254        ok: false,
 255        latencyMs: 0,
 256        approvalReference: null,
 257        result: { error: 'The arguments box does not contain valid JSON.' },
 258      });
 259      return;
 260    }
 261    this.running.set(true);
 262    this.api.invoke(name, parsed).subscribe({
 263      next: (outcome) => {
 264        this.result.set(outcome);
 265        this.running.set(false);
 266      },
 267      error: (error) => {
 268        this.result.set({
 269          tool: name,
 270          ok: false,
 271          latencyMs: 0,
 272          approvalReference: null,
 273          result: { error: String(error?.message ?? error) },
 274        });
 275        this.running.set(false);
 276      },
 277    });
 278  }
 279}

   1import { Component, computed, effect, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
   2import { Api, AuditRecord, Briefing, Finding, ToolCard } from '../api';
   3
   4/**
   5 * The governance page: what a reviewer, a risk officer or an auditor turns up asking for.
   6 *
   7 * <p>Four things, each of which is usually buried in a log or a build output.
   8 *
   9 * <p>The <strong>conformance report</strong> is the output of the gate that runs at startup, so
  10 * what the registry refused to serve is visible rather than inferred from a stack trace.
  11 *
  12 * <p>The <strong>generated briefing</strong> is the system prompt as the model will receive it,
  13 * today, for this role. Not a copy kept in a wiki — the thing itself.
  14 *
  15 * <p>The <strong>kill switches</strong> are live. Trip one and the tool leaves the catalog on the
  16 * next turn; the agent does not see it, so there is no error to retry.
  17 *
  18 * <p>The <strong>audit trail</strong> shows what was called, by whom, with which approval, and
  19 * under what retention. Argument names appear; argument values never do.
  20 */
  21@Component({
  22  selector: 'app-governance',
  23  template: `
  24    <h1>Governance</h1>
  25
  26    <h2>Conformance</h2>
  27    @if (findings().length === 0) {
  28      <p class="pill ok">
  29        14 descriptors &middot; 0 errors &middot; 0 warnings. The registry refuses to start
  30        otherwise.
  31      </p>
  32    } @else {
  33      <table>
  34        <thead><tr><th>rule</th><th>severity</th><th>tool</th><th>finding</th></tr></thead>
  35        <tbody>
  36          @for (finding of findings(); track finding.rule + finding.tool + finding.message) {
  37            <tr>
  38              <td><code>{{ finding.rule }}</code></td>
  39              <td><span class="pill" [class.bad]="finding.severity === 'ERROR'"
  40                        [class.warn]="finding.severity === 'WARNING'">
  41                {{ finding.severity }}</span></td>
  42              <td><code class="small">{{ finding.tool }}</code>
  43                @if (finding.where) { <div class="faint small">{{ finding.where }}</div> }
  44              </td>
  45              <td class="small">{{ finding.message }}</td>
  46            </tr>
  47          }
  48        </tbody>
  49      </table>
  50    }
  51
  52    <h2>Evaluation</h2>
  53    <p class="muted small">
  54      Read from each descriptor's governance block, which is where the suite writes its scores. A
  55      tier 2 or 3 tool that cites no suite does not pass the linter, which is how these numbers
  56      stay attached to something.
  57    </p>
  58    <table>
  59      <thead>
  60        <tr><th>tool</th><th>tier</th><th>level</th><th>selection accuracy</th><th>switch</th></tr>
  61      </thead>
  62      <tbody>
  63        @for (tool of tools(); track tool.name) {
  64          <tr>
  65            <td><code>{{ tool.name }}</code></td>
  66            <td><span class="tier" [class]="'tier tier-' + tool.riskTier">T{{ tool.riskTier }}</span></td>
  67            <td>{{ tool.conformanceLevel }}</td>
  68            <td>
  69              @if (tool.selectionAccuracy !== null) {
  70                {{ (tool.selectionAccuracy * 100).toFixed(0) }}%
  71              } @else {
  72                <span class="faint">not measured</span>
  73              }
  74            </td>
  75            <td class="small">
  76              @if (tool.killSwitch) {
  77                <label class="row" style="gap: 0.35rem">
  78                  <input type="checkbox" [checked]="!tool.enabled"
  79                         (change)="toggle(tool, $any($event.target).checked)" />
  80                  <code>{{ tool.killSwitch }}</code>
  81                </label>
  82              } @else {
  83                <span class="faint">none</span>
  84              }
  85            </td>
  86          </tr>
  87        }
  88      </tbody>
  89    </table>
  90
  91    <h2>The generated briefing</h2>
  92    @if (briefing(); as brief) {
  93      <p class="muted small">
  94        {{ brief.characters }} characters, {{ brief.visible }} tools visible to a
  95        {{ brief.role }} session. Generated from the ontology on every turn, so nothing in it can
  96        disagree with the catalog. Per-tool advice is deliberately absent: that belongs in each
  97        descriptor, where it is reviewed and versioned with the tool.
  98      </p>
  99      <pre>{{ brief.briefing }}</pre>
 100      @if (hidden().length) {
 101        <p class="small muted">
 102          Hidden from this role: @for (entry of hidden(); track entry.tool) {
 103            <code>{{ entry.tool }}</code><span class="faint"> ({{ entry.missing.join(', ') }})</span>
 104            @if (!$last) { <span>, </span> }
 105          }
 106        </p>
 107      }
 108    }
 109
 110    <h2>Audit trail</h2>
 111    <p class="muted small">
 112      Written before the handler runs and completed after, so a call that hangs still leaves
 113      evidence it was attempted. Argument names are recorded; values are not.
 114    </p>
 115    <div class="row" style="margin-bottom: 0.5rem">
 116      <button (click)="refresh()">Refresh</button>
 117      <span class="faint small">{{ audit().length }} records</span>
 118    </div>
 119    <table>
 120      <thead>
 121        <tr>
 122          <th>when</th><th>tool</th><th>tier</th><th>outcome</th><th>arguments</th>
 123          <th>approval</th><th>retention</th><th>ms</th>
 124        </tr>
 125      </thead>
 126      <tbody>
 127        @for (record of audit(); track record.requestId) {
 128          <tr>
 129            <td class="small faint">{{ record.at }}</td>
 130            <td><code class="small">{{ record.tool }}</code>
 131              <div class="faint small">{{ record.auditEvent }}</div>
 132            </td>
 133            <td><span class="tier" [class]="'tier tier-' + record.riskTier">
 134              T{{ record.riskTier }}</span></td>
 135            <td>
 136              <span class="pill" [class.ok]="record.outcome === 'OK'"
 137                    [class.bad]="record.outcome !== 'OK'">{{ record.outcome }}</span>
 138            </td>
 139            <td class="small faint">{{ record.argumentFields.join(', ') || '&mdash;' }}</td>
 140            <td class="small">
 141              @if (record.approval) {
 142                <code>{{ record.approval }}</code>
 143                <div class="faint">{{ record.approvalMode }}</div>
 144              } @else {
 145                <span class="faint">&mdash;</span>
 146              }
 147            </td>
 148            <td class="small faint">{{ record.retention }}</td>
 149            <td class="small faint">{{ record.latencyMs }}</td>
 150          </tr>
 151        } @empty {
 152          <tr><td colspan="8" class="faint">
 153            Nothing yet. Call a tool from the Catalog page, or talk to the agent.
 154          </td></tr>
 155        }
 156      </tbody>
 157    </table>
 158  `,
 159  styles: `
 160    table { margin-bottom: 1.5rem; }
 161    pre { max-height: 28rem; overflow-y: auto; }
 162  `,
 163})
 164export class GovernancePage {
 165  private readonly api = inject(Api);
 166  protected readonly findings = signal<Finding[]>([]);
 167  protected readonly tools = signal<ToolCard[]>([]);
 168  protected readonly briefing = signal<Briefing | null>(null);
 169  protected readonly audit = signal<AuditRecord[]>([]);
 170
 171  protected readonly hidden = computed(() => {
 172    const brief = this.briefing();
 173    return brief
 174      ? Object.entries(brief.hidden).map(([tool, missing]) => ({ tool, missing }))
 175      : [];
 176  });
 177
 178  constructor() {
 179    this.api.conformance().subscribe((findings) => this.findings.set(findings));
 180    effect(() => {
 181      const role = this.api.role();
 182      this.api.briefing(role).subscribe((brief) => this.briefing.set(brief));
 183      this.api.catalog('TRADING').subscribe((tools) => this.tools.set(tools));
 184    });
 185    this.refresh();
 186  }
 187
 188  protected refresh(): void {
 189    this.api.audit(50).subscribe((records) => this.audit.set(records));
 190  }
 191
 192  protected toggle(tool: ToolCard, off: boolean): void {
 193    if (!tool.killSwitch) {
 194      return;
 195    }
 196    this.api.toggleSwitch(tool.killSwitch, off).subscribe(() => {
 197      this.api.catalog('TRADING').subscribe((tools) => this.tools.set(tools));
 198    });
 199  }
 200}

   1import { Component, computed, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
   2import { Api, Capability, Graph, Ontology } from '../api';
   3
   4/**
   5 * The ontology page: what this catalog is supposed to cover, and what has to happen before what.
   6 *
   7 * <p>Two things here are worth a reviewer's time and are not visible anywhere else.
   8 *
   9 * <p>The <strong>capability table</strong> is the catalog's specification. Each row is an
  10 * (operation, entity) pair with the identifiers it needs and the identifiers it hands back, and
  11 * the tool name is derived from the row rather than chosen. A question like "is this catalog
  12 * complete" becomes a question about this table instead of a question about somebody's memory.
  13 *
  14 * <p>The <strong>producer graph</strong> is the answer to "how does the agent know what to call
  15 * first". It is drawn from the same two maps the generated system briefing is written from, so
  16 * what the picture says and what the model is told cannot disagree. The edge from
  17 * {@code brokerage_order_preview} to the three tools that change something is the one to look at:
  18 * it is why preview-before-place is structural here rather than advisory.
  19 */
  20@Component({
  21  selector: 'app-ontology',
  22  template: `
  23    @if (ontology(); as model) {
  24      <h1>{{ model.id }} <span class="faint small">v{{ model.version }}</span></h1>
  25      <p class="muted">{{ model.description }}</p>
  26
  27      <h2>Identifier types</h2>
  28      <p class="muted small">
  29        Declared once, referenced by every schema. This is what stops one descriptor accepting
  30        <code>^acct_[A-Z0-9]+$</code> while its neighbour accepts <code>^ACC-\\d&#123;4&#125;$</code>.
  31      </p>
  32      <table>
  33        <thead>
  34          <tr><th>type</th><th>pattern</th><th>example</th><th>produced by</th></tr>
  35        </thead>
  36        <tbody>
  37          @for (entry of identifiers(); track entry.name) {
  38            <tr>
  39              <td><code>{{ entry.name }}</code>
  40                @if (entry.opaque) { <span class="pill">opaque</span> }
  41              </td>
  42              <td><code class="small">{{ entry.pattern }}</code></td>
  43              <td><code class="small">{{ entry.example }}</code></td>
  44              <td class="small">
  45                @if (entry.producers.length) {
  46                  @for (tool of entry.producers; track tool) {
  47                    <div><code>{{ tool }}</code></div>
  48                  }
  49                } @else {
  50                  <span class="pill bad">nothing</span>
  51                }
  52              </td>
  53            </tr>
  54          }
  55        </tbody>
  56      </table>
  57
  58      <h2>The capability table</h2>
  59      <p class="muted small">
  60        The tool name is derived from the entity and the operation, which is why
  61        <code>brokerage_order_cancel</code> could not have been called <code>cancelOrder</code>.
  62        The risk tier comes from the operation, and every exception is an override with a note.
  63      </p>
  64      <table>
  65        <thead>
  66          <tr>
  67            <th>tool</th><th>operation</th><th>entity</th><th>card.</th>
  68            <th>consumes</th><th>produces</th><th>tier</th>
  69          </tr>
  70        </thead>
  71        <tbody>
  72          @for (capability of model.capabilities; track capability.tool) {
  73            <tr>
  74              <td><code>{{ capability.tool }}</code>
  75                @if (capability.note) {
  76                  <div class="faint small">{{ capability.note }}</div>
  77                }
  78              </td>
  79              <td>{{ capability.operation }}</td>
  80              <td>{{ capability.entity }}</td>
  81              <td class="faint">{{ capability.cardinality }}</td>
  82              <td class="small">{{ capability.consumes.join(', ') || '&mdash;' }}</td>
  83              <td class="small">{{ capability.produces.join(', ') || '&mdash;' }}</td>
  84              <td>
  85                <span class="tier"
  86                      [class]="'tier tier-' + tierOf(capability)">T{{ tierOf(capability) }}</span>
  87              </td>
  88            </tr>
  89          }
  90        </tbody>
  91      </table>
  92
  93      <h2>The producer graph</h2>
  94      <p class="muted small">
  95        An arrow from A to B means B needs a value only A can give it. Read the right-hand column
  96        first: three tools change something, and all three sit behind
  97        <code>brokerage_order_preview</code>.
  98      </p>
  99      @if (graph(); as edges) {
 100        <div class="card" style="overflow-x: auto">
 101          <svg [attr.viewBox]="'0 0 860 ' + height()" [attr.height]="height()"
 102               width="100%" role="img"
 103               aria-label="Which tool produces the identifiers each other tool needs">
 104            <defs>
 105              <marker id="arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5"
 106                      markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
 107                <path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.45" />
 108              </marker>
 109            </defs>
 110            @for (edge of lines(); track edge.key) {
 111              <path [attr.d]="edge.path" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1"
 112                    opacity="0.35" marker-end="url(#arrow)" />
 113            }
 114            @for (node of nodes(); track node.name) {
 115              <g>
 116                <!-- Two rects: an opaque base so the edges behind do not show through the label,
 117                     then the tier tint on top of it. -->
 118                <rect [attr.x]="node.x" [attr.y]="node.y" [attr.width]="node.width" height="26"
 119                      rx="4" fill="var(--surface)" />
 120                <rect [attr.x]="node.x" [attr.y]="node.y" [attr.width]="node.width" height="26"
 121                      rx="4" [attr.fill]="'var(--tier-' + node.tier + ')'" opacity="0.16"
 122                      [attr.stroke]="'var(--tier-' + node.tier + ')'" stroke-width="1" />
 123                <text [attr.x]="node.x + 9" [attr.y]="node.y + 17"
 124                      font-family="var(--mono)" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">
 125                  {{ node.label }}
 126                </text>
 127              </g>
 128            }
 129            @for (column of columns(); track column.x) {
 130              <text [attr.x]="column.x" y="14" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.5"
 131                    font-family="var(--sans)">{{ column.label }}</text>
 132            }
 133          </svg>
 134        </div>
 135        @if (edges.unreachable.length) {
 136          <p class="pill bad">
 137            Unreachable identifiers: {{ edges.unreachable.join(', ') }}
 138          </p>
 139        }
 140      }
 141
 142      <h2>Entities</h2>
 143      <table>
 144        <thead>
 145          <tr><th>entity</th><th>terms</th><th>identifier</th><th>classification</th>
 146              <th>entitlement</th><th>relations</th></tr>
 147        </thead>
 148        <tbody>
 149          @for (entity of entities(); track entity.name) {
 150            <tr>
 151              <td><strong>{{ entity.label }}</strong>
 152                <div class="faint small">{{ entity.description }}</div>
 153              </td>
 154              <td class="small"><code>{{ entity.term }}</code> /
 155                <code>{{ entity.collectionTerm }}</code></td>
 156              <td class="small"><code>{{ entity.identifier }}</code></td>
 157              <td class="small">{{ entity.classification }}</td>
 158              <td class="small"><code>{{ entity.entitlement }}</code></td>
 159              <td class="small">
 160                @for (relation of entity.relations; track relation.name) {
 161                  <div>{{ relation.name }} &rarr; {{ relation.target }}</div>
 162                }
 163              </td>
 164            </tr>
 165          }
 166        </tbody>
 167      </table>
 168
 169      <h2>Operations</h2>
 170      <table>
 171        <thead><tr><th>verb</th><th>base tier</th><th>read-only</th><th>what it means</th></tr></thead>
 172        <tbody>
 173          @for (operation of operations(); track operation.name) {
 174            <tr>
 175              <td><code>{{ operation.name }}</code></td>
 176              <td><span class="tier" [class]="'tier tier-' + operation.baseRiskTier">
 177                T{{ operation.baseRiskTier }}</span></td>
 178              <td>{{ operation.readOnly ? 'yes' : 'no' }}</td>
 179              <td>
 180                {{ operation.gloss }}
 181                <div class="faint small">{{ operation.semantics }}</div>
 182              </td>
 183            </tr>
 184          }
 185        </tbody>
 186      </table>
 187    } @else {
 188      <p class="faint">Loading the ontology...</p>
 189    }
 190  `,
 191  styles: `
 192    th { border-bottom-color: var(--border-strong); }
 193    table { margin-bottom: 1.5rem; }
 194    svg { display: block; min-width: 860px; }
 195  `,
 196})
 197export class OntologyPage {
 198  private readonly api = inject(Api);
 199  protected readonly ontology = signal<Ontology | null>(null);
 200  protected readonly graph = signal<Graph | null>(null);
 201
 202  /** Column x positions, one per step in the chain the agent walks. */
 203  private static readonly COLUMNS = [
 204    { x: 8, label: 'needs nothing' },
 205    { x: 226, label: 'needs an account or a symbol' },
 206    { x: 444, label: 'needs an order' },
 207    { x: 662, label: 'needs a confirmation' },
 208  ];
 209
 210  constructor() {
 211    this.api.ontology().subscribe((model) => this.ontology.set(model));
 212    this.api.graph().subscribe((graph) => this.graph.set(graph));
 213  }
 214
 215  protected readonly identifiers = computed(() => {
 216    const model = this.ontology();
 217    const producers = this.graph()?.producers ?? {};
 218    if (!model) {
 219      return [];
 220    }
 221    return Object.entries(model.identifierTypes).map(([name, value]) => ({
 222      name,
 223      pattern: value.pattern,
 224      example: value.example,
 225      opaque: value.opaque,
 226      producers: producers[name] ?? [],
 227    }));
 228  });
 229
 230  protected readonly entities = computed(() => {
 231    const model = this.ontology();
 232    return model
 233      ? Object.entries(model.entities).map(([name, value]) => ({ name, ...value }))
 234      : [];
 235  });
 236
 237  protected readonly operations = computed(() => {
 238    const model = this.ontology();
 239    return model
 240      ? Object.entries(model.operations).map(([name, value]) => ({ name, ...value }))
 241      : [];
 242  });
 243
 244  protected tierOf(capability: Capability): number {
 245    const model = this.ontology();
 246    return capability.riskTier ?? model?.operations[capability.operation]?.baseRiskTier ?? 0;
 247  }
 248
 249  /**
 250   * Lay the tools out in columns by how far they are from needing nothing, which is the order an
 251   * agent discovers them in. A tool with no prerequisites is column 0; everything else is one
 252   * past the deepest tool it depends on.
 253   */
 254  protected readonly nodes = computed(() => {
 255    const model = this.ontology();
 256    const prerequisites = this.graph()?.prerequisites ?? {};
 257    if (!model) {
 258      return [];
 259    }
 260    const depth = new Map<string, number>();
 261    const depthOf = (tool: string, seen: Set<string>): number => {
 262      if (depth.has(tool)) {
 263        return depth.get(tool)!;
 264      }
 265      if (seen.has(tool)) {
 266        return 0;
 267      }
 268      seen.add(tool);
 269      const needs = (prerequisites[tool] ?? []).filter((other) => other !== tool);
 270      const value = needs.length
 271        ? Math.min(3, 1 + Math.max(...needs.map((other) => depthOf(other, seen))))
 272        : 0;
 273      depth.set(tool, value);
 274      return value;
 275    };
 276
 277    const rows = new Map<number, number>();
 278    return model.capabilities.map((capability) => {
 279      const column = depthOf(capability.tool, new Set());
 280      const row = rows.get(column) ?? 0;
 281      rows.set(column, row + 1);
 282      const layout = OntologyPage.COLUMNS[column];
 283      return {
 284        name: capability.tool,
 285        label: capability.tool.replace('brokerage_', ''),
 286        tier: this.tierOf(capability),
 287        x: layout.x,
 288        y: 26 + row * 34,
 289        width: 186,
 290      };
 291    });
 292  });
 293
 294  protected readonly height = computed(() => {
 295    const nodes = this.nodes();
 296    return nodes.length ? Math.max(...nodes.map((node) => node.y)) + 44 : 80;
 297  });
 298
 299  protected readonly columns = computed(() =>
 300    OntologyPage.COLUMNS.filter((column) => this.nodes().some((node) => node.x === column.x)),
 301  );
 302
 303  protected readonly lines = computed(() => {
 304    const prerequisites = this.graph()?.prerequisites ?? {};
 305    const byName = new Map(this.nodes().map((node) => [node.name, node]));
 306    const edges: { key: string; path: string }[] = [];
 307    for (const [tool, needs] of Object.entries(prerequisites)) {
 308      const target = byName.get(tool);
 309      if (!target) {
 310        continue;
 311      }
 312      for (const need of needs) {
 313        const source = byName.get(need);
 314        // Only draw the edges that move rightward: the backward ones are the same fact again.
 315        if (!source || source.x >= target.x) {
 316          continue;
 317        }
 318        const x1 = source.x + source.width;
 319        const y1 = source.y + 13;
 320        const x2 = target.x;
 321        const y2 = target.y + 13;
 322        const bend = (x2 - x1) / 2;
 323        edges.push({
 324          key: need + '>' + tool,
 325          path: `M ${x1} ${y1} C ${x1 + bend} ${y1}, ${x2 - bend} ${y2}, ${x2 - 3} ${y2}`,
 326        });
 327      }
 328    }
 329    return edges;
 330  });
 331}

   1/*
   2 * One stylesheet, tokens first.
   3 *
   4 * The console has a job rather than a look: it has to make a JSON Schema, a risk tier and a tool
   5 * trace readable by somebody who is deciding whether to approve a catalog. So the palette is
   6 * almost entirely neutral, and the only colors that carry meaning are the four risk tiers and the
   7 * three outcome states. Anything else colored would compete with them.
   8 */

  11class ErrorTaxonomyTest {

  19    @Test
  20    @DisplayName("every code tells the agent what to do, in the imperative")
  21    void everyCodeCarriesGuidance() {

  24        }
  25    }

  27    @Test
  28    @DisplayName("a terminal code is neither retryable nor the caller's to fix")
  29    void terminalMeansStop() {
  30        assertThat(ErrorCode.NOT_ENTITLED.terminal()).isTrue();
  31        assertThat(ErrorCode.PRECONDITION_FAILED.terminal()).isTrue();
  32        assertThat(ErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT.terminal()).isFalse();
  33        assertThat(ErrorCode.RATE_LIMITED.terminal()).isFalse();

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract;
   2
   3import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
   4import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
   5
   6import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
   7
   8/**
   9 * The profile is a whitelist, and these tests exist to stop it quietly becoming a blacklist.
  10 *
  11 * <p>The failure mode they guard against is specific: somebody needs {@code oneOf} for one tool,
  12 * adds it to {@code PERMITTED} because the linter was in the way, and six months later a quarter
  13 * of the catalog uses alternation that two of the four runtimes silently drop.
  14 */
  15class SchemaProfileTest {
  16
  17    @Test
  18    @DisplayName("alternation and conditionals are prohibited, with a reason the author can act on")
  19    void prohibitionsCarryReasons() {
  20        for (String keyword : new String[] {"oneOf", "anyOf", "allOf", "not", "if", "then", "else"}) {
  21            SchemaProfile.Prohibition prohibition = SchemaProfile.prohibitionFor(keyword);
  22            assertThat(prohibition).as("%s must be prohibited", keyword).isNotNull();
  23            assertThat(prohibition.why())
  24                    .as("%s must say what to do instead, not just that it is banned", keyword)
  25                    .isNotBlank()
  26                    .hasSizeGreaterThan(40);
  27        }
  28    }
  29
  30    @Test
  31    @DisplayName("nothing is both permitted and prohibited")
  32    void theTwoListsDoNotOverlap() {
  33        for (SchemaProfile.Prohibition prohibition : SchemaProfile.PROHIBITED) {
  34            assertThat(SchemaProfile.PERMITTED).doesNotContain(prohibition.keyword());
  35        }
  36    }
  37
  38    @Test
  39    @DisplayName("identity and override parameter names are reserved")
  40    void identityCannotBeAnArgument() {
  41        assertThat(SchemaProfile.RESERVED_PARAMETERS)
  42                .contains("customerId", "userId", "onBehalfOf", "impersonate")
  43                .as("a model must never be able to set its own identity")
  44                .contains("principal", "token", "scopes")
  45                .as("nor talk its way past a check")
  46                .contains("dryRun", "force", "skipValidation", "override", "sudo");
  47    }
  48
  49    @Test
  50    @DisplayName("accountId is not reserved, because choosing between a customer's own accounts "
  51            + "is exactly what the model is for")
  52    void theLineIsDrawnAtIdentityNotAtScope() {
  53        assertThat(SchemaProfile.RESERVED_PARAMETERS)
  54                .doesNotContain("accountId", "orderId", "symbol");
  55    }
  56}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.time.Instant;
   4
   5import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
   6import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
   7import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
   8import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.CsvSource;
   9
  10import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
  11
  12/**
  13 * Sessions, because "the market is closed" is the single most common reason a correct-looking
  14 * order is refused, and getting the boundaries wrong is invisible until a customer trades at
  15 * 09:28.
  16 */
  17class MarketClockTest {
  18
  19    private static MarketClock at(String instant) {
  20        MarketClock clock = new MarketClock();
  21        clock.set(Instant.parse(instant));
  22        return clock;
  23    }
  24
  25    @ParameterizedTest(name = "{0} is {1}")
  26    @CsvSource({
  27            // Thursday 1 October 2026, in UTC. New York is on daylight time, so UTC minus four.
  28            "2026-10-01T07:59:00Z, CLOSED",          // 03:59 — before the pre-market opens
  29            "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z, PRE_MARKET",      // 04:00 — the pre-market opens
  30            "2026-10-01T13:29:00Z, PRE_MARKET",      // 09:29 — one minute before the bell
  31            "2026-10-01T13:30:00Z, REGULAR",         // 09:30 — the bell
  32            "2026-10-01T19:59:00Z, REGULAR",         // 15:59 — one minute before the close
  33            "2026-10-01T20:00:00Z, AFTER_HOURS",     // 16:00 — the close
  34            "2026-10-01T23:59:00Z, AFTER_HOURS",     // 19:59 — the last minute of the session
  35            "2026-10-02T00:00:00Z, CLOSED",          // 20:00 — after-hours ends
  36            "2026-10-03T17:00:00Z, CLOSED",          // Saturday
  37            "2026-10-04T17:00:00Z, CLOSED",          // Sunday
  38    })
  39    void sessionBoundaries(String instant, MarketClock.Session expected) {
  40        assertThat(at(instant).session()).isEqualTo(expected);
  41    }
  42
  43    @Test
  44    @DisplayName("only the regular session is tradeable without a limit order")
  45    void tradeability() {
  46        assertThat(MarketClock.Session.REGULAR.tradeable()).isTrue();
  47        assertThat(MarketClock.Session.PRE_MARKET.tradeable()).isTrue();
  48        assertThat(MarketClock.Session.AFTER_HOURS.tradeable()).isTrue();
  49        assertThat(MarketClock.Session.CLOSED.tradeable()).isFalse();
  50    }
  51
  52    @Test
  53    @DisplayName("the next open skips the weekend, because a customer wants to know how long")
  54    void theNextOpenIsUseful() {
  55        // Friday evening: the next regular session is Monday morning.
  56        assertThat(at("2026-10-02T23:00:00Z").nextRegularOpen())
  57                .isEqualTo(Instant.parse("2026-10-05T13:30:00Z"));
  58        // Thursday before the bell: later the same morning.
  59        assertThat(at("2026-10-01T10:00:00Z").nextRegularOpen())
  60                .isEqualTo(Instant.parse("2026-10-01T13:30:00Z"));
  61        // Thursday after the close: tomorrow morning.
  62        assertThat(at("2026-10-01T21:00:00Z").nextRegularOpen())
  63                .isEqualTo(Instant.parse("2026-10-02T13:30:00Z"));
  64    }
  65
  66    @Test
  67    @DisplayName("the clock can be moved, which is the only reason it is a component")
  68    void theClockMoves() {
  69        MarketClock clock = at("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z");
  70        clock.advance(java.time.Duration.ofHours(8));
  71        assertThat(clock.now()).isEqualTo(Instant.parse("2026-10-01T22:30:00Z"));
  72        assertThat(clock.session()).isEqualTo(MarketClock.Session.AFTER_HOURS);
  73    }
  74}

   1package com.example.brokerage.domain;
   2
   3import java.math.BigDecimal;
   4import java.time.Instant;
   5import java.util.List;
   6
   7import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
   8import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
   9
  10import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
  11
  12/**
  13 * The simulated market has to be boring in two specific ways, and neither is guaranteed by
  14 * anything except these tests.
  15 *
  16 * <p>It has to be <b>repeatable</b>, because the book prints these numbers, the evaluation
  17 * cassettes were recorded against them and the contract tests assert on them. A price that moved
  18 * because a random number generator felt like it would make all three unreadable.
  19 *
  20 * <p>And consecutive days have to be <b>close together</b>, because the day-over-day change is
  21 * published in every quote. The first version of this generator drew each day independently from a
  22 * wide band and produced a blue chip down sixteen percent, which made every figure in the book look
  23 * like a bug. {@link #theDayOverDayMoveIsBelievable()} is what stops that coming back.
  24 */
  25class MarketDataTest {
  26
  27    private static final List<String> SYMBOLS =
  28            List.of("AAPL", "MSFT", "NVDA", "BRK.B", "VOO", "KO", "GME", "TSM");
  29
  30    private MarketData at(String instant) {
  31        MarketClock clock = new MarketClock();
  32        clock.set(Instant.parse(instant));
  33        return new MarketData(new Instruments(), clock);
  34    }
  35
  36    @Test
  37    @DisplayName("the same symbol on the same day is the same price on every run")
  38    void pricesAreRepeatable() {
  39        for (String symbol : SYMBOLS) {
  40            BigDecimal first = at("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z").quote(symbol).last();
  41            BigDecimal again = at("2026-10-01T18:00:00Z").quote(symbol).last();
  42            assertThat(again).as("%s within the same trading day", symbol).isEqualByComparingTo(first);
  43        }
  44    }
  45
  46    @Test
  47    @DisplayName("no day-over-day move exceeds two percent")
  48    void theDayOverDayMoveIsBelievable() {
  49        for (String symbol : SYMBOLS) {
  50            for (int day = 1; day <= 60; day++) {
  51                MarketData market = at("2026-%02d-%02dT14:30:00Z"
  52                        .formatted(8 + day / 31, 1 + day % 28));
  53                MarketData.Quote quote = market.quote(symbol);
  54                assertThat(quote.changePercent().abs())
  55                        .as("%s on day %d moved %s percent", symbol, day, quote.changePercent())
  56                        .isLessThan(BigDecimal.valueOf(2));
  57            }
  58        }
  59    }
  60
  61    @Test
  62    @DisplayName("prices stay inside a believable band around the instrument's base")
  63    void pricesAreBounded() {
  64        Instruments instruments = new Instruments();
  65        for (String symbol : SYMBOLS) {
  66            BigDecimal base = instruments.require(symbol).basePrice();
  67            for (int month = 1; month <= 12; month++) {
  68                BigDecimal last = at("2026-%02d-15T14:30:00Z".formatted(month)).quote(symbol).last();
  69                assertThat(last).as("%s in month %d", symbol, month)
  70                        .isGreaterThan(base.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(0.8)))
  71                        .isLessThan(base.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(1.2)));
  72            }
  73        }
  74    }
  75
  76    @Test
  77    @DisplayName("the bid is below the ask, and the spread widens outside the regular session")
  78    void theSpreadReflectsTheSession() {
  79        MarketData.Quote regular = at("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z").quote("AAPL");
  80        MarketData.Quote afterHours = at("2026-10-01T21:00:00Z").quote("AAPL");
  81
  82        assertThat(regular.bid()).isLessThan(regular.ask());
  83        assertThat(regular.session()).isEqualTo(MarketClock.Session.REGULAR);
  84        assertThat(afterHours.session()).isEqualTo(MarketClock.Session.AFTER_HOURS);
  85        assertThat(afterHours.spreadBasisPoints())
  86                .as("a thin session is a wider market, and the agent is told so")
  87                .isGreaterThan(regular.spreadBasisPoints());
  88    }
  89
  90    @Test
  91    @DisplayName("the last bar's close agrees with the quote, so one turn cannot contradict itself")
  92    void theSeriesAndTheQuoteAgree() {
  93        MarketData market = at("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z");
  94        List<MarketData.Bar> bars = market.history("NVDA", 30);
  95        assertThat(bars.getLast().close()).isEqualByComparingTo(market.quote("NVDA").last());
  96        assertThat(bars.getLast().date()).isEqualTo(java.time.LocalDate.of(2026, 10, 1));
  97    }
  98
  99    @Test
 100    @DisplayName("history covers trading days only, and every bar is internally consistent")
 101    void barsAreWellFormed() {
 102        for (MarketData.Bar bar : at("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z").history("MSFT", 30)) {
 103            assertThat(bar.date().getDayOfWeek().getValue())
 104                    .as("%s is a weekend", bar.date()).isLessThanOrEqualTo(5);
 105            assertThat(bar.high()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(bar.open().max(bar.close()));
 106            assertThat(bar.low()).isLessThanOrEqualTo(bar.open().min(bar.close()));
 107            assertThat(bar.low()).isGreaterThan(BigDecimal.ZERO);
 108            assertThat(bar.volume()).isPositive();
 109        }
 110    }
 111}

   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.DescriptorCodec;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ErrorCode;

  14import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolFailure;
  15import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolHandler;
  16
  17/**
  18 * A two-tool catalog, built in this file, for testing the pipeline in isolation.
  19 *
  20 * <p>The brokerage catalog is a fine thing to test the pipeline <em>through</em> and a poor thing
  21 * to test it <em>with</em>: when a pipeline test fails against fourteen real tools, the first
  22 * question is whether the pipeline broke or a handler did. Two tools defined here — one read, one
  23 * that needs approval — answer that question before it is asked.
  24 */
  25final class Fixture {
  26
  27    static final String READ = "fixture_thing_get";
  28    static final String WRITE = "fixture_thing_place";
  29    static final String READ_SCOPE = "fixture:thing:read";
  30    static final String WRITE_SCOPE = "fixture:thing:write";
  31
  32    private static final String DESCRIPTION_READ =
  33            "Echoes its arguments back, so that a test of the pipeline has something to assert "
  34            + "on without a domain behind it. Use when a test needs a conformant descriptor that "
  35            + "changes nothing. Do not use for anything real; it is a fixture. Read the label and "
  36            + "count fields in the result, which are the ones that were sent. This changes "
  37            + "nothing and may be called freely.";
  38
  39    private static final String DESCRIPTION_WRITE =
  40            "Pretends to commit something, and echoes the arguments back as the record of what it "
  41            + "did. Use when a test needs a tool that requires the customer's approval before it "
  42            + "runs. Do not use for anything real; it is a fixture. Read the label and count in "
  43            + "the result to confirm what was committed. The effect cannot be undone, so it "
  44            + "requires an approval the runtime enforces.";
  45
  46    private Fixture() {
  47    }
  48
  49    static ToolDescriptor read() {
  50        return descriptor(READ, "Read a fixture thing", DESCRIPTION_READ, true, 0, 60);
  51    }
  52
  53    static ToolDescriptor write() {
  54        return descriptor(WRITE, "Commit a fixture thing", DESCRIPTION_WRITE, false, 3, 5);
  55    }
  56
  57    /**
  58     * Titles are distinct per fixture, because the linter requires it — a human approving one of
  59     * two tools called "a fixture tool" cannot tell which. The first thing this fixture caught was
  60     * itself.
  61     */
  62    static ToolDescriptor descriptor(String name, String title, String description,
  63                                     boolean readOnly, int riskTier, int perMinute) {
  64        String approval = riskTier >= 2
  65                ? """
  66                  {
  67                    "mode": "confirm",
  68                    "confirmationTemplate": "Do {{label}}, {{count}} times? This cannot be undone.",
  69                    "expiresInSeconds": 60
  70                  }"""
  71                : "{ \"mode\": \"none\" }";
  72        String json = """
  73                {
  74                  "name": "%s",
  75                  "title": "%s",
  76                  "description": "%s",
  77                  "inputSchema": {
  78                    "type": "object",
  79                    "properties": {
  80                      "label": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z]{1,16}$",
  81                                 "description": "A lowercase label, at most sixteen letters." },
  82                      "count": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 10,
  83                                 "description": "How many, between one and ten." }
  84                    },
  85                    "required": ["label"],
  86                    "additionalProperties": false
  87                  },
  88                  "outputSchema": {
  89                    "type": "object",
  90                    "properties": {
  91                      "label": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 16, "description": "The label." },
  92                      "count": { "type": "integer", "description": "The count that was used." }
  93                    },
  94                    "required": ["label", "count"],
  95                    "additionalProperties": false
  96                  },
  97                  "annotations": {
  98                    "readOnlyHint": %b,
  99                    "destructiveHint": %b,
 100                    "idempotentHint": true,
 101                    "openWorldHint": false
 102                  },
 103                  "_meta": {
 104                    "com.example.tooling/governance": {
 105                      "version": "1.0.0",
 106                      "lifecycle": "active",
 107                      "conformanceLevel": "L2",
 108                      "riskTier": %d,
 109                      "owner": { "team": "t", "contact": "t@example.com", "escalation": "page://t" },
 110                      "dataClassification": "internal",
 111                      "containsPii": false,
 112                      "piiFields": [],
 113                      "entitlements": ["%s"],
 114                      "approval": %s,
 115                      "recordKeeping": { "auditEvent": "tool.fixture", "retention": "P1Y" },
 116                      "rateLimit": { "perPrincipalPerMinute": %d },
 117                      "availability": { "slo": "99.9", "killSwitch": "tools.fixture.%s" },
 118                      "evaluation": { "suite": "evals/fixture", "lastRunAt": "2026-09-28T07:00:00Z",
 119                                      "selectionAccuracy": 1.0, "refusalAccuracy": 1.0 }
 120                    }
 121                  }
 122                }
 123                """.formatted(name, title, description, readOnly, !readOnly, riskTier,
 124                readOnly ? READ_SCOPE : WRITE_SCOPE, approval, perMinute,
 125                readOnly ? "read" : "write");
 126        return DescriptorCodec.read(json);
 127    }
 128
 129    /** A handler that echoes, counts its calls, and can be told to misbehave. */
 130    static final class Echo implements ToolHandler {
 131
 132        enum Behavior { NORMAL, REFUSE, THROW, BAD_PAYLOAD }
 133
 134        record Payload(String label, int count) {
 135        }
 136
 137        final AtomicInteger calls = new AtomicInteger();
 138        private final String name;
 139        private final Behavior behavior;
 140
 141        Echo(String name, Behavior behavior) {
 142            this.name = name;
 143            this.behavior = behavior;
 144        }
 145
 146        static Echo of(String name) {
 147            return new Echo(name, Behavior.NORMAL);
 148        }
 149
 150        @Override
 151        public String name() {
 152            return name;
 153        }
 154
 155        @Override
 156        public Object handle(Invocation invocation) {
 157            calls.incrementAndGet();
 158            return switch (behavior) {
 159                case REFUSE -> throw ToolFailure.of(ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
 160                        "Nothing by that label.", "Ask the customer for a different label.");
 161                case THROW -> throw new IllegalStateException(
 162                        "a leaked constraint name the model must never see");
 163                case BAD_PAYLOAD -> Map.of("label", invocation.string("label"));
 164                case NORMAL -> new Payload(invocation.string("label"),
 165                        invocation.integer("count", 1));
 166            };
 167        }
 168    }
 169
 170    static Principal principal(String... entitlements) {
 171        return new Principal("test:subject", "cust_test", Set.of(entitlements), "session-1");
 172    }
 173
 174    static InvocationPipeline pipeline(ToolRegistry registry, ApprovalGate approvals,
 175                                       KillSwitches switches, AuditLog audit) {
 176        return new InvocationPipeline(registry, approvals, new RateLimiter(), switches, audit,
 177                null, () -> Instant.parse("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z"));
 178    }
 179
 180    static ToolRegistry registry(List<ToolDescriptor> descriptors, List<ToolHandler> handlers) {
 181        return new ToolRegistry(null, descriptors, handlers);
 182    }
 183}

   1package com.example.brokerage.tooling.runtime;

   3import java.time.Instant;

   6import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ErrorCode;

   9import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
  10import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
  11import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
  12
  13import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
  14
  15/**
  16 * The ten steps, one at a time.
  17 *
  18 * <p>Each test here corresponds to a line in the pipeline's documented order of operations, and
  19 * together they are the argument that the order is deliberate. The two that are easiest to get
  20 * wrong, and the two most worth reading, are
  21 * {@link #schemaViolationsAreExplainedBeforeEntitlementsAreChecked()} and
  22 * {@link #aHandlerThatDriftsFromItsOwnOutputSchemaFailsClosed()}.
  23 */
  24class InvocationPipelineTest {
  25
  26    private static final Instant NOW = Instant.parse("2026-10-01T14:30:00Z");
  27
  28    private Fixture.Echo readHandler;
  29    private Fixture.Echo writeHandler;
  30    private ToolRegistry registry;
  31    private ApprovalGate approvals;
  32    private KillSwitches switches;
  33    private AuditLog audit;
  34    private InvocationPipeline pipeline;
  35    private Principal reader;
  36    private Principal trader;
  37
  38    @BeforeEach
  39    void setUp() {
  40        readHandler = Fixture.Echo.of(Fixture.READ);
  41        writeHandler = Fixture.Echo.of(Fixture.WRITE);
  42        registry = Fixture.registry(List.of(Fixture.read(), Fixture.write()),
  43                List.of(readHandler, writeHandler));
  44        approvals = new ApprovalGate();
  45        switches = new KillSwitches();
  46        audit = new AuditLog();
  47        pipeline = Fixture.pipeline(registry, approvals, switches, audit);
  48        reader = Fixture.principal(Fixture.READ_SCOPE);
  49        trader = Fixture.principal(Fixture.READ_SCOPE, Fixture.WRITE_SCOPE);
  50    }
  51
  52    @Test
  53    @DisplayName("a valid call runs the handler and comes back in an envelope with provenance")
  54    void aValidCallSucceeds() {
  55        var outcome = pipeline.invoke(Fixture.READ, "{\"label\":\"hello\",\"count\":3}", reader);
  56        assertThat(outcome.ok()).isTrue();

   1package com.example.brokerage.catalog;
   2
   3import java.util.List;
   4import java.util.Set;
   5import java.util.TreeSet;
   6
   7import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ConformanceLinter;
   8import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Finding;
   9import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Governance;
  10import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.Ontology;
  11import com.example.brokerage.tooling.contract.ToolDescriptor;
  12
  13import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
  14import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
  15
  16import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
  17
  18/**
  19 * The conformance gate. This is the test that makes the specification a specification rather than
  20 * a document, and it is the reason the other tests in this project can be about behavior instead
  21 * of about style.
  22 *
  23 * <p>It runs with no model, no network and no application context, in a few milliseconds, on every
  24 * commit. That is the whole argument for writing descriptors as data and rules as code.
  25 */
  26class CatalogConformanceTest {
  27
  28    private final BrokerageCatalog catalog = new BrokerageCatalog();
  29
  30    @Test
  31    @DisplayName("every descriptor conforms, with no warnings either")
  32    void theCatalogConforms() {
  33        List<Finding> findings = new ConformanceLinter(catalog.ontology())
  34                .lint(catalog.descriptors());
  35        assertThat(findings)
  36                .as("conformance findings:%n  %s",
  37                        String.join("\n  ", findings.stream().map(Finding::toString).toList()))
  38                .isEmpty();
  39    }
  40
  41    @Test
  42    @DisplayName("the catalog and the ontology describe the same fourteen capabilities")
  43    void theOntologyAndTheCatalogAgree() {
  44        Set<String> descriptors = new TreeSet<>(
  45                catalog.descriptors().stream().map(ToolDescriptor::name).toList());
  46        Set<String> capabilities = new TreeSet<>(
  47                catalog.ontology().capabilities().stream().map(Ontology.Capability::tool).toList());
  48        assertThat(descriptors).isEqualTo(capabilities).hasSize(14);
  49    }
  50
  51    @Test
  52    @DisplayName("every identifier a tool consumes is produced by some other tool")
  53    void nothingIsADeadEnd() {
  54        assertThat(catalog.ontology().unreachableIdentifiers())
  55                .as("an identifier nothing produces is an argument the agent can only guess at")
  56                .isEmpty();
  57    }
  58
  59    @Test
  60    @DisplayName("only the preview tool can mint a confirmation token")
  61    void previewIsTheOnlyWayToTrade() {
  62        assertThat(catalog.ontology().producers().get("ConfirmationToken"))
  63                .containsExactly("brokerage_order_preview");
  64        for (String tool : List.of("brokerage_order_place", "brokerage_order_replace")) {
  65            assertThat(catalog.ontology().capabilityOf(tool).consumes())
  66                    .as("%s must require a token", tool)
  67                    .contains("ConfirmationToken");
  68            assertThat(catalog.ontology().prerequisitesOf(tool))
  69                    .contains("brokerage_order_preview");
  70        }
  71    }
  72
  73    @Test
  74    @DisplayName("every tool that changes state is tier 2 or 3 and needs a human")
  75    void writingNeedsApproval() {
  76        for (ToolDescriptor descriptor : catalog.descriptors()) {
  77            if (descriptor.annotations().readOnlyHint()) {
  78                continue;
  79            }
  80            Governance governance = descriptor.governance();
  81            assertThat(governance.riskTier()).as("%s tier", descriptor.name())
  82                    .isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(2);
  83            assertThat(governance.requiresApproval()).as("%s approval", descriptor.name()).isTrue();
  84            assertThat(governance.approval().confirmationTemplate())
  85                    .as("%s must show the human what they are agreeing to", descriptor.name())
  86                    .isNotBlank();
  87            assertThat(governance.availability().killSwitch())
  88                    .as("%s must be switchable off", descriptor.name()).isNotBlank();
  89        }
  90    }
  91
  92    @Test
  93    @DisplayName("ten of the fourteen tools are read-only, so an agent can orient itself safely")
  94    void theCatalogIsMostlyReads() {
  95        long readOnly = catalog.descriptors().stream()
  96                .filter(descriptor -> descriptor.annotations().readOnlyHint()).count();
  97        assertThat(readOnly).isEqualTo(11);
  98    }
  99
 100    @Test
 101    @DisplayName("no description points the model at a tool that does not exist")
 102    void crossReferencesResolve() {
 103        Set<String> names = new TreeSet<>(
 104                catalog.descriptors().stream().map(ToolDescriptor::name).toList());
 105        for (ToolDescriptor descriptor : catalog.descriptors()) {
 106            for (String referenced : ConformanceLinter.referencedTools(descriptor.description())) {
 107                assertThat(names).as("%s points at %s", descriptor.name(), referenced)
 108                        .contains(referenced);
 109            }
 110        }
 111    }
 112
 113    @Test
 114    @DisplayName("the conduct prompt is present and says nothing about individual tools")
 115    void conductIsPolicyNotDocumentation() {
 116        String conduct = catalog.conduct();
 117        assertThat(conduct).hasSizeGreaterThan(500);
 118        for (ToolDescriptor descriptor : catalog.descriptors()) {
 119            assertThat(conduct)
 120                    .as("conduct must not name %s; per-tool advice belongs in the descriptor",
 121                            descriptor.name())
 122                    .doesNotContain(descriptor.name());
 123        }
 124    }
 125}
